listed={f['path'] for f in m['files']}

for root,d,fs in os.walk('.'):

        rp=os.path.relpath(os.path.join(root,x),'.')
        actual.add(rp)
print('unlisted:',sorted(actual-listed-{'consumer-input-manifest.json'}))
EOF

1	# OpenSIP product contracts
2	
3	This consolidated contract set describes the complete intended product selected
4	by D-371. Its current review and application standing is recorded in the
5	[correction record](../../../coop/design-corrections/README.md) and the
6	[central readiness register](../../architecture/08-decision-and-readiness-register.md#unified-product-design-readiness).
7	These contract bytes alone grant no readiness grade or implementation authority.
8	
9	The product has one host for discovery, input admission, authority, orchestration,
10	evaluation, evidence storage and output. Language-specific analyzers contribute
11	facts and Coverage through versioned protocols. The evaluator is pure. An
12	invocation can compose analysis, queries, imports, policy changes, repair and
13	verification; only an authoritative analysis seals a source-bound Run.
14	
15	```mermaid
16	flowchart LR
17	  R[Repository and explicit inputs] --> H[Host discovery and admission]
18	  H --> I[Invocation and ordered steps]
19	  I --> N[Native analyzers]
20	  N --> F[Admitted facts and Coverage]
21	  F --> E[Pure policy evaluation]
22	  E --> V[Proof verification and immutable Run]
23	  V --> S[Evidence store and portable baseline]
24	  S --> O[CLI JSON SARIF HTML agent views]
25	  S --> P[Authorized repair preview and apply]
26	  P --> H
27	```
28	
29	Read the five contracts together:
30	
31	1. [Identity and evidence](identity-and-evidence.md): exact semantic identities,
32	   independent replay, durable defaults, retention, purge and recovery.
33	2. [Security and lifecycle](security-and-lifecycle.md): repository boundaries,
34	   time/trust recovery, revocation, supported platform profiles, migration and
35	   concurrent operations.
36	3. [Native evidence](native-evidence.md): TS/JS/Rust capability cells, sealed
37	   dependency/prepared inputs, resolution completeness and clone candidates.
38	4. [Workflows and surfaces](workflows-and-surfaces.md): invocations, baseline and
39	   changed-code audit, typed imports/comparison, policy/review/repair and output.
40	5. [Admission and qualification](admission-and-qualification.md): exact numeric
41	   parsing, independent report oracles and release measurement requirements.
42	
43	The Fallow-inspired behavior belongs in these contracts now, even where its
44	implementation is scheduled later. Zero-config discovery, stable output,
45	composed invocations, retained evidence, changed-code gating and advisory
46	boundaries apply across languages. Native syntax/resolution, clone normalization
47	and runtime-format adapters are deliberately language-specific.
48	
49	Historical contracts and preview reviews remain immutable evidence. They do
50	not provide an alternative current command grammar or a competing preview
51	product. The normative retained/superseded selector tables in these five
52	contracts determine the applicable design recipes; a current explicit successor
53	wins over the named inherited selector only within its declared scope. Any
54	unresolved overlap is a design defect, never reviewer discretion. The correction
55	crosswalk records the corresponding review/application evidence, and the central
56	readiness register remains the sole completion checklist. Those two governance
57	records grant standing; they are not additional semantic recipes and are omitted
58	from blind reconstruction inputs to avoid disclosing prior verdicts. Passing design reference checks is not product qualification.

1	# Identity, authoritative evidence, and retention
2	
3	Standing: product successor authored by Codex, with review and application
4	standing governed by the [correction record](../../../coop/design-corrections/README.md)
5	and central readiness register. This is the Phase-1A packet for the intended
6	product, not a repair of the historical preview's acceptance record. The
7	machine-readable descriptors and reference semantics are in
8	[foundation](../../../coop/design-corrections/foundation/). Every `schemaVersion`
9	in the new semantic identity graph is 2. Old identifiers remain old identifiers.
10	
11	## 1. Authority and applicability
12	
13	The host admits inputs, mints identities, evaluates policy through the pure
14	evaluator, verifies its result, and commits evidence. Native providers, imported
15	observations, model suggestions and stored caller-supplied identifiers do not
16	have evaluation or custody authority. Signed software provenance does not prove
17	that an algorithm is correct; the selected, authenticated first-party host and
18	pure evaluator remain in the TCB. No Python introspection guard or caller's
19	`verified=true` is an authority mechanism.
20	
21	This contract prospectively replaces the Run/evidence/Plan/source/view/finding/
22	proof/cache/regeneration recipes and their parks in freeze §7.1,
23	`evidence-identity-recipes.v5.json`, `evaluation-proof.v8.json`'s claim-shape
24	lineage and `evaluation-proof.v13.json`'s provenance lineage. Neither evaluation
25	candidate becomes retrospectively applied. It replaces the Phase-1A and
26	retention-result join missing from `evidence.v15.json`, and consumes the
27	CD-RT-5 posture implemented by `retention-tiers.v28.json`. It supplies the
28	identity-dependent parts of R-1, trusted-request context and OPERABILITY G19.
29	Precise residual dispositions and source pins are in the integration record.
30	
31	Unchanged inherited constraints: no ambient provider reads; sealed snapshot;
32	complete protocol transaction plus successful process exit and EOF before facts
33	are admitted; pure deterministic evaluation; one host writer; deny-by-absence
34	permissions; lifetime-neutral semantics. Existing relation payload schemas can
35	be referenced by exact digest. Their historical FactRecord1 wrapper cannot bind
36	a snapshot2 identifier; product FactRecord2 is an explicit successor.
37	
38	## 2. Tenant and operational identity
39	
40	ProjectId retains PROJECT-ID-V1: `prj1-` followed by 64 lower-case hex digits,
41	32 host-CSPRNG bytes. The untracked `.opensip/project-id.v1` marker and the
42	private host registry must agree exactly. A private namespace UUID is an
43	operational storage locator, bound one-to-one to ProjectId; it does not enter
44	semantic identities. The host verifies marker, root identity, owner, no-follow
45	handles and registry binding before any project writer. Missing marker and
46	registry is first use; agreement is reuse; either unilateral or contradictory
47	presence is an admission refusal requiring explicit recovery/adoption. It never
48	silently chooses one identity. Discovery and admission use the security unit's
49	root boundary.
50	
51	An ordinary fresh clone gets a fresh ProjectId. Explicit adoption from an
52	admitted portable project bundle preserves a ProjectId after showing its source
53	and target; it never imports another machine's local authorization, credentials,
54	leases or execution receipts. A fork gets a new ProjectId and explicit origin
55	metadata. A root move preserves ProjectId only through an authenticated registry
56	move with no live writer; duplicate simultaneous roots for one local namespace
57	refuse. Read-only comparison of two tenants does not merge their stores.
58	
59	Invocation identity is RequestId (`req1_` plus 32 lower-case hex digits), minted
60	before admission and retained for refusal as well as success. Each admitted
61	attempt receives a fresh ExecutionId (`exec1_` plus 32 lowercase hex digits).
62	`c2-plan-stage-schema.v4.json` `planIntent.wireTypes.executionId` is the C-2
63	owner selector for EXECUTION-ID-V1 **provenance** — where the identifier and its
64	uniqueness discipline come from — and it is not byte-equivalent to the product
65	successor grammar. Its pattern ends in a bare `$`, so it admits
66	`exec1_<32 hex>\n`, which `admission-and-qualification` §1 declares malformed and
67	which `common.schema.json#/$defs/ExecutionId` refuses. The **product successor
68	grammar is end-anchored**: `^exec1_[0-9a-f]{32}(?![\s\S])`, exactly as
69	`identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/commit-receipt/properties/executionId` and the
70	workflow `ExecutionId` spell it, and a trailing newline, carriage return or space
71	is refused rather than trimmed. RequestId is `^req1_[0-9a-f]{32}(?![\s\S])` on the
72	same rule. This is the same deliberate non-equivalence security §S9.1 states for
73	`RootV1`: the retained selector remains the immutable provenance record, the
74	successor is what admits.
75	Both RequestId and ExecutionId use independent 16-byte host-CSPRNG draws, reserved
76	with uniqueness checked in the corresponding operational ledger before use.
77	Caller-supplied IDs and reuse are refused; neither is derived from a content hash.
78	This prospectively settles RES-C2V4-01 ownership in the shared identity contract.
79	StepId is the zero-based integer position in the invocation's ordered DAG.
80	Retry always receives a new ExecutionId. These identities, wall clocks, PIDs,
81	credentials, authorization nonces, receipts and output destinations are
82	operational and excluded from Run identity. Identical semantic inputs can
83	produce the same Run on two attempts; attempts remain separately auditable.
84	
85	## 3. Exact canonical encoding and identity preimages
86	
87	The authoritative schema is `foundation/identity-schemas.v2.json` (closed
88	Draft 2020-12 records); semantic joins below are equally mandatory. JSON Schema
89	alone does not establish exact numeric admission. Before deserialization loses
90	lexical information, reject duplicate keys, floating/exponent tokens, `-0`,
91	nonfinite tokens, malformed UTF-8 and non-scalar Unicode. Integer range is
92	[-2^63, 2^64-1], booleans are distinct, and every field has its narrower schema
93	bound. Maximum descriptor is 4 MiB and nesting depth 32: the root container
94	counts as 1; scalar leaves and object keys add no container depth. Byte inventories may
95	name larger independently bounded blobs. A descriptor exceeding a bound is
96	rejected; it is never truncated into a different identity.
97	
98	Canonical JSON has UTF-8 byte-ordered keys, no whitespace or trailing newline,
99	no Unicode normalization, shortest ordinary decimal integers, and unescaped
100	Unicode scalar characters. Escape quote and backslash, use `\b\t\n\f\r`, and
101	lowercase `\u00xx` for other U+0000–001F controls; do not escape slash. Arrays are encoded **in their admitted order**: C never sorts, deduplicates or
102	infers semantics from a field name or `uniqueItems`. The closing default for
103	any array in a registered payload is an **ordered sequence**, including nested
104	arrays and raw token arrays. A schema/owning contract may prescribe a stricter
105	order; its producer constructs that order and admission refuses deviations
106	before hashing. This separation applies to every auxiliary digest as well as H.
107	
108	`x-opensip-order` is the machine-readable schema annotation for these orders, and
109	the closed vocabulary is exactly the one the `x-opensip-order` validator keyword in
110	`foundation/canonical.py` implements: `sequence` (default); `canonical-set` (strict
111	ascending canonical item bytes); `canonical-order` (nondecreasing canonical item
112	bytes, repeats allowed); `utf8` (strict ascending UTF-8 bytes of a scalar string
113	item); `path` (strict ascending UTF-8 `path`); `numeric` (strict ascending
114	integers); `ordinal` (contiguous zero-based `ordinal`); `predicate` (strict
115	ascending UTF-8 `ruleId,subjectId,predicateId` tuple); `ruleId` and `waiverId`
116	(strict ascending UTF-8 value of that key); and the generic object form
117	`{"by": [key, ...]}` (strict ascending UTF-8 tuple of those item keys, in the
118	listed order). All except `sequence` and `canonical-order` also require unique sort
119	keys; `uniqueItems` alone neither selects nor overrides an order. An annotation
120	outside this vocabulary refuses rather than passing silently. Explicit owning
121	schema/contract order takes precedence over the sequence default and must agree
122	with any annotation. No caller may elect a different order for one schema.
123	
124	Every array in identity-schemas.v2 carries this annotation: semantic collections
125	use `canonical-set`, inventories use `path`, dependencies use `numeric`, stages
126	use `ordinal` and predicate proofs use `predicate`. Inventory paths must be
127	unique even when two rows have different byte digests or lengths; there is no
128	tie-break, and duplicate paths refuse before an identity is minted. Configuration
129	`allowedScopes` preserves declared priority; declaration-signature tokens
130	preserve grammar order, including repeated tokens. PolicyDocumentV1 and
131	RuleProgramV1 `rules` preserve their schema's `ruleId` order, never canonical
132	rule-object order; WaiverSetV1 uses `waiverId`. Other native/workflow arrays
133	preserve their admitted sequence subject to their explicitly declared ordering
134	rules. This settles all arrays without an implicit set heuristic.
135	
136	Text maxLength counts Unicode scalar values, while the descriptor byte cap
137	remains independent. U+007F and U+2028 remain unescaped. Logical
138	paths are relative slash-separated scalar strings, without empty, dot, dot-dot,
139	NUL or backslash segments. Source spans are half-open byte offsets, bounded by
140	the exact named source blob; they never split UTF-8 characters in text anchors.
141	Native language identifiers may have their own explicit normalization; that is
142	a payload property, never an implicit change to this canonical encoder.
143	
144	For domain D and descriptor X:
145	
146	`H(D,X) = SHA256(ASCII("opensip.product.v1") || 00 || ASCII(D) || 00 || uint64BE(length(C(X))) || C(X))`.
147	
148	The identifier is the prefix below, a colon, and lowercase H hex. A raw blob
149	reference uses SHA256 of its exact bytes and its byte length. A semantic
150	reference must name its domain, not just an untyped hash. No path, display
151	version or claimed digest substitutes for verified bytes.
152	
153	| Domain / prefix | Exact semantic content (schema contains field types) |
154	|---|---|
155	| snapshot / snapshot2 | ProjectId, sorted source inventory, resolved config, scope and VCS digests |
156	| closure / closure2 | role kind, signed manifest digest, exact executable/data tree, semantic version, protocol major and platform |
157	| import / import2 | typed payload/schema, source and build correspondence, producer/adapter closures, blobs, scope, observation and completeness |
158	| plan / plan2 | snapshot, capability manifest, semantic closures, analysis spec, resolved config, native contexts, imports, policy, waivers, scope, deterministic budget and semantic grant |
159	| subject-scope / scope2 | snapshot, relation/rung, source/target universes, enumerator closure and complete sorted subject inventory |
160	| fact / fact2 | snapshot, relation/rung, universes, producer closure, exact relation payload/schema, anchors and confidence millionths |
161	| coverage / coverage2 | scope, CoverageResultV3 payload and exact schema digest |
162	| view / view2 | Plan, scopes, facts, Coverage, producer and schema closure |
163	| execution-plan / exec-plan2 | Plan and ordered acyclic derivation stages, each with exact stage spec, dependencies and output domains |
164	| finding-fingerprint / finding-key2 | stable rule name, detector semantics major, logical subject key and related subject keys |
165	| finding / finding2 | fingerprint, exact rule closure, subject, message code/parameters, severity and evidence references |
166	| proof-bundle / proof2 | Plan, derivation plan, evaluator closure, rule program, admitted evaluation input references, predicate proofs, findings and verdict |
167	| semantic-evidence / evidence2 | Plan, views, Coverage, imports, findings and proof |
168	| evaluation-seal / seal2 | Plan, derivation plan, evidence, evaluator, policy, proof and verdict |
169	| run / run2 | ProjectId, snapshot, Plan, evidence, evaluation seal and capability manifest |
170	| cache-key / cache2; regeneration-key / regen2 | Plan, exact producer, stage spec, scopes, inputs and output schema |
171	| policy-derivation / policy-derivation2 | Plan, proof, policy, waivers and verdict |
172	| quality-difference (unprefixed operational digest) | G13 independently recomputed expected/actual observation difference; never Run authority |
173	
174	The graph is acyclic: proof does not include EvidenceId or RunId; evidence may
175	include proof; seal includes both; Run includes seal. A finding fingerprint
176	excludes line offsets, messages, timestamps and concrete evidence, but includes
177	a discriminator for otherwise indistinguishable logical subjects. The host
178	refuses an ambiguous key; it does not suffix it by encounter order. The native
179	subject adapter supplies declaration-signature tokens in grammar order, preserving
180	language/kind, qualified binding name, generic arity and parameter/type signature
181	syntax, excluding body and positions. `discriminator` is raw SHA256 of their
182	canonical JSON **ordered** string array (grammar order, repeated tokens retained). The selected detector closure defines the token
183	projection. Identical signatures within one logical-name collision class are
184	ambiguous and refuse correspondence; anonymous subjects without a unique enclosing
185	name/signature remain unmatched. A changed signature may change the key. This is
186	syntactic correspondence, never semantic equivalence. Renames
187	require explicit subject correspondence; a stable fingerprint is not proof of
188	unchanged detector semantics. Schema/domain changes require a new identifier
189	major and reviewed migration, not a permissive parser.
190	
191	Finding citations cannot introduce extra authoritative input roots. Fact and
192	Coverage citations must belong to an evaluated view; import citations must be
193	both selected by Plan and listed in evaluationInputRefs; predicate-witness
194	citations must name a witness of this proof; raw blob citations must be explicit
195	blob inputs to this evaluation. Every evaluated import must belong to Plan even
196	when no finding cites it. A well-formed, hash-valid object outside this closure
197	is refused, rather than admitted as hidden finding evidence.
198	
199	CapabilityManifestId uses the inherited applied producing recipe and exact
200	schema: it is 64 lowercase hex characters without a prefix. Its separate
201	CVE1 producing encoder is fully defined by
202	`docs/coop/artifacts/resolved-inputs.v2.json#planIdContract.canonicalValueEncoding`
203	(eight closed types and exact tags/lengths); that normative dependency must be
204	provided to a release-builder or blind consumer. CVE1's already-NFC string
205	admission applies to the capability manifest only and does not change C's
206	no-normalization product descriptor profile. Plan carries
207	`capabilityManifestBytesDigest` (raw SHA256) as well as capabilityManifestId.
208	The host validates the committed CVE1 artifact under the effective
209	`delivery.v4.json` schema and recomputes capabilityManifestId as
210	SHA256(UTF8("opensip.capability-manifest.v1") || 00 || committedBytes). `TypeScriptNativeContextV2.toolchain.typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` and
211	`NativeContextV2.toolchain.rustcDevLlvmDigest` (inside the Rust
212	`ToolchainIdentityV1`) are the 64-hex suffixes of
213	`closure2` identities for `kind=stdlib` and `kind=rust-dev-llvm`, respectively.
214	Both complete descriptors and trees are retained and joined to the selected
215	compiler/toolchain; these are explicit successor recipes despite the retained
216	field names, never reinterpretations of a historical Plan. They are never read
217	from an unverified worker claim. `closure.manifestDigest` is raw SHA256 of the
218	admitted component manifest body bytes encoded with the security metadata
219	profile, excluding the signature envelope; the signed envelope and verified
220	role/namespace join are retained as operational provenance. A manifest for a
221	different tree, platform or selected component is refused by delivery admission. They enter the native-context
222	payload, hence Plan. Closure tree hashing includes relative path, byte length
223	and digest for every selected file. A semantic version alone is not a closure.
224	
225	The native `subjectScopeCommitment` is `"sha256:"` plus the 64-hex suffix
226	of the exact admitted `scope2` identity, using H("subject-scope", descriptor).
227	It is another textual form of the **same** digest, not a separate hash of the
228	subjects or of the scope identifier string. Its retained descriptor includes
229	snapshot, relation/rung, source/target universes, enumerator closure and sorted
230	unique subjects. `subjectCount` is exactly that inventory's length. The native
231	Coverage admission boundary joins both key/entry commitments and count to this
232	host-owned scope descriptor and mints `coverage2.scopeId` from that same scope;
233	a mismatched provider claim mints neither Coverage nor Run (native §4).
234	
235	Native contexts have explicit H domains: `native.context.typescript.v2` over
236	TypeScriptNativeContextV2 and `native.context.rust.v2` over NativeContextV2.
237	Native records carry `sha256:<H hex>`; `plan.nativeContextDigests` carries the
238	sorted unique bare 64-hex suffixes for selected, admitted contexts. These are
239	**H digests**, not raw SHA256 of context JSON. Native universe identities follow
240	native §11's own H domain — `native.semantic-universe.typescript.v2` over
241	TypeScriptUniverseV2ResolvedInputs — and `fact` and `subject-scope`
242	`sourceUniverse`/`targetUniverse` carry its bare 64-hex suffix. A native
243	`sha256:` text form is never a foundation typed Ref domain.
244	When a field specifically names a raw payload digest, raw SHA256(C(payload))
245	is retained separately and cannot substitute for either H identity.
246	
247	Both of these are `h-identity` fields, so the object retained under each is the
248	exact H preimage frame, and Run closure admits it by parsing that frame rather
249	than by trusting a producer's claim or an ADMIT flag. **A frame proves retention,
250	never admission.** Frame parsing alone would let a claimant re-frame a context
251	the native boundary refuses and still mint a Run, so Run closure additionally
252	**re-runs the owning contract's own admission over the retained bytes**: the
253	native context admission of native §2.3/§2.4/§3/§14 (reference entry point
254	`admit_native_context`) against the Run's own retained `closure2` descriptors and
255	trees, and the universe binding of native §11 (reference entry point
256	`bind_typescript_universe`) against that admission and those exact context bytes.
257	Any refusal either returns is a Run admission refusal, reported with the native
258	contract's own typed refusal string. The registry rows in
259	`x-opensip-digest-domains.domainSets` name the language, the admission entry
260	point and the joins for each domain. Nothing is re-executed: no compiler, cargo,
261	provider, repository or filesystem operation runs at Run closure; the admission
262	is re-decided over retained descriptors alone.
263	
264	Beyond that, the closure re-derives the joins this contract names, from the
265	retained frame: `toolClosure.closureId` must be a retained `closure2` of kind
266	`toolchain`; `TypeScriptNativeContextV2.toolchain.typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` and
267	`NativeContextV2.toolchain.rustcDevLlvmDigest` must, prefixed with `closure2:`,
268	name retained closures of kind `stdlib` and `rust-dev-llvm` respectively, whose
269	recomputed identities equal them and whose complete trees are retained; the
270	recomputed context identity must equal the Plan's bare-hex member and the
271	recomputed universe identity must equal the field that named it; the set of
272	retained context frames must equal `plan.nativeContextDigests` exactly, so a
273	context reached by no Plan is refused and a Plan naming an unretained context
274	cannot close; and every retained universe frame's `nativeContextId` must be
275	`sha256:` plus a member of `plan.nativeContextDigests`, so a universe cannot bind
276	a context this Plan did not select.
277	
278	The native-context and native-universe source correspondence that this section
279	already requires to agree with the snapshot is discharged here rather than
280	assumed: every repository path a context or universe names must be an inventoried
281	snapshot path (`TypeScriptConfigProjectionV2.configGraphPaths`,
282	`CargoConfigProjectionV2.replacedSnapshotConfigs`,
283	`RustUniverseV2ResolvedInputs.crateRootPaths`), and a named lockfile
284	(`TypeScriptNativeContextV2.lockfileIdentity`,
285	`RustUniverseV2ResolvedInputs.lockfileIdentity`) must name an inventoried path
286	whose inventory digest equals its `contentSha256`. A context or universe
287	describing configuration, crate roots or a lockfile that is not in the analysed
288	snapshot cannot enter a Plan.
289	
290	Both universe domains native §11 registers are registered here:
291	`native.semantic-universe.typescript.v2` over TypeScriptUniverseV2ResolvedInputs
292	and `native.semantic-universe.rust.v2` over RustUniverseV2ResolvedInputs. A
293	universe must bind a context of **its own language** — the bound context's H
294	domain must be the one its registry row names, in either direction — and every
295	identifier the two records both carry must be equal; for Rust that is
296	`dependencySourceSetId`, `unifiedFeaturesId` and `preparedOutputSetId`. Each
297	domain names its owning binding — `bind_typescript_universe` (native §11) and
298	`bind_rust_universe` (native §2.1/§11) — and Run closure re-runs it over the
299	retained universe, the retained context bytes, the retained nested input records
300	and the snapshot inventory, exactly as it re-runs `admit_native_context`. Where
301	the owning contract registers a domain but supplies no binding for it, a universe
302	of that domain is **refused with a typed named cause**
303	(`NATIVE_UNIVERSE_BINDING_UNAVAILABLE`), never admitted unbound: an unfinished
304	owner obligation must not become a weaker admission.
305	
306	**Nested native semantic identities are records, not opaque strings.** A native
307	context or universe names further H identities, and each is admitted the same way:
308	retained as its own frame, parsed, validated under the record its domain
309	registers, and re-hashed. `native.dependency-source-set.v1`,
310	`native.unified-features.rust.v1`, `native.prepared-output-set.v3` and
311	`native.cargo-config-projection.v2` are registered here for that purpose, and the
312	chain continues to raw bytes: a dependency package's `fileManifestSha256` is a
313	`native.dependency-file-manifest.v1` identity whose every row's `contentSha256`
314	must be retained with exactly its declared `byteLength`, and every inert
315	prepared-output row's blob must be retained with exactly its declared length.
316	A semantically required dependency identity is never admitted merely because an
317	outer frame hashes.
318	
319	`CargoConfigProjectionV2` carries **two** digests that are not interchangeable:
320	its own `projectionSha256` is the raw SHA-256 of the projected `.cargo/config.toml`
321	file bytes, while `rust-v2.configProjectionSha256` is the 64-hex suffix of
322	`H("native.cargo-config-projection.v2", CargoConfigProjectionV2)` over the whole
323	record. Both are retained; neither substitutes for the other, and neither is the
324	raw SHA-256 of the canonical projection bytes.
325	
326	**Prepared products are inert data; execution authority stays operational.** A
327	universe's `preparedResolution` projects the grant operation the native contract
328	names — `host-prepared` requires `prepare-code` and `imported-inert` requires
329	`read-import` in the Plan's semantic grant — and a universe that consumed prepared
330	products without it refuses. Retained prepared bytes never imply an execution
331	grant, `executionCapableResolution` is a statement about what the resolution
332	consumed rather than a permission, and an unselected prepared set stays absent:
333	bytes in custody do not enter a resolution by being in custody.
334	
335	### The closing digest law
336	
337	Arrays have a closing default; so do digests. **Every 64-hex field in
338	identity-schemas.v2 has exactly one representation and one retention mode**,
339	declared field-by-field by the machine-readable `x-opensip-digest` schema
340	annotation. There is no residue: a 64-hex field carrying no annotation is

335	### The closing digest law
336	
337	Arrays have a closing default; so do digests. **Every 64-hex field in
338	identity-schemas.v2 has exactly one representation and one retention mode**,
339	declared field-by-field by the machine-readable `x-opensip-digest` schema
340	annotation. There is no residue: a 64-hex field carrying no annotation is
341	inadmissible, and a producer may not choose a representation for it. Nothing in
342	this graph infers a digest's meaning from a **field name**: a `Digest` spelling,
343	a `sha256` key or a bare hex string carries no meaning by itself, and two fields
344	with the same name have the same recipe only because the annotation says so.
345	The array law closes by naming a default; this law closes by admitting **no**
346	default, which is stronger: a new 64-hex field added without an annotation
347	refuses at admission instead of silently inheriting a plausible rule, so the
348	omission that produced this paragraph cannot recur unnoticed.
349	
350	The four representations are closed:
351	
352	| Representation | Meaning |
353	|---|---|
354	| `raw-artifact` | raw SHA256 of the **exact retained artifact bytes** — a source or closure-tree file, a committed capability-manifest artifact, a component manifest body, or a complete registered schema document. Not of a canonicalization of anything. |
355	| `canonical-record` | raw SHA256 of `C(record)` for a **named registered record**. The annotation names it: a `#/$defs/…` record of this bundle, a `{document, selector}` record registered by another unit's pinned schema, a record `registeredBy` a sibling schema-document digest, or the workflow `PayloadRegistryV1` row keyed by an import's `kind` and `payloadDomain`. |
356	| `h-identity` | the lowercase hex of `H(D, X)` — either a typed object of a domain in the table above, carried with its prefix, or the **bare 64-hex suffix** of a domain in a named domain set. Never raw SHA256 of the payload. |
357	| `capability-manifest-id` | the inherited CVE1 recipe `SHA256(UTF8("opensip.capability-manifest.v1") ‖ 00 ‖ committedBytes)`, closed to `plan.capabilityManifestId`, `run.capabilityManifestId` and the `capability-manifest` reference domain. |

359	The four retention modes are closed:
360	
361	| Retention | Meaning |
362	|---|---|
363	| `preimage` (default) | the exact preimage bytes are retained in the content-addressed store **under this digest**; the closure checker fetches them and re-hashes. |
364	| `fragment` | the preimage is a canonical sub-object of an already retained record; the annotation's `locatedBy` states which record and which addressing rule, and the closure checker recomputes it there rather than storing it twice. Closed to `program-predicate.nodeDigest`. |
365	| `derived` | recomputed from another retained artifact by the stated recipe. Closed to `capabilityManifestId`, derived from the `capabilityManifestBytesDigest` artifact. |
366	| `owner-retained` | the named owning contract retains and admits the bytes; this closure joins by digest equality only. Closed to `owner-source-set[].ownerFileManifestSha256`, owned by security's `RepoExecutionGrantV2` owner admission. |
367	
368	Because `H(D, X)` is `SHA256` of the framed preimage, **one** content-addressed
369	store keyed by raw SHA256 retains all three of raw artifacts, canonical records
370	and H identities: the object retained under a bare-hex `h-identity` digest is the
371	exact H preimage frame
372	`ASCII("opensip.product.v1") ‖ 00 ‖ ASCII(D) ‖ 00 ‖ uint64BE(length(C(X))) ‖ C(X)`.
373	Frame admission is exact and is not a blob escape: the literal prefix must match,
374	the domain must be a member of the annotation's named domain set, the declared
375	length must equal the remaining byte count, the remainder must be byte-identical
376	to `C` of its own parse, and the parsed payload must validate under the record
377	that the domain set registers for that domain. A frame is admissible **only**
378	where the annotation says `h-identity`; conversely a raw canonical payload is
379	never admissible there, because `C(X)` does not begin with the framing prefix and
380	`SHA256(C(X))` is not `H(D, X)`. A native `sha256:`-prefixed identity and a Plan's
381	bare-hex suffix are two spellings of one H digest and can never become a raw
382	payload SHA256, in either direction. Offering a frame where a `canonical-record`
383	is required fails parsing; offering a payload where a frame is required fails the
384	prefix.
385	
386	Two things are easy to conflate here, so they are separated explicitly. The
387	**annotation** is what closes a field: it says which representation and retention
388	that one field has. A **spelling** — a bare 64-hex string, a `sha256:` prefix, a
389	`fact2:`/`plan2:` typed prefix — is not an annotation and never implies one. This
390	contract does not claim that every prefixed identity in the graph carries the same
391	annotation, and no reader should infer that from the prefix: a typed prefix tells
392	you which domain *table* interprets the value, while the field's own annotation
393	tells you what the value *is*. Where a field carries the bare 64-hex suffix of an
394	`h-identity`, the annotation must name the **domain set** that resolves it,
395	because the suffix alone does not.
396	
397	`plan.nativeContextDigests` is exactly this case, and it is a **set**. A Plan may
398	name several admitted native contexts, including **several of the same language** —
399	two TypeScript projects under one Plan is ordinary, not exceptional. Nothing
400	elects one of them by position, by display order or by any other scalar. A fact's
401	`sourceUniverse` is an `h-identity` of a semantic-universe domain, and that
402	universe record names **its own** `nativeContextId`; that is what selects the
403	corresponding context, and the closure requires the selected context to be one the
404	Plan committed to. There is no arbitrary scalar display anywhere in that
405	selection.

487	### The payload registry
488	
489	An earlier draft of this section additionally required "a document offered as a
490	*payload* schema must constrain the payload directly, so a multi-record bundle
491	cannot pass vacuously". **That requirement is withdrawn.** It contradicted the
492	native and workflow registries, which correctly hash the *exact full schema
493	document bytes* and validate through a registered **selector**; under the
494	withdrawn rule their own bundles were non-conforming, and no registry row named
495	a single-record document to replace them. The bundles were right and the sentence
496	was wrong.
497	
498	What replaces it is the thing that was actually missing: a closed registry saying,
499	for each payload, exactly which document bytes are hashed and which selector
500	validates. `identity-schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-payload-registry` is that
501	registry. For every class in it:
502	
503	- `payloadSchemaDigest` is the **raw SHA-256 of the exact full bytes of the
504	  document the row names** — never a canonicalization of a selected `$def`;
505	- admission validates the payload against the row's **selector**, resolved through
506	  the pinned local closure with no network retrieval, so a multi-record bundle is
507	  admitted through its row and never needs a root type;
508	- the codec is `C`;
509	- a key with no row **refuses**. There is no default row, no caller-selected
510	  schema and no inferred one. A key name prefixed `payload.` is read from the
511	  parsed payload; every other name is read from the naming record.
512	
513	| Class | Keyed by | Document and selector |
514	|---|---|---|
515	| `relation` | `fact.relation` | `foundation/relation-payload-schemas.v2.json`, selector from that document's own `x-opensip-relation-registry` row |
516	| `coverage` | `payload.schemaVersion` | `native/native-evidence.schemas.v2.json#/$defs/CoverageResultV3` |
517	| `import` | `import.kind` + `payload.payloadDomain` | the workflow `PayloadRegistryV1` / native §7.1 rows, mirrored; Run closure re-derives them from the workflow registry and refuses on drift, so the two cannot diverge |
518	| `parameter` | the cited `schemaDigest` | a document on the closed list: `foundation/import-source-context.schema.json`, and `workflows/schemas/policy-document.schema.json#/$defs/ScopeDocumentV1` |
519	
520	`view.schemaDigests` names the registered documents a view admitted, and each
521	member must be one of them.
522	
523	**The `ScopeDocumentV1` parameter row (CB3-MUST-4).** The comparison contract
524	states that `EvaluationContext.scopeDigest` is the workflow glob scope-policy
525	document "bound as an analysis-spec parameter", and the `parameter` class was
526	closed to a single document. A key with no row refuses — there is no default row
527	and no caller-selected schema — so that binding refused at Plan admission and
528	the comparison scope axis (E2 to E3) could not be populated at all: one contract
529	required a binding a sibling contract's closed registry forbade. The row is
530	registered rather than the mechanism abandoned, because the scope policy is a
531	genuine Plan input and the parameter class is where Plan inputs are admitted.
532	
533	It is deliberately a **different record** from the foundation `scope-descriptor`
534	that `plan.scopeDigest` names, and neither substitutes for the other:
535	`scope-descriptor` is the repository extent actually walked (workspace roots and
536	path prefixes), `ScopeDocumentV1` is the policy's include/exclude glob selection
537	over that extent. Both may appear in one Plan. Because the class is keyed by the
538	cited **document** digest, two rows selecting different records out of one
539	document would be indistinguishable and the first listed would silently win;
540	that is the arbitrary selection the registry law forbids, so an ambiguous key
541	refuses. The class remains closed: a real but unregistered document, and a
542	caller-chosen permissive one, both still refuse.
543	
544	**Where the binding is actually decided, and where it is only asserted.**
545	Registering the row makes a lawful scope parameter admissible at Plan closure;
546	it does not by itself bind the *comparison* context to it. `adopt_baseline`
547	assigns `context.scopeDigest` from the scope document it is **passed**, and its
548	`plan` argument is a PlanId **string** — so that assignment records the digest
549	of whatever document the caller supplied and is **not** evidence that the
550	document was the Run's selected analysis-spec parameter. The same holds for
551	`policyDigest` and `waiverSetDigest`. Calling that assignment a binding would be
552	false, and this contract does not.
553	
554	The honest boundary is therefore stated rather than implied. `adopt_baseline` is
555	a **pure projection over documents the caller must already have admitted**, and
556	its precondition is exactly that `policy`, `scope` and `waivers` are the
557	documents the Plan selected. Selection membership is decidable only with the
558	retained analysis-spec record in hand, so a bounded verifier takes that record
559	and proves it: the scope document's canonical digest must be the `payloadDigest`
560	of a selected parameter row citing the registered `ScopeDocumentV1` **document**
561	digest. A document that is not selected, a spec that selects no scope parameter,
562	and a row cited under another schema each refuse with their own typed reason.
563	When the analysis spec is supplied, `adopt_baseline` performs that verification;
564	when it is not, the scope binding is a **caller assertion** and this contract
565	says so rather than implying a join. Neither path changes the baseline
566	descriptor or its identity, and no product host is implied here.
567	
568	The two scope records remain different things throughout: the foundation
569	`scope-descriptor` that `plan.scopeDigest` names is the repository extent
570	actually walked, while `ScopeDocumentV1` is the operator's include/exclude glob
571	policy over that extent.

573	### `fact2` payload encoding: one explicit successor law
574	
575	The inherited `fact-plane.v1.json`
576	`$.factRecordContractV1.relationPayloadSchemaRegistryV1.canonicalPayloadEncoding`
577	is a deterministic-CBOR profile that forbids negative integers and non-NFC text,
578	while `fact2.payloadDigest` is a `canonical-record` digest under `C`, which admits
579	both. Two owning statements in direct contradiction is a design defect, so this
580	contract settles it in one direction and says exactly what changes.
581	
582	**`fact2` payloads are `C`.** There is one product encoder and no second codec in
583	the trusted computing base. Every *logical* restriction the CBOR profile carried
584	survives, as an admission rule expressed in the registered schema rather than
585	implied by a codec: NFC-only text, no negative integers, `uint64` range, the
586	closed field set, the enums, the per-rung required/forbidden fields and the
587	`universeRule`. `foundation/relation-payload-schemas.v2.json` carries all
588	thirteen relations — the twelve inherited from fact-plane plus native §4.4's
589	`unresolved-edge` — reproducing each inherited `required`, `optional`, field type
590	and enum exactly, and its `x-opensip-relation-registry` carries each relation's
591	selector, universe rule and rung ladder.
592	
593	**The ladder is an explicit array, and `rungs` is not it (CB3-MUST-1).** That
594	registry had no `ladder` key at all. Its `rungs` member is a per-rung
595	required/forbidden **field-rule** table, and it is legitimately the empty object
596	for a relation with no per-rung field variance — which is every single-rung
597	relation: `file`, `package`, `vcs-change`, `declares`, `literal`,
598	`control-flow`, `reachability` and `clones`. Reading `rungs` as the ladder gives
599	two conforming readings and both are wrong: read strictly, those eight relations
600	admit no `resolution` at all and no Run of the kind these contracts require
601	could close; read leniently — as the reference closure did, via an
602	`and row['rungs']` guard — the ladder check is skipped entirely for them, and a
603	`declares` fact carrying `resolved-callee`, a rung of `calls`, closes a Run.
604	The rung vocabulary is shared across relations, so such a value is perfectly
605	well-formed; **schema vocabulary is not relation membership.**
606	
607	Each row therefore carries an explicit ordered **`ladder`**, weakest-first,
608	inherited verbatim from `fact-plane.v1 relationRegistry.relations[].ladder` plus
609	`[observed]` for `unresolved-edge`. This registry is the **single authority**;
610	`native_evidence_model.v2.LADDERS` and
611	`capability-manifest-domains.v2 RELATION-LADDER-DOMAIN-V2.ladders` are declared
612	mirrors of it and are drift-checked **exactly and in order**. Order is not
613	decoration: the capability registry's arrays had been alphabetised while still
614	naming the inherited ladder as their source, which reversed `calls`, `imports`
615	and `references` — harmless only because that registry is consulted for
616	membership alone, and an inversion for anything that read it as an order.
617	
618	Membership is decided against `ladder`, always, with **no empty-ladder
619	fallback**: a relation with no ladder is a registry defect and refuses rather
620	than admitting anything. Order comparison is the index within one relation's
621	own ladder. Nothing orders a rung of one relation against a rung of another,
622	and there is no global rank; a cross-relation comparison is an admission
623	refusal, never a true or false predicate.
624	
625	**One rung vocabulary, named directly (CB3-MUST-2).** The policy DSL previously
626	carried its own abstract tier vocabulary — `syntax`, `resolved`, `type`,
627	`external` — reached from `PolicyDocumentV1` `Atom.minResolution` and reused by
628	repair's `EvidenceRequirement`. It shared **zero** members with the fifteen rung
629	names every fact, Coverage entry and native `RequirementV2` actually carries, no
630	document mapped one onto the other, and the evaluator compared them through a
631	single global rank table (`{syntax:0, resolved:1, type:2, external:1}`) shared by
632	every relation. Whether `minResolution: resolved` was satisfied by
633	`resolved-target`, by `resolved-binding`, by `checked` or by all three is a
634	public semantic decision, so two conforming implementations emitted different
635	findings from the same Plan.
636	
637	Preserving the abstract syntax with a published mapping was considered and
638	rejected. Such a mapping must be **per relation** — `resolved` names a different
639	rung in each of `imports`, `references`, `calls` and `reachability`, `type`
640	names a rung only for `types`, and `external` names no native rung at all — so
641	it is a partial, lossy renaming with no expressive power, and it does not even
642	preserve the one-word-one-meaning property that motivates an abstract syntax. It
643	also cannot survive C-1: `syntax < resolved < type` **is** a global ladder, and
644	making it relation-relative dissolves it into the rung names. The smaller and
645	coherent correction is to name the rung: `Atom.minResolution` and
646	`EvidenceRequirement.minResolution` are rung names, the abstract `Resolution`
647	enum and the global `RES_ORDER` rank are **withdrawn**, and satisfaction is
648	ladder-index comparison inside one relation.
649	
650	Two admission conditions follow, because no schema keyword can express the
651	second without restating the ladders and creating another independent source.
652	The schema constrains `minResolution` to the flat rung vocabulary — exactly the
653	union of the registry's ladders, drift-checked — which is **necessary**.
654	Membership of *this atom's relation's* ladder is **sufficient** and is enforced
655	at admission: in the workflow policy resolver, and at the **Run closure**, over
656	both the Plan's `PolicyDocumentV1` and the proof's compiled `RuleProgramV1`. An
657	evaluator-only check would let a sealed Run assert a predicate that was never
658	admissible. Atom relations are closed too: an atom names either one of the
659	thirteen native fact relations or one of the imported-evidence relations closed
660	by `imported-evidence.schema.json#/x-opensip-evidence-relation-registry`
661	(`runtime-observation`, `history-change`, each with the one-rung ladder
662	`[observed]` — no new rung token), and an evidence relation must declare its
663	`evidence` kind while a native fact relation must not.
664	
665	**What does not change:** historical `FactRecord1` records, their CBOR wire bytes
666	and their provenance are untouched and remain valid history. They are never a
667	`fact2` preimage, and this contract has always said the historical wrapper cannot
668	bind a `snapshot2` identifier. **The conversion is stated, not delegated:** a
669	provider that emits deterministic CBOR has its payload decoded under the selected
670	registered schema and re-encoded to `C` by the trusted first-party host adapter
671	before `fact2` is minted; the adapter refuses rather than repairs a payload that
672	violates any retained restriction, and persistence stores the `C` bytes that
673	`payloadDigest` names. No unspecified adapter invents a schema.
674	
675	Joined at Run closure for every fact: the relation must be registered;
676	`payloadSchemaDigest` must be the relation document's own file digest;
677	`resolution` must be a rung of that relation's ladder; that rung's required and
678	forbidden fields must hold; and `universeRule: same-only` requires
679	`sourceUniverse == targetUniverse`.

681	#### Relation payloads: the digest law, and what a payload's claim is joined to
682	
683	The closing digest law above governs identity-schemas.v2, and the native contract
684	extends it to its own bundle. `foundation/relation-payload-schemas.v2.json` was

681	#### Relation payloads: the digest law, and what a payload's claim is joined to
682	
683	The closing digest law above governs identity-schemas.v2, and the native contract
684	extends it to its own bundle. `foundation/relation-payload-schemas.v2.json` was
685	governed by **neither**, so its digest-bearing and path-bearing fields carried no
686	annotation and a `file` payload's `path`, `contentSha256` and `byteLength` were
687	joined to nothing at all: a schema-valid fact could claim any content hash for
688	any path, including a path in no snapshot, and close a Run. That was a real
689	defect and this is its closure, as a class rather than as one field.
690	
691	That document now carries its own `x-opensip-digest-law`, and **every**
692	`DigestHex`, `Sha256Text` and `CanonicalPath` field in it is annotated with its
693	representation, producing preimage or codec, retention and owning authority. The
694	law is **consumed, not declared**: every annotated field must be reachable from
695	its relation's registry joins or must declare `retention: not-joined` with its
696	reason, and every field a join names must exist in the selector. A newly
697	annotated field with no join refuses, so this omission cannot recur silently.
698	
699	The relation document's annotation law also governs schema structure. A governed
700	occurrence is a reference to `DigestHex`, `Sha256Text` or `CanonicalPath`, including
701	an intermediate local `$defs` alias, or an inline pattern exactly equal to one of
702	those definitions' patterns. Follow local references, nested `properties`,
703	`items`, `additionalProperties` and `oneOf`/`anyOf`/`allOf` branches when checking
704	these occurrences. Following local references must terminate even when a local
705	definition is cyclic. An annotation on the occurrence, its enclosing schema
706	path, or an intermediate alias applies to that occurrence. An annotation on
707	the terminal governed scalar definition does **not** provide a blanket default
708	for all references to that type. Directly annotated top-level selector
709	properties remain subject to retention and join checks even when their scalar
710	form is not one of these three.
711	
712	Every governed occurrence must have an effective annotation. An annotated
713	alternative does not cover an unannotated alternative; a parent annotation may
714	cover each alternative it encloses. When multiple schema paths reach the same
715	location, any occurrence lacking an effective annotation makes that location
716	inadmissible. Later annotated occurrences cannot undo that absence. Object-key
717	order and the order in which these paths are visited must not change admission.
718	
719	There is no precedence rule between disagreeing effective annotations at one
720	location: distinct annotations conflict and the document refuses; repeated
721	annotations that are equal under typed canonical equality do not conflict.
722	Every effective annotation must use the declared retention vocabulary. These
723	same effective annotations govern coverage, retention and join/exemption checks;
724	none of those checks may silently revert to inspecting only direct properties.
725	
726	The current registry's join fields address top-level selector properties.
727	Taking a scalar alternative of such a property preserves that address; entering
728	an object member, array element or map value does not. A governed occurrence at
729	one of those nested locations must explicitly declare `retention: not-joined`.
730	As elsewhere in this law, the reason for an exemption is stated on the field
731	for a reader; admission checks the declared retention, not the presence or
732	content of that prose. It cannot claim a joinable retention that the current
733	join vocabulary cannot address. An addressable annotated property requires its
734	registry join unless it declares that exemption, and every named join field
735	must exist in the selector. Missing annotations, conflicting annotations,
736	undeclared retention values, unaddressable claimed joins, missing joins and
737	joins naming absent fields all refuse at schema-law admission. This check
738	establishes coherence of the registered schema; the owning-fact snapshot and
739	retained-byte joins below still establish the truth of each admitted payload.
740	
741	`x-opensip-relation-registry` carries a normative per-relation **`snapshotJoins`**
742	table, and Run closure applies it to **every owning fact** — after the registered
743	selector validation, and **independently of the payload decode memo**, because
744	the truth of a claim about a snapshot is a property of the *owner*, not of the
745	bytes. A payload alone cannot decide it, so the closure requires owner context:
746	the enclosing fact, the snapshot **that fact names**, the retained blobs and the
747	bound native context. The four relations that make such a claim:
748	
749	| Relation | Join |
750	|---|---|
751	| `file` | `path` must be in the enclosing fact's snapshot source inventory; `contentSha256` must equal that inventory row's digest; `byteLength` must equal its length; the bytes must be **retained** under that digest and re-hash to it; and every anchor of the fact must lie in the very file the payload claims. |
752	| `package` | `manifestPath` must be in that inventory. |
753	| `vcs-change` | `path` must be in that inventory **unless** `changeKind` is `deleted`, where the path is by definition absent from the analysed snapshot. |
754	| `clones` | the framed body-identity join below. |
755	
756	`vcs-change.previousPath` is the one declared exemption. A pre-rename path names
757	a state **before** the analysed snapshot; it is a historical observation, not a

767	#### `clones`: the inherited body recipe, reused and not restated

771	`#/canonicalisationSchema`, `#/normalisationLadder` and

776	- `normalisationVersion` is the raw SHA-256 of the **exact retained canonical
777	  level-specification bytes** — the per-language lexical boundary rules, canonical
778	  token-kind registry, directive classification, transform order and replacement
779	  byte rules. A human version label is insufficient and an opaque caller hash is
780	  inadmissible; the specification is retained and re-hashed at closure.
781	- `bodyIdentity` is `sha256:` followed by SHA-256 of the **fully framed,
782	  domain-separated preimage**: `u8 len‖"opensip.fact-identity.v1"`,
783	  `u8 len‖levelId`, `u8 len‖levelVersion` as the **raw 32 digest bytes and never
784	  the hexadecimal display text**, `u8 len‖languageId`, `u8 len‖languageVersion`,
785	  then `u32be len‖payload`. Unframed concatenation is forbidden. At
786	  `L0-verbatim` the payload is `u32be raw_byte_len ‖ the exact body-span bytes`
787	  with tokenisation forbidden; at `L1`–`L3` it is the level's framed token stream.
788	- The frame itself is **retained** under that 64-hex suffix, so closure fetches
789	  it, re-hashes it, parses it and joins each component to something the Run has
790	  already admitted: the domain tag to the policy, `levelId` to the payload's own
791	  `normalisationLevel`, `levelVersion` to the retained specification, and
792	  `languageId`/`languageVersion` to the fact's own semantic universe.
793	- `languageVersion` is the **raw 32 bytes of `SHA-256(C(body-language-version))`**

795	  `levelVersion`, so the inherited frame bytes and field grammar are unchanged.
796	  Fixed width is not a convenience: the inherited frame gives each component a
797	  **`u8` length**, and any component built by embedding per-crate or per-package
798	  data is not representable for ordinary valid inputs. A Rust workspace of
799	  twenty-one crates already produces 723 bytes of raw map, against a maximum of
800	  255.

817	Dialect is **body specific**, per language, closed, and always **selected** —

1016	waivers. The declarative rule program defines the exact subject enumeration,

1012	## 4. Evaluation and proof verification
1013	
1014	The deterministic evaluator consumes only the Plan-bound, schema-admitted
1015	finite fact views, Coverage, imported evidence, declarative program, policy and
1016	waivers. The declarative rule program defines the exact subject enumeration,
1017	relation/rung, typed field filter, quantifier, deterministic work bound and
1018	emission condition for each predicate. Query planning is an optimization only:
1019	a retained full-scan reference must agree on selected facts. Neither a provider
1020	nor a witness supplies its own expected result or filter. All consumed data are
1021	listed in the proof's evaluationInputRefs; no hidden lookup is allowed.
1022	
1023	A predicate proof binds rule, subject, predicate, operation, admitted inputs,
1024	scopes, value and a retained witness digest. The closed witness record contains
1025	schemaVersion=2, program predicate digest, sorted matching fact IDs, sorted
1026	Coverage IDs, optional integer count limit and sorted child-predicate IDs.
1027	The program predicate digest is the §3 `program-predicate` record, which addresses
1028	the exact node of the admitted rule program this proof discharges; the predicate
1029	ID and the child predicate IDs are that section's node addresses, not free
1030	labels. An atomic witness names no children; boolean witnesses name only earlier
1031	nodes in the same subject/rule DAG, and each named child must itself be proven
1032	for the same rule and subject. Predicate IDs are unique and the DAG is bounded
1033	by the rule program's admitted work bound. Witness facts must be exactly those
1034	selected by the program over the complete admitted view, not merely a subset
1035	chosen by the producer. Counts count distinct selected fact IDs. The verifier
1036	recomputes scope membership, matches, completeness and each result, and then
1037	recomputes finding fingerprints, findings, rule outcomes and aggregate verdict.
1038	Missing witness bytes is retention loss, not a false predicate.
1039	
1040	| Predicate | Positive/complete case | Incomplete case |
1041	|---|---|---|
1042	| exists | true on a matching fact; false only on complete absence | true on a known match, otherwise indeterminate |
1043	| none | false on a known match; true only on complete absence | false on a known match, otherwise indeterminate |
1044	| count-at-most N | false once more than N distinct matches exist; true when complete count ≤ N | false above N, otherwise indeterminate |
1045	| all-covered | true only with admitted resolution-complete coverage for the requested universe/rung | indeterminate |
1046	| and / or / not | strong Kleene three-valued logic; false dominates and, true dominates or | unresolved value propagates unless dominated |
1047	
1048	Completeness means the native contract's examined partition **and** resolution
1049	and closed-world requirements. An unresolved `m[k]()` can never establish
1050	no-consumer merely because the enumerator visited all subjects. Runtime unhit
1051	observations never supply universal static completeness. A rule expression that
1052	is true produces its declared outcome; findings arise only from the program's
1053	emission condition. A false condition is a retained no-match proof. An
1054	indeterminate required predicate is retained with typed deficiency. A schema,
1055	identity or interpreter fault is an operational failure, not a fourth logical
1056	truth value and not an authoritative Run. Aggregate policy fail dominates
1057	indeterminate, which dominates pass; a required operational fault has D9's
1058	operational precedence even if other steps have committed failing Runs.
1059	
1060	Before sealing, the host independently replays the admitted deterministic
1061	program against the retained closure and compares the complete normalized
1062	result (all predicate outcomes, omissions, findings and verdict), not just a
1063	checksum supplied by the producer. This verifier is first-party trusted code;
1064	this is reproducible verification, not a proof of mathematical soundness or a
1065	sandbox against a malicious host. Semantic conformance uses independent
1066	oracles and mutation cases. The exact evaluator executable, declarative program,
1067	input closure and witness bytes are retained, so an independent installation
1068	can replay without trusting the original result flags. No old Python route
1069	region is executed to decide product authority.
1070	
1071	Verification reads retained objects and creates an operational verification
1072	receipt. Regeneration executes the exact retained producer and Plan input
1073	closure into a candidate namespace, verifies each expected semantic identity,
1074	and publishes recovered availability only if all required bytes agree. A
1075	mismatch is an operational regeneration verification refusal: `HOST.IO_FAILURE`
1076	(class `operational-failed`, faultCause `host-io`, exit4), domain detail
1077	`evidence.regeneration-mismatch`. It cannot replace the sealed Run. New
1078	source or policy creates a new Plan/Run. Expired or
1079	revoked permission cannot be resurrected by a matching hash. A miss recomputes
1080	normally; a corrupt hit is quarantined and disclosed before any permitted retry.
1081	
1082	**Constructing a cache key and admitting a hit are two different acts, and only
1083	the second is an admission.** Key construction is pure and deterministic: exact
1084	schema admission and canonical order over the `cache-key` record, nothing more. It
1085	reads no bytes and resolves no reference, so a host may compute it before loading
1086	anything and miss cheaply; it is a lookup key and grants nothing. **Finding bytes
1087	under a matching key is not authority.** An entry may be consumed only against
1088	exactly the closure the Run itself requires: the stage spec retained and joined to
1089	this Plan, the producing closure retained and Plan-selected, every `scopeIds`
1090	member a retained `subject-scope` of this snapshot, the output schema document
1091	retained, and every `inputRefs` entry resolved through the same
1092	`x-opensip-digest-domains` registry the Run uses — so a consumed native context
1093	must be one this Plan selected, a consumed import must be one this Plan selected,
1094	and nothing is admitted under a guessed payload-domain schema. A bare
1095	`coverage-payload`, `import-payload` or `fact-payload` reference is refused as an
1096	authoritative root rather than resolved by guesswork; those are reached only
1097	through their owning object. A hit that clears all of this is reusable producer
1098	output, never evidence authority, and it never replaces or re-seals a Run. The
1099	same record and the same admission apply to a regeneration key; only the H domain
1100	differs, and a regeneration whose result disagrees remains the
1101	`evidence.regeneration-mismatch` refusal above.

1103	## 5. Durable custody and failure protocol
1104	
1105	Default `opensip`/`analyze` is DURABLE_AUTHORITATIVE under CD-RT-5. The host
1106	reports retention origin DEFAULTED and durable-unbounded posture before first
1107	write; the command's documented effect is admission of the project marker and
1108	private registry/store, followed by an authoritative Run. No implicit policy
1109	file is written. Explicit retention overrides have independent byte/time/count
1110	bounds with provenance; failure to satisfy an authoritative request never
1111	silently demotes it to ephemeral. `--ephemeral` is explicitly non-authoritative,
1112	uses temporary custody, mints no authoritative commit receipt and cannot satisfy
1113	baseline adoption, repair or authoritative replay prerequisites.
1114	
1115	The storage-root admission still applies the inherited sync, backup and private
1116	custody classifications separately. A detected backup-managed root requires an
1117	explicit storage-policy choice before the first source-derived write (TM V17):
1118	select another admitted root, choose explicit ephemeral mode, or acknowledge
1119	backup custody for this invocation with `--allow-backup-custody` (or the
1120	corresponding already-admitted host storage-policy record). CI never prompts;
1121	without that explicit choice it refuses REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED with detail
1122	`storage.backup-choice-required`, before creating evidence. The acknowledgement
1123	is retained as operational custody metadata; it does not alter semantic Run
1124	identity or silently write a policy file. UNKNOWN backup status is disclosed as
1125	unknown, never as not-backed-up. Purge never claims deletion of external copies.
1126	Sync/upload roots and group/ACL exposure retain their separate admission rules;
1127	a backup acknowledgement is not a network-export or shared-storage grant.
1128	
1129	Exactly one per-project writer holds the lifecycle lease/fence through source
1130	admission, evaluation and atomic commit. Read-only clients use a consistent
1131	committed ledger snapshot and never wait while holding a lock needed by the
1132	writer. Global trust admission and revocation use the security contract's lock
1133	order. SQLite WAL, transaction settings, fsync/atomic-rename carrier and crash
1134	reconciliation retain the reviewed lifecycle carrier's native obligations;
1135	the reference model here tests the semantic transition, not OS durability.
1136	
1137	Commit order:
1138	
1139	1. Validate closure and independently replay proof; compute all final IDs.
1140	2. Write immutable blobs and descriptors to private temporary files, verify
1141	   digest/length, fsync files, atomically publish under digest, fsync directories.
1142	3. In one synchronous ledger transaction insert Run manifest, object references,
1143	   retained availability generation, baseline/other authorized pins and a commit
1144	   receipt with ExecutionId, namespace, monotonic sequence, inventory digest,
1145	   signer and immutable assurance; commit and satisfy the carrier's barriers.
1146	4. Only then acknowledge commitment. Required rendering/delivery is later and
1147	   cannot rewrite the Run. Receipt signing is operational custody evidence and
1148	   excluded from semantic IDs; the receipt authenticates RunId and inventory.
1149	
1150	A failure before step 3 publishes no authoritative Run. Orphan blobs are
1151	unreferenced and eligible for GC after reconciliation. A crash after ledger
1152	commit but before acknowledgement is `durability-undetermined` to the caller,
1153	exit 4, with an ExecutionId for read-only recovery. Recovery checks the ledger
1154	and actual objects; it returns committed or failed, never repeats a repository
1155	mutation. Duplicate retry can share a Run but has a separate attempt receipt.
1156	An acknowledged Run with missing/corrupt objects becomes partially available or
1157	corrupt; the host does not pretend it was never sealed.
1158	
1159	Sealed assurance is immutable: verified means exact identity+proof checks at
1160	seal; verifiable also commits the verification closure; replayable also commits
1161	all exact admitted producer executables and source/input closure. The default
1162	authoritative profile requires replayable retention at seal. Current
1163	availability is a separate monotonic-generation record: retained, partial,
1164	expired, purged, corrupt or unavailable, with exact missing references and
1165	cause. Availability may improve through verified restoration or regeneration;
1166	sealed assurance and historical verdict never change. A query reports both.
1167	
1168	Retention roots include every live Run's required closure, active baseline,
1169	authorized repair prerequisite and backup/export operation pin. Automatic
1170	expiry respects these pins and all independent policy bounds; it refuses a
1171	new durable admission if the required closure cannot be retained within bounds.
1172	A direct purge of a pinned Run refuses unless the explicit destructive purge
1173	also revokes the named pins after disclosing consequences. That refusal has a
1174	registered public projection and this contract does not restate it: the
1175	foundation-owned detail `evidence.pinned` projects as `request-rejected`,
1176	`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`, exit 2, carrying the closed
1177	`common.schema.json#/$defs/PinnedPurgeDisclosure` — the RunId, the complete
1178	current `activePins` inventory sorted uniquely by `pinId`, and the three ordered
1179	consequences `named-pins-revoked`,
1180	`dependent-evidence-replay-unavailable`, `sealed-history-retained` — exactly as
1181	**workflows-and-surfaces §12** specifies. No pin is omitted, truncated or
1182	aggregated into a count. Neither that disclosure nor any flag confers authority:
1183	a later destructive attempt still requires the explicit lifecycle authorization
1184	and disclosure of its then-current complete pin set, and a changed pin inventory
1185	requires renewed disclosure before destruction. Purge retains the
1186	minimal sealed manifest, provenance and tombstone but deletes unshared evidence
1187	bytes by reachability GC; shared bytes survive until the final reference is
1188	removed. Purged is not deleted-history. The user may separately destroy the
1189	whole project store/marker under lifecycle authorization; no indefinite privacy
1190	claim is made for backups or exports already outside that store.
1191	
1192	A retention decision never changes a fact, Coverage, finding or Run identity.
1193	It never turns expired evidence into `no match`. Query of retained manifest is
1194	allowed after purge and states evidence unavailable. Query requiring actual
1195	proof, comparison baseline or repair input refuses with
1196	REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED and `evidence.{expired,purged,missing,corrupt}`
1197	before evaluation (exit 2); inability during a selected operation is HOST.IO_FAILURE
1198	with evidence detail (exit 4). Successfully admitted partial native inputs may
1199	instead produce an indeterminate Run (exit 3) under the native and D9 contracts.
1200	These are different event positions, not interchangeable error spellings.
1201	
1202	Backup/export holds a read snapshot plus short-lived object pins, writes a
1203	bounded relative-path inventory, hashes and verifies every object, then seals
1204	the bundle. Import checks path traversal, symlinks, sizes, duplicate paths,
1205	cryptographic identities and all referenced schemas before publishing anything.
1206	Source provenance/authenticity is reported separately from hash integrity.
1207	Trust floors, current authorization and local custody receipts are never
1208	restored backwards from an evidence backup. Portable baseline details are in
1209	the workflow contract. An import cannot silently claim a remote Run was locally
1210	evaluated: its imported-custody receipt names origin and local verification.
1211	
1212	## 6. Required implementation conformance
1213	
1214	Reference checks cover exact numeric and canonical encodings, wrong-source and
1215	wrong-Plan joins, identity changes for each semantic input, operational identity
1216	exclusion, universal negatives under incomplete resolution, proof tampering,
1217	retention/purge invariance and crash acknowledgement states. They additionally
1218	assert the digest law mechanically: that every 64-hex field carries a registered
1219	representation, that each new closed record reproduces an independently computed
1220	canonical digest vector and moves under every single-field mutation, and that a
1221	complete Run with a non-empty native context set closes while an altered frame, a
1222	missing preimage, a wrong preimage, an unregistered H domain, a raw payload
1223	offered as an H identity and a hidden input each refuse with a typed cause. They
1224	also assert that a fully re-framed and re-keyed Run built around a context the
1225	native boundary refuses — contradicting honored options, a compiler or runtime
1226	digest outside the tool closure, an incomplete stdlib inventory, a component
1227	digest that is not the retained tree's, a compiler version not from the manifest,
1228	a universe contradicting its context, or a config graph or lockfile path outside
1229	the snapshot — is refused with that boundary's own typed refusal string. They
1230	exercise a complete Rust universe/fact/Coverage Run alongside the TypeScript one,
1231	with the nested dependency, features, config-projection and prepared-output
1232	records retained and joined; and they separate cache key construction from cache
1233	hit admission, showing that a key needs no bytes while a hit needs the Run's whole
1234	closure. Their source pins
1235	and independent review are part of D-372. They do not qualify a native carrier.
1236	
1237	Before shipping, the exact implementation must additionally demonstrate:
1238	all supported platform fsync/SQLite/process-death cases; concurrent readers and
1239	writers plus trust revocation; independent replay across machines; missing,
1240	corrupt, stale and wrong-tenant closure rejection; hostile archive import; GC
1241	with shared references; backup restoration preserving trust floors; and public
1242	D9/CLI/JSON/SARIF/HTML/agent parity. Those are implementation acceptance criteria
1243	under existing G gates, not unresolved design alternatives.
1244	
1245	### Reference lifecycle joins
1246	
1247	The reference store instantiates closed commit-receipt and availability records.
1248	An availability transition increments generation and never rewrites a sealed Run
1249	or its original assurance. Read-only `recover(ExecutionId)` inspects the committed
1250	receipt after a lost acknowledgement and never repeats effects. Verified restoration
1251	requires the same complete identity closure and replay result before availability
1252	returns to retained; a regeneration mismatch refuses. Physical fsync, authenticated
1253	receipt signing, shared-blob deletion and OS crash recovery remain implementation
1254	qualification obligations; the reference transitions do not claim to execute them.
1255	
1256	The security chapter's three lease modes refine the inherited single-writer rule:
1257	immutable readers coexist with the append writer; exclusive migration/purge acquires
1258	the writer lease and reader exclusion. No second writer is permitted.
1259	
1260	At Run closure, every Plan-selected import re-admits its retained canonical SourceCorrespondence. An exact-snapshot import must name the Plan snapshot. VCS-revision imports require a retained, canonical admitted SourceMappingV1 to that snapshot, with inventory-matching source digests and the current clean revision; an unmapped/stale intake artifact may remain available for inspection but cannot be selected as an analyzed Plan input. Intake storage does not establish this source join. The authenticated importer/evaluator still owns payload-schema, observation-scope and polarity admission; rehashing an opaque import is insufficient. The reference closure reuses the same workflow import/mapping schema admission functions so the source law has one implementation.
1261	
1262	The semantic grant's `prepare-code` operation is present exactly when it projects trusted-repository-code preparation principals. Their provenance comes from consumed admitted host-prepared inputs; no test-runner operation or principal is added. Verification/replay checks these immutable bindings without reusing expired operational grants.
1263	
1264	The expected VCS build context is explicit, never inferred from the imported claim. The host may select one analysis-spec parameter whose schemaDigest is the raw SHA-256 of `foundation/import-source-context.schema.json` and whose payloadDigest binds canonical ImportSourceContextV1 `{schemaVersion:1, declaredBuildIds:[...]}`. These expected labels come from the separately admitted analysis request/build configuration; the importer cannot nominate its own expected labels. No parameter means an empty set; more than one is refused. Labels are declarations, not proof: source mapping remains mandatory. Run closure reconstructs workflow §4's binding from this retained parameter and the snapshot's VCS observation, then applies the same staleness function (both dirty flags, revision, expected build label and admitted mapping). A label not in the expected set is wrong-build and cannot become a Plan-selected import. The schema bytes and payload are retained with the Plan parameters for independent replay.
1265	
1266	Snapshot capture consumes the same admitted boundary inventory as native discovery. The host obtains it from successful security discovery, passes it unchanged to native discovery/membership and the shared scope descriptor, and removes nested-repository, nested-project and directory-custody-excluded paths before opening or hashing snapshot source bytes. The remaining paths are only capture candidates: per-file custody, safe handles and exact hashing still precede source admission. Boundary exclusion anchors enter the Plan's scope descriptor and their operational provenance is retained beside it. The host reference join admits one inventory; caller-supplied alternative boundary lists or substituted marker sets are refused. Discovery's dependency-tree pruning is an analysis-unit rule; explicitly required native dependency read-set bytes require separate custody/closure admission and cannot cross a nested authority boundary.
1267	
1268	Every Plan with selected import2 inputs also requires read-import in its semantic grant. This includes imported-inert preparation. Close_run enforces this operation/input join as well as prepare-code/principal equality; the later consuming-Plan admission separately validates the actual preparedResolution provenance.
1269	
1270	
1271	The reference closure entry point reports a missing promised object/blob as EvidenceUnavailable carrying the closed operational-failed/HOST.IO_FAILURE/host-io termination with evidence.missing and the missing reference. It never emits a bare lookup error or turns missing witness bytes into a false predicate or admission rejection. This models the host's retained-byte/custody observation boundary. Untrusted malformed records still receive exact schema/identity admission refusal; an inventory of available retained bytes does not authorize rewriting the assurance of a sealed Run.

89	## 1. Supported native cells (AR-13)
90	
91	### 1.1 Cell coordinates
92	
93	A cell is `capability × languageMode × platformFamily`. The machine-readable
94	matrix is `native/native-capability-matrix.v2.json` (60 cells, validated by
95	`NativeCapabilityMatrixV2`). Platform families are exactly the four `platformId`
96	values in the delivery release inventory: `linux-x86_64-gnu`,
97	`linux-aarch64-gnu`, `macos-aarch64`, `macos-x86_64`. The OS/kernel/libc/filesystem
98	*baseline* that qualifies a machine into a family is owned by the security unit
99	(AR-06); this contract states only that native capabilities are platform-invariant
100	by design (`platformInvariantDesign: true`) and that no cell is `QUALIFIED` here.
101	
102	Cell states (closed): `SUPPORTED-DESIGN` (contracted behavior, corpus named,
103	qualification pending), `UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` (refuses with the named deficiency;
104	never silently narrows), `NOT-SELECTED` (outside D-371; no promise).

106	### 1.2 Language modes (closed)
107	
108	| Mode id | Recognition | Universe | Notes |
109	|---|---|---|---|
