111	| `js-allowjs` | `tsconfig.json`/`jsconfig.json` with effective `allowJs=true` (jsconfig defaults `allowJs=true`) | `typescript-v2`, `allowJs=true` | `.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` are program roots. |

116	
117	**The syntax-only universe (CB3-MUST-3).** This column previously read
118	"none (syntax-all provider)", and that made the mode's own advertised cells
119	unrepresentable. `fact2` and `subject-scope` both **require** a
120	`native-semantic-universe` h-identity, that domain set held exactly the
121	TypeScript and Rust universes, and there is no null branch — so a
122	`declares@syntactic` or `clones@normalized-body-hash` fact in `syntax-only`
123	mode, and every `file`/`package`/`vcs-change` fact in a repository containing
124	no TypeScript and no Rust unit at all, could mint no fact and no scope. An
125	implementer had to invent a third domain, invent a null branch on a required
126	identity field, or quietly narrow this table.
127	
128	The registered answer is a third universe, `native.semantic-universe.syntax.v2`,
129	over a third native context, `native.context.syntax.v2`. Making the universe
130	fields nullable was rejected: it would delete the invariant that every fact
131	states what produced it, and would leave "which grammar read this body"
132	unanswerable for exactly the facts that depend on the answer.
133	
134	- **What it carries.** The context holds one thing: the installed
135	  `SyntaxGrammarBundleV1`, pinned the way a toolchain is — an admitted
136	  `kind=grammar` closure, a `parserVersion` that must equal that closure
137	  manifest's `semanticVersion`
138	  (`native.syntax-grammar-version-not-from-manifest`), and every grammar
139	  definition, the bundle manifest and the normalizer specification present in
140	  the retained tree. It has no toolchain, no stdlib, no lockfile, no
141	  `node_modules` layout and no config graph, because a grammar-only analysis
142	  reads none of them. A syntax-only context that named a compiler would assert
143	  semantics the mode never computes.
144	- **What the universe commits.** The admitted context plus the **selected**
145	  grammar set. Selecting a different set is a different universe, exactly as
146	  selecting different compilation targets is for Rust, so what was parsed is
147	  visible to every consumer instead of being an invisible default. A selection
148	  naming a grammar the bundle does not contain refuses
149	  (`native.syntax-grammar-not-in-bundle`). The constant
150	  `resolutionAttempted=false` is carried so no consumer can read the universe
151	  as a resolution claim.
152	- **The body dialect axis.** `body-language-version.dialect` gains a third
153	  branch, `{grammarVariant}`. A syntax-only analysis has no compilation unit, so
154	  it has no edition to select and no program to join; claiming `{edition: 2021}`
155	  for a `.rs` body read without Cargo would fabricate compiler semantics. One
156	  suffix must map to one grammar
157	  (`native.syntax-grammar-suffix-ambiguous`), longest match wins, and a suffix
158	  with no bundled grammar refuses rather than being folded into a neighbour —
159	  which is what keeps `unsupported-file / no-bundled-grammar` an honest
160	  classification. Because it is a distinct branch, **a grammar-parsed body never
161	  mints the same identity as a compiler-parsed one over the same bytes.** That
162	  is required: a grammar parse and a compiler parse are different
163	  interpretations, and equating them would be a false clone claim.
164	- **Capability is not widened.** A `syntax-only` universe carries only the
165	  inventory rungs, the `syntactic` rungs and `clones@normalized-body-hash`.
166	  `imports`/`references`/`calls`/`types`/`reachability` remain
167	  `language-tier-unsupported` under it, `unresolved-edge` stays unavailable
168	  because no resolution was attempted, and a universal-negative predicate still
169	  requires its own complete `CoverageResultV3`. Nothing here lets a syntax-only
170	  Run claim a resolved or type fact.
171	- **The bundled grammar set is closed, and it has SEVEN languages.** The host
172	  bundles grammars for `rust`, `typescript`, `javascript`, `json`, `toml`,
173	  `markdown` and `yaml`; the shared discovery rule routes all fourteen of their
174	  suffixes to membership `syntax-only`, reason `grammar-only`. An earlier
175	  revision of this section let the grammar descriptor name only the three code
176	  languages and asserted equality with the `body-language-version` `languageId`
177	  enum as a drift check. That check proved the enum matched itself: it could not
178	  express the four data/document grammars the host has always shipped, so the
179	  promise directly above — *any* file whose extension maps to a bundled grammar —
180	  was unrepresentable for them. The descriptor now covers exactly the bundled
181	  set, and each row declares its **`syntaxClass`**.
182	
183	**`code` versus `data-document`: the distinction the contracts already draw.**
184	This is not a new narrowing; it is an existing law made machine-readable.
185	
186	- **`code`** — `rust`, `typescript`, `javascript`. §6.3 defines body spans as
187	  function, method, closure/lambda, `impl` item and block bodies, publishes the
188	  L2/L3 normalisation tables for exactly these languages, and puts
189	  `languageId ∈ {typescript, javascript, rust}` in the clone preimage. These
190	  grammars bear clone body identity and the code-construct syntax relations, and
191	  their `languageId` **must** be a member of the `body-language-version` enum.
192	- **`data-document`** — `json`, `toml`, `markdown`, `yaml`. These formats have no
193	  such body spans, and this kit publishes **no** tokenisation, `literalKind`
194	  mapping or normalisation law for them anywhere. Their files are grammar-only
195	  members — accounted, inventoried, and never `unsupported-file` — bearing
196	  `file`/`package`/`vcs-change` inventory evidence under the syntax universe.
197	  They mint **no** body identity, no suffix of theirs appears in the grammar
198	  dialect table, and their `languageId` **must not** be in the
199	  `body-language-version` enum, since it could never appear in a clone preimage.
200	
201	Both directions are enforced at grammar-bundle admission: a data grammar
202	claiming `code`, a code grammar demoted to `data-document`, and a row claiming a
203	suffix the discovery table routes to another language each refuse with their own
204	typed cause. What is held equal to the `body-language-version` enum is therefore
205	the **`code` subset**, not the whole bundle — which accounts for all seven
206	languages instead of ignoring four.
207	
208	Claiming `declares`/`literal`/`control-flow` facts for a data format would
209	require a tokenisation law this kit does not publish, and inventing one would be
210	precisely the fabricated-semantics failure the syntax-only universe exists to
211	prevent. If the product later wants data-format syntax facts, it needs a
212	published tokenisation and `literalKind` law first; that is a bounded future
213	capability and this matrix does not promise it today.
214	
215	An unbundled language stays unrepresentable: `.py` has no bundled grammar, is
216	not in the descriptor vocabulary, and its files remain `unsupported-file` with
217	reason `no-bundled-grammar`.
218	
219	**The capability law binds facts and Coverage, not just descriptors.** Validating
220	a grammar bundle's declared `syntaxClass` constrains what a bundle may say about
221	itself; it does not constrain what a Run may claim. An earlier revision enforced
222	the registry only there, and full Runs consequently admitted a Markdown-anchored
223	`declares` fact, a **complete** empty `declares`/`clones` Coverage over a
224	data-only repository, and `references@resolved-binding` under a universe whose
225	own record declares `resolutionAttempted: false`. The registry is therefore
226	consulted at the two boundaries that decide what a Run asserts, and at neither
227	does it consult the claimed coverage value, the caller-declared class, or
228	whether facts happen to exist:
229	
230	- **Every admitted fact.** A `fact2` under a syntax universe is admissible only
231	  if **every one of its anchor paths** is read by a **selected** grammar whose
232	  registry capability set contains that `relation@rung`. The anchor is the file
233	  the body was actually read from, so a Markdown-anchored code fact refuses in a
234	  mixed repository exactly as it does in a data-only one
235	  (`SYNTAX_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED_FACT`).
236	- **Every requested scope, including an empty view.** A `subject-scope` under a
237	  syntax universe is judged on its committed **examined extent** — the source
238	  inventory of the snapshot it names. **Inventory** capabilities
239	  (`file@enumerated`, `package@manifest-declared`, `vcs-change@vcs-reported`) are
240	  **always** available and are deliberately **not** grammar-gated: a snapshot
241	  inventories every file it contains, including ones no bundled grammar reads,
242	  and requiring a grammar per inventory row would silently narrow that promise.
243	  A **code** capability requires at least one path in that extent to be read by a
244	  selected `code` grammar. A capability no selected grammar bears is unavailable —
245	  which is every semantic rung and `unresolved-edge` under a syntax universe,
246	  exactly as the matrix already says.
247	
248	An **unselected** grammar lends no capability: selection is committed in the
249	universe identity, so a bundle that ships a Rust grammar the universe did not
250	select cannot make `declares@syntactic` available for `.rs` files.
251	
252	**An unavailable request is disclosed, not answered, and never refused outright.**
253	The capability is retained and representable: the scope closes a Run and carries
254	`coverage: unknown` with `deficiency: language-tier-unsupported` and
255	`nativeCause: capability-missing` — both already in the existing vocabulary, and
256	mapped in §10. A **false `complete`** for an unavailable capability, a wrong or
257	null cause, and a wrong deficiency each refuse with their own reason
258	(`SYNTAX_CAPABILITY_UNSUPPORTED_SCOPE`, `…_CAUSE_MISMATCH`,
259	`…_DEFICIENCY_MISMATCH`). No syntax Run is made blanket-indeterminate to achieve
260	this: a data-grammar inventory Run and a code-grammar `declares`/`clones` Run
261	both still close with a genuine `complete` and no deficiency.
262	
263	The guard is **syntax-universe specific**. Every capability of the TypeScript and
264	Rust universes is unchanged, including all five semantic relations, and the Rust
265	compilation-ownership guards are untouched — see the ownership disclosure law in
266	§10, whose prerequisite is now derived from the actual universe kind so that a
267	grammar-only clone scope, which has no compilation unit at all, owes no
268	compiler-ownership obligation.
269	
270	**A scope is judged on ITS OWN extent where the published law supplies one.** The
271	relation registry states, per relation, what `subject-scope.subjects` identify
272	(`subjectKindLaw`). For a **`source-path`** relation — `clones`, `file`,
273	`vcs-change`, which bind their subject to a snapshot path through their registry
274	`snapshotJoins` `pathField` or, for `clones`, through the single `bodyIdentityJoin`
275	anchor — the subjects **are** the extent, and **every** named path must be
276	supported. So a `README.md`-scoped clone request is unavailable even in a mixed
277	snapshot that also contains `src/plain.rs`: an unrelated code file elsewhere does
278	not serve it, and a scope naming both cannot hide its unsupported part behind its
279	supported one.
280	
281	For a **`symbol`** relation the subjects are opaque `SubjectIdV1` values that the
282	retained record associates with **no** path. The enumerator's attribution of
283	symbols to files is **trusted** and is not re-derivable from the retained Run, so
284	the only answerable question is the coarser one — can this universe produce this
285	capability anywhere in the committed extent — and that is what is asked. Treating
286	a symbol identifier as a path would reject lawful code scopes, and inventing
287	symbol-to-path parsing would be fabricated evidence. This is a stated
288	trust-boundary limit, not an oversight, and a mixed-repository empty `declares`
289	scope therefore remains admissible.
290	
291	**Path support is decided by the SELECTED grammar ROWS and their own suffixes**,
292	not by the set of selected languages. The descriptor permits a row to own a
293	**subset** of its language's bundled suffixes, and two rows of one language may
294	own disjoint suffixes; admission requires only that a claimed suffix belong to
295	that language and that no suffix be claimed twice. A selected TypeScript row
296	owning `.ts` therefore establishes nothing about a `.tsx` path when no selected
297	row owns `.tsx`, and longest match runs over the union of the selected rows' own
298	suffixes so `.d.ts` still resolves through a row owning `.ts`. An unanchored code
299	fact is **not** vacuously supported: it names no file that could have been read.
300	
301	**`allowJs` and `checkJs` are not completeness claims** (feedback 11; primary
302	sources `typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/allowJs` and `/checkJs`, read 2026-09-06).
303	`allowJs` is a *program-membership* option: it admits JavaScript roots. `checkJs`
304	is a *diagnostics* option: it reports errors in JavaScript files and changes
305	nothing about what is resolved. Both are universe keys (they change PlanId);
306	neither gates a capability, and neither implies that resolution was attempted or
307	complete. Resolution completeness is asserted only by `CoverageResultV3` (§4.3).
308	The universe carries `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `jsDiagnosticsEnabled` and the
309	constant `resolutionCompletenessImplied=false` so no consumer can confuse them.
310	
311	Module systems inside `typescript-v2` are observed, not chosen: `import`/`export`
312	and `require()`/`module.exports` are both resolved by the pinned compiler under
313	`module=node16` semantics keyed by `package.json` `type`. A non-literal specifier
314	is an unresolved edge (§4.4), never a silent drop.

342	- **L-JS2** dynamic forms: computed member access, non-literal `require`/`import()`, indirect `eval`, reflective access and `any`-typed calls produce unresolved edges; resolution completeness for universal negatives is then `incomplete` (§4).

351	### 1.4 Mixed repositories and workspace units (R1)
352	
353	The v1 rule ("deepest root, then `Cargo.toml` > `tsconfig.json`") was wrong: in a
354	repository whose root holds both `Cargo.toml` and `package.json`/`tsconfig.json`
355	every TypeScript file fell into the Rust unit and silently left the TypeScript
356	program. Units are now **per language family and program membership**, and may
357	share a root.
358	
359	**Reference discovery model** (`discover_units`, `assign_membership` in the model;
360	records `WorkspaceUnitV2`, `FileMembershipRowV1`, `UnitMembershipV1`). The root
361	discovery boundary and trust decision remain the security/foundation owners'
362	(DR-103); this contract defines what happens inside that boundary.
363	
364	`WorkspaceUnitV2` (closed): `{unitOrdinal, rootPath, languageFamily: rust|tsjs|none,
365	languageMode, unitKind: cargo-workspace|cargo-package|ts-program|js-program|syntax-only,
366	markerPath, markerSha256, recognizerId, recognizerVersion, provenance:
367	EXPLICIT|DISCOVERED|DEFAULTED, memberPackageRoots[]}`.
368	
369	- **U-1 (one unit per directory and language family)** A directory holding
370	  `Cargo.toml` yields a `rust` unit; a directory holding `tsconfig.json`,
371	  `jsconfig.json` or `package.json` yields exactly one `tsjs` unit whose mode is
372	  chosen by precedence `tsconfig.json` (→ `ts-tsconfig`/`js-allowjs`) >
373	  `jsconfig.json` (→ `js-allowjs`) > `package.json` (→ `js-synthesized`). The
374	  precedence selects the mode **within** `tsjs`; it never removes the co-located
375	  `rust` unit. A root with both markers has two units with the same `rootPath`
376	  (`units-colocated-cargo-and-package-json-root-keeps-both-languages`).
377	- **U-2 (Cargo workspace folding)** A `Cargo.toml` package inside a Cargo
378	  workspace root's tree is folded into the workspace unit as a member package
379	  (Cargo resolves the workspace as one program); it is listed in
380	  `memberPackageRoots`, not as a separate unit. A standalone package outside any
381	  workspace is its own `cargo-package` unit. **Explicit roots are unit
382	  selection, never loss of Cargo workspace semantics (post-reset v2 A-3/P22):**
383	  naming a Cargo workspace root explicitly yields exactly the automatic result
384	  for that unit (members folded, member `target` output pruned, a member's
385	  `src/target` still source); naming a member package alone selects that package
386	  as its own `cargo-package` unit, and files of the unselected root or siblings
387	  are honest `no-program-unit-for-language` rows, neither claimed nor
388	  over-ignored (`units-explicit-cargo-workspace-root-keeps-member-folding-and-member-target-pruning`).
389	- **U-3 (deterministic membership within a language)** A file's family is fixed
390	  by extension (`.rs` → `rust`; `.ts/.tsx/.mts/.cts/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.jsx` → `tsjs`).
391	  It belongs to the **deepest unit of its own family** whose root prefixes its
392	  path. Units of another family never claim it. Nested monorepo packages
393	  (`packages/web/tsconfig.json` under a root `tsconfig.json`) are therefore
394	  distinct `tsjs` units and the deeper one wins for its subtree
395	  (`units-nested-monorepo-deepest-within-language-and-workspace-folding`).
396	- **U-4 (no source erasure; honest unsupported files)** Every snapshot inventory
397	  file appears in exactly one `FileMembershipRowV1`: `program-member`;
398	  `syntax-only` with reason `no-program-unit-for-language` (a `.rs` file with no
399	  enclosing Rust unit: semantic rungs `unknown`, cause `no-program-unit`),
400	  `grammar-only` (bundled grammar, no program) or `host-ignore-convention`
401	  (the file lies inside a pruned tree of the shared rule below); or
402	  `unsupported-file` with reason `no-bundled-grammar`, listed in
403	  `unsupportedFiles`. `erasedFiles` is a schema-constant empty array
404	  (`maxItems 0`) and the model refuses a membership that does not cover the
405	  inventory exactly once.
406	- **U-4a (one shared discovery rule; post-reset MUST-3)** The host ignore
407	  conventions and unit enumeration are stated once, in
408	  `docs/coop/design-corrections/discovery-defaults.py`, and consumed by both
409	  `discover_units`/`assign_membership`/`unit_scope_descriptor`/`typescript_mode`
410	  here and by the security discovery instrument (security S3). Pruned trees,
411	  by **exact path segment** (never substring): dependency trees (`node_modules`),
412	  VCS trees (`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.jj`) and Cargo build output (a `target`
413	  segment whose parent directory holds `Cargo.toml`, an actual Cargo root known
414	  from the units: workspace root or folded member package). `packages/target/index.ts`
415	  and `src/target/x.ts` are ordinary program members; `target/debug/x.rs` under
416	  a root `Cargo.toml` is `host-ignore-convention`. A marker inside a pruned tree
417	  (every `node_modules/<pkg>/package.json`, a `Cargo.toml` under `node_modules`)
418	  is never a unit and never a Cargo root; each pruned tree is reported once in
419	  `UnitDiscoveryV1.prunedTrees` (`PrunedTreeV1 {path, reason, markerCount}`) and
420	  its anchor enters `excludedPathPrefixes`. Pruning is a discovery rule, not a

547	## 2. Semantic universe successors
548	
549	Every array in the current native schema bundle declares `x-opensip-order`
550	under identity §3. `sequence` preserves order and repeated items unless a separate
551	uniqueness constraint applies. It is intentional for compiler flags, signature
552	tokens, substitution precedence and ordered observations. Stricter orders are
553	machine-checked at schema admission: declaration components by `component`,
554	dependency packages by `(name, version, sourceId)`, owner records by `ownerKey`,
555	file-manifest rows by `path`, and the explicitly sorted path/name/enum collections
556	by raw UTF-8 bytes. These keys must be unique; a second row with the same key and
557	different payload also refuses. The canonical encoder never sorts a collection.
558	Input-adapter observation sequences retain their own declared order; a producer
559	must construct any stricter output collection before admitting it.
560

560	
561	### 2.1 `rust-v2` (replaces `rust-v1.resolvedInputs`)
562	
563	All `rust-v1` release/toolchain identity fields are retained unchanged.
564	`resolvedInputs` becomes `RustUniverseV2ResolvedInputs`:
565	
566	| Field | Type | Rule |
567	|---|---|---|
568	| `schemaVersion` | `2` | exact integer |
569	| `edition` | per-package map `{packageKey: 2015\|2018\|2021\|2024}` | keys sorted; every workspace member present |
570	| `lockfileIdentity` | `{path:"Cargo.lock", contentSha256, lockfileVersion∈{3,4}}` | absence is `input-closure-incomplete` (`lockfile-missing`), never an implicit `cargo generate-lockfile` |
571	| `dependencySourceSetId` | `Sha256Text` | identity of the admitted `DependencySourceSetV1` (§3) |
572	| `unifiedFeaturesId` | `Sha256Text` | identity of `UnifiedFeaturesV1` (§3.4) |
573	| `nativeContextId` | `Sha256Text` | identity of `NativeContextV2` (§2.3) |
574	| `cfgSets` | array of `{cfgSetId, cfg}` length 1..4 | default `[primary, primary+test]`; extra sets are Plan-bound. Every set's `cfg` **contains every member of the context's `baseCfg`**: sets differ from the base only by additions, and `cfgSetId` is unique within the universe. A set that dropped a base cfg would analyse a configuration nothing selected |
575	| `rustflags` | `RustflagsProjectionV1` | the *honored* and *stripped* flag lists after the exact allowlist (§3.3); equal to the bound context's `configProjection.rustflags` |
576	| `crateRootPaths` | sorted unique canonical paths | unchanged; every path must be in the analysed snapshot inventory |
577	| `configProjectionSha256` | `DigestHex` | the 64-hex suffix of `H("native.cargo-config-projection.v2", CargoConfigProjectionV2)` over the bound context's `configProjection` (§3.3). It is **not** the raw SHA-256 of the canonical projection bytes, and **not** `CargoConfigProjectionV2.projectionSha256`, which is the raw digest of the projected config *file*. Raw file digests are also in the snapshot |
578	| `preparedResolution` | `none \| host-prepared \| imported-inert` | how prepared products entered the universe (R4) |
579	| `executionCapableResolution` | boolean | `preparedResolution ≠ none`. It names the **meaning** of the universe (resolution consumed inert products of some execution). It is **never** a host execution grant: the grant is the operational `RepoExecutionGrantV2` reference outside Plan (§5.1). `imported-inert` needs only `read-import` in the semantic grant; only `host-prepared` projects `prepare-code` |
580	| `preparedOutputSetId` | `Sha256Text \| null` | identity of the admitted `PreparedOutputSetV3`; `null` when `preparedResolution=none` |
581	
582	Change rule: any field change changes PlanId. Missing, unknown, float-spelled,
583	unordered or handshake-mismatched values fail before provider execution.
584	
585	**Binding a `rust-v2` universe (`bind_rust_universe`).** A universe is bound to its
586	admitted context before PlanId, exactly as `typescript-v2` is bound by
587	`bind_typescript_universe` (§2.4), and for the same reason: an identity commits to
588	the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them. The binding is pure — it
589	executes no cargo, rustc, build script, proc macro or filesystem read — and takes
590	the admitted context descriptor, the retained nested input records
591	(`DependencySourceSetV1`, `UnifiedFeaturesV1`, `PreparedOutputSetV3` when one is
592	selected) and the analysed snapshot inventory. All three are **required**: there is
593	no context-free or input-free admit path, because an optional join is not a rule,
594	and omission is the typed refusal `native.universe-retained-inputs-not-supplied`,
595	never an ADMIT. It refuses when
596	
597	- the admission is not a Rust context admission, or the universe names a context
598	  this host did not mint, or the supplied context bytes are not the admitted ones;
599	- any overlapping field disagrees:
600	  `dependencySourceSetId`, `unifiedFeaturesId`, `preparedOutputSetId`, `rustflags`,
601	  `configProjectionSha256`, `executionCapableResolution`, `preparedResolution`, or a
602	  `cfgSets` entry that drops a base cfg or repeats a `cfgSetId`;
603	- a nested semantic identity is not the exact H identity of the retained record of
604	  its registered domain, or that record contradicts the universe or context —
605	  a dependency set whose `lockfileIdentity` differs, unified features computed for
606	  another `targetTriple` or resolver version, or a prepared set bound to another
607	  dependency set, toolchain, cfg set or preparation kind;
608	- a prepared output set is retained but **no** universe selected it
609	  (`preparedOutputSetId = null`): optional absent preparation stays absent, and
610	  bytes in custody never enter a resolution by being in custody;
611	- the snapshot does not contain what the universe names: `Cargo.lock` missing or
612	  with different bytes, a `crateRootPaths` entry not inventoried, or a
613	  `replacedSnapshotConfigs` entry not inventoried.
614	
615	`executionCapableResolution` remains a statement about what the resolution
616	consumed, never an execution grant; retained inert prepared bytes cannot imply one,
617	and the operational `RepoExecutionGrantV2` reference stays outside Plan (§5.1).

621	Retained **in the universe**: `tsconfigGraphHash`, `programRootFiles`,

623	execution is selected).

625	**Relocated to the context** (§2.4), and therefore *not* fields of the closed

658	§2.4's agreement check needs; without the record the `tsconfig`/`jsconfig`

704	### 2.3 `NativeContextV2` (Rust)
705	
706	**There is exactly one native-context record and one `H` domain per language.**
707	`NativeContextV2` is the **Rust** context; `TypeScriptNativeContextV2` (§2.4) is the
708	TypeScript one. Neither is a general "native context": a universe binds the record of its
709	own language and refuses the other.
710	
711	Descriptor (domain `native.context.rust.v2`): `{schemaVersion:2, targetTriple,
712	hostTriple, toolchain: ToolchainIdentityV1, toolClosure: ToolClosureV1, baseCfg,
713	resolverVersion, dependencySourceSetId, unifiedFeaturesId, preparedOutputSetId|null,
714	configProjection: CargoConfigProjectionV2}`.
715	
716	`rustcDevLlvmDigest` is at **`NativeContextV2.toolchain.rustcDevLlvmDigest`**, inside
717	`ToolchainIdentityV1` — not a top-level field of the context (a citation that says only "in
718	native-context schema 2" is reachable but under-specified). Its value is the 64-hex suffix
719	of the `closure2` identity of the admitted `kind=rust-dev-llvm` closure, so `"closure2:" +`
720	the field must name a retained closure of that kind whose recomputed identity equals it;
721	`admit_native_context('rust', …)` performs exactly that join against the retained closure
722	descriptor and tree.
723	
724	`ToolClosureV1` = `{rustc, cargo, linker|null, ar|null, procMacroServer, closureId}`
725	— the raw digests of every executable the adapter may select, all members of the
726	signed `closure2` named by `closureId`. **Every tool that runs is in this
727	closure**: `rustc`, `cargo`, the linker rustc spawns when a build script or
728	proc-macro crate is linked, `ar`, and the proc-macro server. No `PATH` lookup, no
729	system `cc`, no `RUSTC`/`CARGO`/`RUSTUP_*`/`CARGO_HOME` from the environment. If a
730	platform family has no bundled linker in the closure, in-host preparation is
731	`UNSUPPORTED-TYPED` there (`native.execution-not-authorized`, cause
732	`linker-unavailable`); it never falls back to a system linker.
733	
734	The host resolved-inputs adapter computes the context before PlanId; the worker
735	recomputes it after sealed inputs are received and refuses with
736	`Unavailable(native-context-mismatch)` before Analyze if any byte differs (§9.5).
737	
738	### 2.4 `TypeScriptNativeContextV2` (TypeScript/JavaScript)
739	
740	Descriptor (domain `native.context.typescript.v2`): `{schemaVersion:2, languageMode,
741	toolchain: TypeScriptToolchainIdentityV1, toolClosure: TypeScriptToolClosureV1,
742	configProjection: TypeScriptConfigProjectionV2, moduleResolutionMode, packageModuleType,
743	nodeModulesLayoutDigest|null, lockfileIdentity|null}`.
744	
745	`TypeScriptToolchainIdentityV1` = `{compilerName:"typescript", compilerVersion,
746	compilerPackageDigest, typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot, standardLibraryComponentDigests[],
747	libSelection[]}`. `TypeScriptToolClosureV1` = `{compiler, runtime, closureId}`.
748	
749	**Exact field locations and producing recipe.** Every value is computed by the host
750	resolved-inputs adapter before PlanId from **admitted, retained** bytes; none is read from a
751	worker claim, a `tsc --version` string or the environment.
752	
753	| Field | Produced from |
754	|---|---|
755	| `toolchain.compilerVersion` | the `semanticVersion` of the **admitted signed compiler closure manifest** named by `toolClosure.closureId`; admission refuses when the two differ, so a version string and the bytes it labels cannot drift apart |
756	| `toolchain.compilerPackageDigest` | a member digest of that retained `kind=toolchain` closure tree |
757	| `toolchain.typescriptStdlibMerkleRoot` | identity §3's existing recipe: the **64-hex suffix** of the `closure2` identity of the admitted `kind=stdlib` closure. `"closure2:" +` the value must name a retained closure of that kind whose recomputed identity equals it |
758	| `toolchain.standardLibraryComponentDigests` | the **complete** declaration-file inventory of that retained stdlib tree — one row per `.d.ts` member, selected or not, `component` = the member basename, sorted by `component`. A missing row refuses `native.native-context-stdlib-inventory-incomplete:<name>`, because an alternate partial declaration inventory for the same retained library is not the required complete record. A tree in which two paths share a basename refuses `native.native-context-stdlib-tree-ambiguous-basename:<name>` rather than resolving the join arbitrarily |
759	| `toolchain.libSelection` | the effective `lib` names the resolved `compilerOptions` select after `target` defaulting, sorted; each must be covered by a retained component |
760	| `toolClosure.compiler`, `toolClosure.runtime` | raw digests of the bundled compiler and of the bundled JavaScript runtime that executes it, both members of the signed closure named by `closureId`. No `PATH` lookup, no system `node`, no `NODE_OPTIONS`/`NODE_PATH`/`TS_NODE_*` from the environment |
761	| `configProjection.honoredOptions` | the closed subset of the **effective** resolved `compilerOptions` (or of `SynthesizedCompilerOptionsV1` under `js-synthesized`) that changes program membership, module resolution or checking |
762	| `configProjection.strippedOptions` | every option removed, with a typed reason (`selects-an-executable`, `emits-output`, `reads-the-environment`, `acquires-types-from-the-network`, `not-a-resolution-or-membership-option`). Stripping is disclosed here and is never a reason to read the option from anywhere else. `typeAcquisitionEnabled` and `executableSelected` are schema constants `false` |
763	| `configProjection.configGraphPaths` | every `tsconfig`/`jsconfig` file of the resolved `extends` graph, in the snapshot, sorted by logical path; empty under `configOrigin=synthesized` |
764	| `nodeModulesLayoutDigest` | raw SHA-256 of `C(ResolvedNodeModulesLayoutV1)` — the retained resolution read-set layout — or `null` exactly when `nodeModulesInReadSet=false` |
765	| `lockfileIdentity` | `{kind, path, contentSha256}` of the admitted lockfile, or `null` when `lockfileKind=none` |
766	
767	**Retained trees.** The stdlib closure and the compiler closure are retained **whole** —
768	complete foundation `closure` descriptor and complete file tree — and joined to the selected
769	compiler. `admit_native_context` recomputes each closure identity from its retained record
770	and refuses `native.native-context-closure-unretained`,
771	`native.native-context-closure-identity-mismatch` or
772	`native.native-context-closure-kind-mismatch` before any digest comparison. The stdlib merkle
773	root is therefore never a bare number a caller can assert.
774	
775	**No platform *field*, and the identity is still platform-specific.** Unlike the Rust context there
776	is no `targetTriple`/`hostTriple`, because TypeScript *resolution semantics* — which specifiers
777	resolve, which subjects are examined, what is checked — are platform-invariant by design (§1.1).
778	That is a design selection of this contract, not a measurement, and it is **not** a claim that the
779	identity is platform-invariant: `toolClosure.closureId` names a signed closure whose foundation
780	`closure` descriptor includes `platform`, so the same source analysed with the platform-specific
781	executables of two families mints two `nativeContextId`s — as it must, because different bytes ran
782	(`typescript-context-identity-is-platform-specific-through-its-signed-tool-closure`).
783	
784	**Universe and Plan binding.** `typescript-v2.nativeContextId` is
785	`H("native.context.typescript.v2", descriptor)` in the `Sha256Text` form. `PlanId` binds the
786	same digest through `plan.nativeContextDigests`, which takes the **bare 64 hex** (§11, the
787	foundation `plan` record's spelling) and is a canonical **set**: several units of one language
788	legitimately share one context, and identical admitted contexts collapse to one member — that is
789	deduplication of an identical descriptor, never of two different ones.
790	
791	`bind_typescript_universe(universe, admission, context)` refuses a universe whose `nativeContextId`
792	this host did not mint (`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch`) and refuses a Rust-minted context
793	outright (`native.native-context-language-mismatch`). The **retained context bytes are a required
794	argument**: there is no context-free admit path, because an optional field-agreement check is not a
795	rule — a caller that omitted it would obtain exactly the bypass this join exists to close. Omission
796	is the typed refusal `native.universe-context-not-supplied`
797	(`typescript-universe-bound-without-the-retained-context-refuses`); context bytes that do not hash to
798	the admitted id refuse
799	`native.universe-context-binding-mismatch:context-bytes-are-not-the-admitted-ones`.
800	
801	Given those bytes the two records must **agree where they overlap**: a matching `nativeContextId`
802	commits to the context bytes, not to the universe's copy of them, so `languageMode`,
803	`packageModuleType`, `allowJs`, `checkJs`, `lockfileKind`, `nodeModulesInReadSet`,
804	`jsDiagnosticsEnabled`, `jsAdmittedToProgram`, `configOrigin`, the `extends`-graph emptiness and the
805	synthesized-options presence are each checked against the context and refuse
806	`native.universe-context-field-mismatch:<field>`.
807	
808	The context itself also has mandatory agreement rules. `moduleResolutionMode`
809	equals `configProjection.honoredOptions.moduleResolution`. `libSelection` is
810	strictly sorted by UTF-8 name bytes, contains no case-insensitive duplicate names,
811	and selects the same case-insensitive name set as the honored `lib` list;
812	each record retains its specified order for hashing. The closed resolved context
813	always materializes that nonempty list. When source configuration omits `lib`,
814	the resolver supplies the pinned compiler's target-default library selection
815	in both records; `null` is not an alternate resolved spelling.
816	`standardLibraryComponentDigests`
817	has strictly unique component keys in UTF-8 order. Context admission refuses any
818	contradiction before its digest may enter Plan. In synthesized mode every value
819	in `synthesizedOptions` equals the corresponding honored option, and an absent
820	optional `jsx` means honored `jsx` is null. Presence alone is insufficient.
821	These are semantic agreement checks in addition to closed schema validation;
822	internal diagnostic suffixes remain operational refusal evidence, not new public
823	DomainDetail codes.
824	
825	**Independent derivation (§9.5) applies to TypeScript exactly as to Rust.** The worker
826	recomputes the context from its own sealed inputs; a differing byte is
827	`Unavailable(native-context-mismatch)` before Analyze.

854	
855	### 3.1 `DependencySourceSetV1`
856	
857	Identity domain `native.dependency-source-set.v1`. Closed descriptor:
858	`{schemaVersion:1, language:"rust", lockfileIdentity, packages:
859	[DependencyPackageSourceV1…] sorted by (name, version, sourceId) UTF-8 bytes,
860	completeness:{state, missing[]}}`.
861	
862	`DependencyPackageSourceV1`:
863	
864	| Field | Rule |
865	|---|---|
866	| `name`, `version` | exact `[[package]]` values from `Cargo.lock` |
867	| `sourceKind` | `registry \| git \| path \| vendored` |
868	| `sourceId` | exact `source` string from `Cargo.lock`, or `""` for path packages |
869	| `lockChecksum` | 64-hex from the lock `checksum`, or `null` for git/path |
870	| `fileManifestSha256` | H(`native.dependency-file-manifest.v1`, sorted `[{path, contentSha256, byteLength}]`) |
871	| `fileCount`, `totalBytes` | exact uint64 |
872	| `acquisition` | `{mode: in-snapshot-path \| in-snapshot-vendored \| imported-descriptor, descriptorId: ImportId\|null, vendorPath\|null}` |
873	| `checksumVerification` | `tarball-matched \| self-consistent \| not-applicable \| mismatch` — `mismatch` refuses the whole set |
874	| `provenanceAssurance` | `registry-authenticated \| declared` |
875	
876	Verification rules (feedback 3 corrected):
877	
878	- **DS-1 (registry, vendored tree)** A vendored directory carries a self-asserted
879	  `.cargo-checksum.json`. Its `package` field equalling `lockChecksum` proves
880	  nothing about the files: an attacker rewrites file contents and every `files`
881	  entry while preserving `package`. The host therefore checks internal
882	  consistency only (`package == lockChecksum`, every listed file's SHA-256
883	  matches, no extra or missing files) and records `checksumVerification =
884	  self-consistent`, `provenanceAssurance = declared`. Inconsistency is `mismatch`
885	  and refuses the set. The reference model contains the mutation
886	  (`ds1-mutation-preserving-package-checksum-stays-declared`): the mutated tree is
887	  still admitted, and it is still *declared*, never authenticated.
888	- **DS-2 (registry, tarball)** Only the exact `.crate` tarball whose SHA-256
889	  equals `lockChecksum` yields `tarball-matched` / `registry-authenticated`. The
890	  host extracts it deterministically into the CAS and computes the file manifest
891	  itself. An extracted tree plus `.cargo-checksum.json` is DS-1.
892	- **DS-3 (git)** The import supplies the checked-out tree for the exact `#rev`;
893	  `not-applicable` / `declared`; the file manifest identity is the binding.
894	- **DS-4 (path)** Path dependencies live in the snapshot; nothing is imported.
895	- **DS-5 (no ambient reads)** `$CARGO_HOME/registry`, `~/.cargo`, `vendor/`
896	  outside the snapshot, or any host path is read **only** as the explicit,
897	  user-named source path of an import step (§7). Any acquisition mode outside the
898	  closed set, or any fetch URL, refuses. No network fetch exists in any first-party
899	  code path (design invariant, conformance-checked; not a confinement claim).
900	- **DS-6 (completeness)** The set is complete for a target when every package
901	  activated by `UnifiedFeaturesV1` is present with `checksumVerification ≠
902	  mismatch`. An incomplete set is admitted with `completeness.incomplete` and
903	  typed `input-closure-incomplete` Coverage for dependent crates; it never blocks
904	  syntax analysis.
905	
906	`declared` provenance is disclosed wherever the package matters: in the Plan
907	(through the set descriptor), in `AuthorizedExecutionV2.owners[].provenanceAssurance`,
908	and in the pre-execution sentence (§5.2). Facts derived from declared sources are
909	still Plan-bound Coverage inputs; the disclosure is what changes.

913	The host stores admitted dependency sources in its content-addressed store keyed

921	### 3.3 Cargo configuration: verified carrier, exact flags (feedback 5, 10)
922	
923	Primary source (`doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html`, read 2026-09-06):
924	Cargo reads `.cargo/config.toml` (and legacy `.cargo/config`) from the current
925	directory and **every ancestor**, plus `$CARGO_HOME/config.toml`, merging arrays;
926	it also honors `CARGO_*` environment overrides and knobs that select executables
927	(`build.rustc`, `build.rustc-wrapper`, `target.*.linker`, `target.*.runner`),
928	credentials and network. Stock Cargo has no switch that disables ancestor
929	discovery, and this contract does not claim `--config` replaces the stack.
930	
931	The first-party `opensip-cargo-adapter` therefore establishes a **verified
932	ancestor carrier** (`CargoConfigProjectionV2`, all checked by
933	`cargo_config_admission` in the model):
934	
935	- **CC-1** Before every Cargo invocation, every ancestor directory of the private
936	  scratch root is checked for `.cargo/config.toml` and `.cargo/config`. Presence
937	  is a refusal (`native.ambient-cargo-config`, exit 4), never a merge and never a
938	  silent skip. `ancestorCarrierVerified=true` is recorded in the context.
939	- **CC-2** `CARGO_HOME` is a fresh private empty directory created for the
940	  invocation; its `config.toml` is absent by construction.
941	- **CC-3** The constructed environment contains no `PATH`, `CARGO_*`, `RUSTFLAGS`,
942	  `RUSTC*`, `RUSTDOC*`, `RUSTUP_*`, `CC`/`CXX`/`LD`/`AR`/`TARGET_*` variables;
943	  presence of any is a refusal. Tool locations are passed as absolute closure
944	  paths on the command line, not via environment.
945	- **CC-4** Every selected tool digest equals its entry in `ToolClosureV1`.
946	- **CC-5** Every `.cargo/config(.toml)` inside the snapshot (any directory, not
947	  only the root) is replaced in the materialization by the single projected file;
948	  the originals remain snapshot bytes for identity but are never read by Cargo.
949	
950	Projected (honored) keys: `build.target`, `build.rustflags`,
951	`target.<triple>.rustflags` (both through the flag allowlist below),
952	`source.<name>.directory` pointing inside the snapshot with `replace-with`,
953	`resolver`, and `[patch]` in `Cargo.toml`. Stripped and recorded: `alias`,
954	`build.rustc`, `build.rustc-wrapper`, `build.rustc-workspace-wrapper`,
955	`build.rustdoc`, `build.target-dir`, `build.build-dir`, `build.incremental`,
956	`build.dep-info-basedir`, `cargo-new`, `credential-alias`, `doc`, `env`,
957	`future-incompat-report`, `http`, `install`, `net`, `patch` (config-level),
958	`profile`, `registries`, `registry`, `target.*.linker`, `target.*.runner`,
959	`target.*.<links>`, `term`, `unstable`. A `[source]` replacement pointing outside
960	the snapshot is `input-closure-incomplete` (`source-replacement-outside-snapshot`).
961	
962	**Two distinct digests, both now named.** `CargoConfigProjectionV2.projectionSha256`
963	is the raw SHA-256 of the exact bytes of the **single projected `.cargo/config.toml`
964	file** the adapter materializes under CC-5 — a raw artifact digest of a file.
965	`rust-v2.configProjectionSha256` (§2.1) is the 64-hex suffix of
966	`H("native.cargo-config-projection.v2", CargoConfigProjectionV2)` over the whole
967	projection record. Neither is the raw SHA-256 of the canonical projection bytes, and
968	neither substitutes for the other. Every `replacedSnapshotConfigs` entry names a
969	path that must be in the analysed snapshot inventory: the originals remain snapshot
970	bytes for identity even though Cargo never reads them.
971	
972	**Rustflags allowlist** (`RustflagsProjectionV1`; primary source
973	`doc.rust-lang.org/rustc/command-line-arguments.html`, read 2026-09-06). Honored,
974	exactly:

976	| Flag | Constraint |
977	|---|---|
978	| `--cfg <ident>` / `--cfg <ident>="<value>"` / `--cfg=<…>` | identifier syntax; no spaces |
979	| `-A/-W/-D/-F <lint>`, `-A<lint>`… and long forms; `--cap-lints <allow\|warn\|deny\|forbid>` | lint name syntax `[a-z0-9_:]+` |

1013	`{schemaVersion:3, preparation: {kind: authorized-execution|imported-descriptor,
1014	authorizationId|null, importId|null, toolchain, dependencySourceSetId, cfgSetId,

1023	  trust proof)** Admissible row kinds are exactly three:
1024	  `build-script-directives` (`text/x-cargo-directives`: the captured `cargo:`
1025	  lines, including `rustc-cfg`/`rustc-env` consumed by `cfg`/`env!`),
1026	  `macro-expansion` (`text/x-rust-expansion`: the fully expanded token text for one
1027	  invocation `site` = `{path, startByte, endByte, inputTokenDigest}`), and
1028	  `generated-file` (`generated = {logicalPath, blob}` with media type
1029	  `text/x-rust-source`, `text/plain` or `application/octet-stream`: one data file
1030	  a build script wrote under `OUT_DIR`). Row kinds `proc-macro-dylib` and

1036	  **No prepared artifact is ever loaded, linked or executed by the semantic
1037	  worker.** Expansions are looked up by exact
1038	  `(path, span, inputTokenDigest, macro crate manifest)`; a miss is a
1039	  `macro-expansion-unavailable` edge (L-RS4).

1044	  `include_str!`/`include_bytes!`) reads the `generated-file` row bound to

1053	  prefix, no `.`/`..` segment, no NUL or backslash, ≤ 1024 bytes; an escaping path
1054	  fails exact typed admission and the worker lookup independently refuses it with

1056	  `maxGeneratedFileBytes 67108864`, `maxGeneratedTotalBytes 1073741824`,
1057	  `maxGeneratedFileRows 1000000` (protocol limit). Imported blobs are bound to

1064	  was selected explicitly, or is ignored with a disclosed `staleRows` list and

1084	
1085	### 4.1 Two different completeness claims
1086

1088

1085	### 4.1 Two different completeness claims
1086	
1087	A Coverage entry commits two things that were previously conflated:
1088	
1089	1. **Examined universe** — the exhaustive examined subject/target partition
1090	   (`subjectScopeCommitment`, retained). "Did we look at every subject?"
1091	2. **Resolution completeness** — whether every reference/import/call edge
1092	   originating in the examined subjects was resolved to a binding at the requested
1093	   rung, *after resolution was actually attempted over the whole partition*.
1094	   "Could we see every consumer?"
1095	
1096	### 4.1a Producing recipe for `subjectScopeCommitment` (closed)
1097	
1098	The retained C-2 selector deferred computation and verification. This is the successor
1099	recipe; nothing about the historical artifact changes.
1100	
1101	**Recipe.** `subjectScopeCommitment` is the foundation **subject-scope** identity of the
1102	examined partition, re-spelled in the native `Sha256Text` text form:
1103	
1104	```
1105	scope2      = identity-and-evidence H("subject-scope", D)          -> "scope2:"  + hex
1106	commitment  = "sha256:" + the same 64 hex                          -> Sha256Text
1107	```
1108	
1109	where `D` is the closed foundation record
1110	`identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/subject-scope`
1111	`{schemaVersion: 2, snapshotId, sourceUniverse, targetUniverse, relation, resolution,
1112	enumeratorClosure, subjects}`.
1113	
1114	**Inputs, exactly, and where each comes from.** `snapshotId` is the admitted `snapshot2`.
1115	`relation`/`resolution` are the Coverage key's own relation and rung. `sourceUniverse` and
1116	`targetUniverse` are the bare 64-hex universe digests of the same key (§2, §11).
1117	`enumeratorClosure` is the `closure2` of the Plan-bound enumerator that produced the
1118	partition. `subjects` is the **complete** examined subject inventory that enumerator
1119	enumerated over that snapshot, a canonical set (foundation ordering, duplicates refuse
1120	rather than dedupe). **Encoding**: the foundation canonical encoder and `H` frame, imported,
1121	not restated. There is **no native `H` domain for this field**: one preimage, one digest,
1122	two admitted textual spellings (§11).
1123	
1124	**Join with `scope2`.** The commitment is the *identical* digest to the `scope2` the host
1125	binds into the `coverage2` descriptor (`coverage.scopeId`). It is therefore not a second
1126	commitment and cannot drift from the scope it names. Its purpose is that the Coverage
1127	*payload* — the bytes whose `payloadDigest` mints `coverage2` — carries the provider's
1128	in-band commitment to the partition it claims to have examined, which the host then checks
1129	against a value the provider never supplied.
1130	
1131	**Where it is produced and checked (`admit_coverage_result_v3`, the admitted native producer
1132	boundary).** For every `CoverageResultV3` a provider sends, before any `coverage2` exists:
1133	
1134	1. The host builds `D` from **its own** enumeration and mints `scope2`. A provider-supplied
1135	   commitment is never an input to this step.
1136	2. `key.relation`, `key.resolution`, `key.sourceUniverse`, `key.targetUniverse` must equal
1137	   `D`'s (`native.coverage-key-scope-mismatch:<field>`).
1138	3. `key.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the computed commitment
1139	   (`native.subject-scope-commitment-mismatch`).
1140	4. `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectScopeCommitment` must equal the key's
1141	   (`native.examined-universe-commitment-mismatch`) and
1142	   `entry.examinedUniverse.subjectCount` must equal `len(D.subjects)`
1143	   (`native.examined-universe-subject-count-mismatch`). A provider that examined a narrower
1144	   partition than the host enumerated is detected here, and by nothing else.
1145	5. RC-2 (§4.3) is rechecked over the same partition.
1146	6. Only then is `coverage2` minted from `{schemaVersion: 2, scopeId, payloadSchemaDigest,
1147	   payloadDigest}`. `payloadSchemaDigest` is the raw SHA-256 of the **exact registered schema

1327	### 4.6 Sufficiency v2 (replaces `$.sufficiency`)
1328	
1329	Evaluated in this order; every applicable cause is collected and the most specific
1330	by §10 precedence is reported. `satisfied=true` may carry `disclosures`.
1331	
1332	1. Relation absent from the view → `required-relation-missing`.
1333	2. Rung below `minResolution` → the rung-unavailable cause (`language-tier-unsupported`, `provider-unavailable`, `input-closure-incomplete`, `budget-exhausted`) else `required-relation-missing`.

1350	### 4.7 Positive coverage case (`positive-static-consumer`)
1351	
1352	Module A exports `foo` and `bar`; module B does `import {foo} from './a'; foo();`
1353	No computed access, no dynamic import, `package.json private:true` without
1354	published entries, explicit entry points, no external consumers declared.
1355	Provider emits `references@resolved-binding` for `foo`, zero `unresolved-edge`
1356	facts, the stage completes, `resolutionCompleteness.complete`,
1357	`exportsClosed=closed`. Then "no consumer of `foo`" → satisfied=false by evidence;
1358	"no consumer of `bar`" under `universal-negative/forbid/forbid` → satisfied=true
1359	with no deficiency. That is the only shape under which an authoritative
1360	no-consumer claim is eligible. No provider verdict exists.

1362	### 4.8 Type derivation provenance (feedback 12)
1363	
1364	The v1 draft capped JSDoc-free JavaScript type facts at `confidenceMillionths ≤
1365	900000`. That number had no evidence rationale: a compiler-inferred type is exact
1366	under the admitted universe, and JSDoc presence is not a calibrated probability.
1367	Replacement: every `types@checked` fact carries `TypeDerivationV1` =
1368	`{derivationKind: annotated|jsdoc-declared|compiler-inferred, confidenceMillionths:
1369	1000000, confidenceMethod: "native.confidence.v1", checkJs, limitations}`.
1370	`native.confidence.v1` is the versioned, conformance-bound method
1371	"declared-exact: every admitted checked fact is 1000000 under its universe; no
1372	value below 1000000 is produced by a native provider". Rule authors express
1373	"declared types only" through `derivationPolicy=declared-only` (§4.2), which
1374	yields the typed `derivation-policy-unmet` deficiency, not a fake percentage.
1375	`checkJs` is recorded because it changes diagnostics, not derivation.

1380	
1381	### 5.1 Principal class `repository-code` and its joins (R4)
1382	
1383	The security contract S10 registers principal class `repository-code`
1384	(`RepoExecutionGrantV2`, execution classes `build-script | proc-macro |
1385	test-runner`). One principal, three current spellings, joined explicitly and
1386	checked by schema constants:
1387	
1388	| Where | Spelling | Role |
1389	|---|---|---|
1390	| security S10 / `AuthorizedExecutionV2.principalClass` | `repository-code` | principal class of the admitted grant |
1391	| foundation `identity-schemas.v2#semantic-grant.principals[].kind` / `AuthorizedExecutionV2.semanticGrantPrincipalKind` | `trusted-repository-code` | Plan-bound semantic projection `{kind, closureId (tool closure), ownerSourceDigest (owner file manifest)}` with `analysisOperations ∋ prepare-code` |
1392	| workflow test-execution / `AuthorizedExecutionV2.workflowPrincipalSpelling` | `P-TRUSTED-REPO` | the workflow step's constant for the same principal (class `test-runner`) |
1393	
1394	The **authority grant** is the operational `authorizationRef`
1395	(`H("security.repo-execution-grant.v2", grant)`, the workflow's `securityGrantRef`):
1396	it is excluded from the Plan descriptor and from every content identity
1397	(`authorized-execution-interactive-with-declared-owner-disclosed` checks
1398	`authorizationRefInPlan=false`). The **semantic grant projection** is what the Plan
1399	binds. A universe with `preparedResolution=imported-inert` projects only
1400	`read-import`; only `host-prepared` projects `prepare-code`. Prepared semantic
1401	availability therefore never implies that this host holds or held an execution
1402	grant (`prepared-imported-inert-implies-no-host-execution-grant`).
1403	
1404	The principal, identified by `{projectId, snapshotId, ownerKey,
1405	ownerFileManifestSha256, toolchainDigest}`, is **outside** the first-party TCB.
1406	Executing it in-host is a disclosed trusted-code execution of code the user chose
1407	to analyze; OpenSIP does not vouch for it and does not confine it unless a
1408	platform primitive is enforced. The security owner supplies the revocation clock
1409	and cancellation carrier (H-2).

1429	JSON output: "Build scripts and procedural macros from N packages will run with

1442	### 5.3 What the preparation step does (feedback 4)
1443	
1444	Owned by the host resolved-inputs adapter (never the semantic worker), after
1445	snapshot seal and dependency-source admission, before PlanId:
1446	
1447	1. Verify the carrier (§3.3 CC-1..CC-5); materialize snapshot and dependency
1448	   sources read-only in private scratch; write the single projected
1449	   `.cargo/config.toml`; construct the environment.
1450	2. Check current trust and revocation state (security owner's clock), then for
1451	   each owner in order: re-check revocation (`before-each-owner`), run the bundled
1452	   Cargo to compile and execute the build script or to build the proc-macro crate
1453	   for the selected cfg set (`cargo check --offline --frozen --locked --target
1454	   <triple>` restricted to the owners; the linker used is the closure linker;
1455	   nothing is installed).
1456	3. **Inside this same authorized step**, drive the bundled compiler's expansion
1457	   through the closure proc-macro server for every invocation site in the
1458	   workspace and dependency crates that names one of the built proc-macro crates,
1459	   and capture the expanded token text per site as `macro-expansion` rows; capture
1460	   `cargo:` directive output as `build-script-directives` rows. Loading the
1461	   proc-macro dylib *is* executing repository code; it happens here, under the
1462	   principal, with the live boundaries, and nowhere else.
1463	4. **Capture required generated data, discard executable products** (R2). For
1464	   each build-script owner: capture the `cargo:` directive lines as a
1465	   `build-script-directives` row; capture as `generated-file` rows the regular
1466	   data files under `OUT_DIR` named by the crate's
1467	   `include!/include_str!/include_bytes!(concat!(env!("OUT_DIR"), …))` sites when
1468	   those are statically determinable, else every regular data file under
1469	   `OUT_DIR` within the PO-4 bounds; discard the build-script binary, every
1470	   dylib/object/archive/executable product and unreferenced scratch files; discard
1471	   the proc-macro dylibs. Referenced paths the script did not produce are recorded
1472	   (`missingReferencedPaths`) and become typed unknowns at analysis. Nothing of
1473	   `OUT_DIR` survives except the captured data rows
1474	   (`preparation-capture-keeps-referenced-data-discards-executable-products`).
1475	   The result is `PreparedOutputSetV3` (`kind: authorized-execution`).
1476	
1477	The semantic worker then consumes the inert set through the protocol
1478	(`PreparedOutputManifest/Chunk/Seal`), looks up expansions by exact site key, and
1479	executes nothing. `RepositoryResolutionV3.workerExecutesRepositoryCode` is the
1480	constant `false`. An external preparer may supply the same inert shape
1481	(`kind: imported-descriptor`, `declared` provenance, §3.6 PO-3); it can never
1482	supply a dylib.

1484	### 5.4 Failure, retry, cancellation, recovery
1485	
1486	| Event | Outcome |
1487	|---|---|
1488	| Owner build script exits non-zero | row `failed`; other owners continue; owner analyzed non-prepared |
1489	| Revocation observed before an owner | step stops; no further owner runs; rows already captured are discarded; `request-rejected` (`native.execution-not-authorized`) |
1490	| Wall or byte bound exceeded | whole step `operational-failed` (4); no row admitted. Existing `HOST.IO_FAILURE` with detail `native.prepare-bound-exceeded`. Not `BudgetExhausted`: a preparation bound is a safety bound of the adapter |
1491	| Cancellation | kill the process group, discard partial OUT_DIR and captured rows, `interrupted` (130) |
1492	| Retry | idempotent by `(dependencySourceSetId, toolchainDigest, cfgSetId, owners manifest)`; an identical inert set already in custody is reused without re-execution and without re-prompt when a policy record covers it |
1493	| Host crash mid-step | scratch reclaimed by ordinary crash reconciliation; no partial set is visible to Plan construction |
1494	| Ambient Cargo config found | `operational-failed` (4), `native.ambient-cargo-config`; never merged |
1495	| Imported set replaces in-host preparation | allowed; PO-0/PO-1/PO-3 apply |

1498

1501	(`executionCapableResolution=false`); `postinstall` scripts, bundler plugins and
1502	`ts-node` transforms are never run. "No network fetch" is a design invariant of
1503	first-party code, not an enforced bound on repository code.

1527	### 6.3 Bodies and language-specific exclusions
1528	
1529	Body spans are function, method, closure/lambda, `impl` item and block bodies.
1530	**Import exclusion means candidate exclusion, not byte editing** (R5): a span that
1531	consists solely of import/`use`/`extern crate`/top-level `require` declarations,
1532	module/file headers, shebangs, license headers, `#![...]` inner attributes or
1533	`declare`-only TypeScript declarations is an *import-only body* and is excluded
1534	as a clone candidate in every mode. A body that is kept is hashed over its
1535	**exact verbatim bytes**: an internal `use`, `import()`, `require` or directive
1536	inside a function body is part of the preimage and is never stripped, rewritten
1537	or normalized away at L0 (`clone-import-only-body-excluded-and-kept-bodies-hash-verbatim`:
1538	two bodies differing only by an internal `use` line are not exact clones).
1539	
1540	| Language | Kept significant at every level | L2 removes | L3 renames |
1541	|---|---|---|---|
1542	| TypeScript/JavaScript | string/template literal contents, regex literals, JSX text, `'use strict'`/`'use client'` directives, `/// <reference>` and `// @ts-*` directives, decorators | non-directive comments | local `let/const/var`, parameters, local function names, destructured locals; **not** properties, imports, exports, globals, `this` members |
1543	| Rust | macro invocation token trees verbatim, attributes including `#[cfg]`, string/byte/raw literals, lifetimes | non-doc comments | local `let` bindings, parameters, closure parameters, pattern bindings; **not** fields, paths, generics, trait names, macro-introduced names |
1544	
1545	Fact identity is same-language: `languageId ∈ {typescript, javascript, rust}` is
1546	in the preimage, so a TypeScript body never groups with a JavaScript or Rust body
1547	in `exact`/`normalized`/`structural`, even with identical bytes.
1548	
1549	### 6.4 TS/JS cross-language decision (feedback 9)
1550	
1551	Decision: `languageId` **stays** in exact fact identities (a `.ts` and a `.js`
1552	body are different facts). Cross-TS/JS matching is a separate **candidate-only**
1553	mode `cross-tsjs` under the named deterministic syntax projection
1554	`tsjs-erasure-v1`:
1555	
1556	- Removed before L3 normalization: type annotations, `type`/`interface`
1557	  declarations, type parameter lists, `as` assertions, `satisfies`, non-null `!`,
1558	  definite-assignment `!`, `declare`/`readonly`/`abstract`/access modifiers,
1559	  `implements` clauses, `import type`/`export type`.
1560	- **Never removed**: tokens that TypeScript compiles into runtime behavior —
1561	  `enum`/`const enum`, parameter properties (`constructor(private x)`),
1562	  value-bearing `namespace`, decorators, `import =`. A body containing any of them
1563	  is **excluded** from cross matching with reason
1564	  `runtime-significant-ts-tokens` and the token list; it is not projected.
1565	- Output rows carry `projectionId=tsjs-erasure-v1`, `authority=candidate-only`,
1566	  `semanticEquivalenceClaimed=false`, `automaticDeletionEligible=false` as schema
1567	  constants. A cross candidate is never a baseline member, never a Control input,
1568	  never a repair prerequisite.
1569	
1570	Cases: `clone-cross-tsjs-candidate-only`, `clone-cross-tsjs-runtime-significant-excluded`.

1572	### 6.5 Reviewed suppressions and false-positive boundary
1573	
1574	`CloneSuppressionV1` is a superseded draft transport shape, admitted by no product
1575	command. The single current review/suppression record is workflow ReviewDisposition.
1576	Its stable candidate key, mandatory finite expiry and advisory-only semantics are
1577	defined in workflow §12. Suppressed groups remain queryable with rationale and
1578	expired suppressions resurface. Fixed by
1579	`clone-false-positive-boundary`: trivial getters below thresholds → no candidate;

1581	comments → L1 not clones, L2 clones; identical bytes in two languages → never a

1722	
1723	`rust-semantic` protocol major **3**; `typescript-semantic` protocol major **2**.
1724	Capability tokens (closed, `CapabilityToken`): identity tokens
1725	`source-identity-snapshot2`, `plan-identity-plan2`, `fact-identity-fact2`,
1726	`coverage-v3`; plus `sealed-vfs-v1`, `multi-stage-analyze-v1`,

1733

1735	   identity tokens are required for every worker; a row lacking any of them, or
1736	   any token the Plan needs, is never spawned: affected Coverage keys are

1741	   array and identity versions; mismatch → `FAULT`, `PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION`,

1744	   including `nativeContext`, and `RepositoryResolutionV3`. The host state
1745	   machine admits it only when `identityNegotiated=true`; otherwise the run faults
1746	   with `sourceBytesSent=false` (`protocol3-open-universe-without-identity-faults`).

1748	   `NativeContextVerified`, then Analyze.

1851	**Clones ownership disclosure is typed, not null (CB3-MUST-5).** §11's
1852	`scopeVersusEnumeration` requires that a clones scope which cannot determine a
1853	body dialect mint no body identity, report the incompleteness in its Coverage,
1854	and leave the predicate and seal indeterminate. `NativeCause` had no member for
1855	any of the three ownership states the `languageVersionBinding` selection law
1856	refuses on, so that mandated disclosure had no expressible value and every
1857	implementation would have invented its own pairing — or emitted
1858	`nativeCause: null`, which records that a disclosure was owed and not made
1859	rather than making it. The closed pairing is now:
1860	`BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNERSHIP_REQUIRED` → `body-language-ownership-missing`;
1861	`BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_UNENUMERATED` → `body-language-owner-unenumerated`;
1862	`BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_AMBIGUOUS` → `body-language-owner-ambiguous`; each with
1863	deficiency `input-closure-incomplete` and the `indeterminate` class above, so
1864	the CLI/JSON/SARIF/HTML/agent parity fields carry one vocabulary.
1865	
1866	**The vocabulary alone did not close this, and an earlier revision wrongly said
1867	it did.** A retained-Run counterexample showed the concrete bypass: the Coverage
1868	prerequisite asked only whether `coverage` was `complete` and whether
1869	`deficiency` was non-null, so under partial ownership a Coverage carrying an
1870	*unrelated* `budget-exhausted` with `nativeCause: null` was admitted, as was
1871	`input-closure-incomplete` with a null cause. A cause vocabulary that nothing
1872	derives and nothing compares leaves the disclosure optional in practice.
1873	
1874	The pair is therefore **derived and enforced**, not merely expressible. The
1875	owning native unit derives the owed `(deficiency, nativeCause)` from the
1876	**committed ownership record** and **this scope's subjects**, in the selection
1877	law's own order: no committed ownership; then `enumeration: partial`, decided
1878	before any row is read so incomplete discovery can never act as an implicit
1879	edition selection; then a subject of this scope whose *selected* owners disagree
1880	on effective edition. Run closure re-derives the same pair independently and
1881	refuses a mismatch, so the claim cannot define its own correctness. Four
1882	distinct refusals keep the faults separable — a false `complete`
1883	(`COVERAGE_DIALECT_PREREQUISITE`), an undisclosed null deficiency
1884	(`…_UNDISCLOSED`), a wrong deficiency (`COVERAGE_DIALECT_DEFICIENCY_MISMATCH`)
1885	and a wrong or null cause (`COVERAGE_DIALECT_CAUSE_MISMATCH`).
1886	
1887	`examinedExhaustive` and `resolutionCompleteness.state` stay **different
1888	claims**: a host may have examined its committed partition exhaustively while
1889	resolution is `not-applicable` entirely, and neither implies the other or the
1890	ownership disclosure.
1891	
1892	A **deliberately excluded** selection is not an unfinished enumeration and owes
1893	no disclosure. The owner exists, enumeration is complete, and the path is
1894	compiled only by targets outside the selection: the host examined that subject
1895	and correctly produced no fact, so `complete` remains lawful. A selection is
1896	committed in the universe identity and visible to every consumer; unfinished
1897	enumeration leaves no such trace. Collapsing the two would either hide a real
1898	gap or slander a lawful selection. The remaining
1899	selection-law refusals get no cause and that is deliberate:
1900	`BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_NOT_COMPILED` and `BODY_LANGUAGE_OWNER_NOT_SELECTED` are
1901	per-body refusals §11 states are compatible with `coverage: complete`, and
1902	`BODY_LANGUAGE_DIALECT_ABSENT`/`BODY_LANGUAGE_DIALECT_AMBIGUOUS` refuse at the
1903	universe before any Coverage entry exists. The body refusal itself is unchanged:
1904	a producer that cannot mint a body identity still must not pretend to, and an
1905	empty clones Coverage remains indeterminate rather than a finding of no clones.
1906	
1907	**Fault law (R7; `stage_authority`, `run_termination`, `StageAuthorityV1`).**
1908	A worker that faults — process fault, protocol violation, `ProviderFault` frame,
1909	crash — contributes **no facts, no Coverage entries and no Run**: its diagnostics
1910	(stderr, fault detail) are an operational record only and can never mint an
1911	authoritative fact; the invocation is `operational-failed` (4)
1912	`PROVIDER.PROTOCOL_VIOLATION`; cancellation is `interrupted` (130) with the same
1913	no-facts rule (`fault-worker-diagnostics-never-mint-facts-or-run`). By contrast a
1914	stage that terminates cleanly over **successfully admitted but incomplete inputs**
1915	(missing crate, generated file unavailable, unresolved edges) yields admitted
1916	facts and typed Coverage, seals an **authoritative** Run, and terminates
1917	`indeterminate` (3) with the deficiency as typed detail in the coverage2 record
1918	(`admitted-incomplete-inputs-yield-authoritative-indeterminate-3`).
1919	`BudgetExhausted` and `Unavailable` are clean typed terminals: facts before the
1920	terminal are admitted and the Run is authoritative with the stage `partial`.

1949	**Three admitted textual forms of one digest, and when each is required.** They are not
1950	alternative recipes; the preimage and the `H` frame are always the foundation's.
1951	
1952	| Form | Where it is required | Example |
1953	|---|---|---|
1954	| foundation typed prefix `<prefix>:<64 hex>` | any foundation identity field: `snapshot2:`, `plan2:`, `closure2:`, `scope2:`, `coverage2:`, `import2:` | `scope2:2c5f…` |
1955	| native `Sha256Text` `sha256:<64 hex>` | any native record field typed `Sha256Text`, where the foundation domain is not carried in-band: `nativeContextId`, `dependencySourceSetId`, `unifiedFeaturesId`, `preparedOutputSetId`, `CoverageKeyV2.subjectScopeCommitment` | `sha256:2c5f…` |
