1958	A suffix field is bare precisely because its typed prefix belongs to the foundation identity
1959	it was taken from; admission recovers that identity by re-prefixing and requires a retained
1960	closure to match (§2.3, §2.4). The textual form is a spelling, not an annotation:
1961	which recipe a field carries is what that field's own `x-opensip-digest`
1962	annotation says, and no prefix implies one.
1963	
1964	**Language-version binding for FACT-IDENTITY body frames.** A `clones` relation
1965	payload's `bodyIdentity` is framed with a `languageId` and a `languageVersion`
1966	that the inherited `fact-identity-policy.v2` requires to be "canonical identity
1967	bytes supplied by ResolvedInputs/PlanId, not a human display string", for "the
1968	provider interpreting the body span". The identity that satisfies it is the
1969	**compiler**, and it is already committed: a universe's own `nativeContextId` —
1970	a reference Run closure already requires to be Plan-selected — reaches the
1971	admitted retained context, whose `toolchain` carries `rustcVersion` and
1972	`rustCommitHash` here, and `compilerName`, `compilerVersion` and
1973	`compilerPackageDigest` for TypeScript. §2.3's admission already refuses
1974	`native.native-context-compiler-version-not-from-manifest` unless that version
1975	equals the admitted tool closure's `semanticVersion`, for both languages, so the
1976	binding inherits a real chain from a retained closure manifest rather than
1977	copying a display string. **Following an existing admitted reference needs no new
1978	universe field**, and none was added.
1979	
1980	The binding lives in the universe domain rows at
1981	`foundation/identity-schemas.v2.json#/x-opensip-digest-domains/domainSets/native-semantic-universe/*/languageVersionBinding`,
1982	and it names, per language, the exact source path of every field of the closed
1983	`body-language-version` record plus each **excluded** field with its reason. The
1984	boundary is: what identifies the component that **interprets the body span**, and
1985	the selected source **dialect**. Not the operational platform (`targetTriple`,
1986	`hostTriple`), not the resolution environment (`sysrootDigest`,
1987	`standardLibraryComponentDigests`, `libSelection`), not the code-generation
1988	backend (`rustcDevLlvmDigest`), not build or dependency tooling (`cargoVersion`,
1989	`resolverVersion`), not paths (`crateRootPaths`), and not option synthesis
1990	(`languageMode`, `synthesizerVersion`), which describes how a program was
1991	assembled rather than which language read the body.
1992	
1993	`edition` is a map from crate **name** to year, so it is the *selected value*
1994	that is the dialect, never the map: a body identity that varied with unrelated
1995	crates would be neither meaningful nor representable. When the map's distinct
1996	value set has exactly one member — the ordinary case, including a large
1997	single-edition workspace — that member is the dialect of every body and no owner
1998	selection arises. When it has more than one, the **owning compilation unit
1999	decides**.
2000	
2001	More precisely, the **compilation target** decides, not the package. Cargo
2002	documents an `edition` on a target that **defaults to** `package.edition` when
2003	absent — `cargo metadata` lists `targets[].edition` and states the package value
2004	is a default individual targets may differ from, and the `[[bin]]`/`[lib]`
2005	`edition` field, though deprecated, is still documented. So *source → package →
2006	package edition* misses a supported override, and a universe whose package
2007	defaults **all agree** can still contain a target that does not. There is
2008	therefore **no single-edition fast path**: a `clones` fact over a Rust universe
2009	requires the committed ownership relation whatever the package map looks like,
2010	and a null `sourceUnitOwnershipId` admits no clone.
2011	
2012	`SourceUnitOwnershipV1` is that relation **and the explicit selection**, and
2013	`RustUniverseV2ResolvedInputs.sourceUnitOwnershipId` is the `h-identity` of
2014	`native.source-unit-ownership.v1` that carries it — required and nullable,
2015	exactly as `preparedOutputSetId` is. It holds three things:
2016	
2017	- `units` — the **closed table of compilation targets**:
2018	  `{unitId, markerPath, crateName, targetKind, targetName, targetEdition}`.
2019	  `targetEdition` is the target's own edition when it sets one and `null` when it
2020	  takes the package default, so the two committed places can never contradict.
2021	- `selectedUnitIds` — the **explicit analysis scope**, non-empty, every member a
2022	  declared `unitId`.
2023	- `ownership` — the pure relation `{path, unitId}`, carrying no edition and no
2024	  metadata, so it cannot contradict the table.
2025	
2026	`unitId` is **derived, never declared**:
2027	
2028	```
2029	unitId = H(native.compilation-unit.v1,
2030	           UnitIdentityV1{schemaVersion: 1, markerPath, targetKind, targetName})
2031	```
2032	
2033	carried as `sha256:<64 hex>`, with **`derived` retention**: nothing separate is
2034	retained, because the preimage *is* the unit row, and admission re-derives and
2035	compares (`sourceUnitOwnership.unitId`). **This is not an opaque digest** — the
2036	preimage record, its domain, its codec and its selector are all published here,
2037	so any consumer rebuilds it from the row that carries it.
2038	
2039	An earlier draft joined the fields with delimiters,
2040	`markerPath#targetKind:targetName`. **That is withdrawn.** It was injective only
2041	by excluding `#` from `markerPath`, and a `#` in a repository directory is
2042	admissible under the canonical repository-path contract — so the recipe narrowed
2043	admitted paths in order to make a delimiter work, which is the wrong trade. `H`
2044	needs no such restriction, is fixed width for every admitted path and name
2045	length, and a marker under a `#`-containing directory closes a complete Run.
2046	
2047	`units` is strictly unique by `unitId`, and `unitId` is a function of the
2048	metadata, so **two contradictory rows for one purported unit are a refusal, never
2049	two units that differ by accident**, and a selection or ownership row naming an
2050	undeclared `unitId` is an unbound caller label and inadmissible.
2051	
2052	`markerPath` is the inventoried manifest that declares the target — the same
2053	vocabulary `WorkspaceUnitV2` already uses, under the ordinary canonical
2054	repository-path admission with no added restriction. **`WorkspaceUnitV2` and
2055	`UnitMembershipV1` cannot supply this binding**, and that is a granularity
2056	statement rather than an oversight: they identify *workspace* units
2057	(`cargo-package`, `cargo-workspace`), while one package holds several targets
2058	that may carry different editions. Naming the marker joins my targets to that
2059	existing discovery vocabulary instead of competing with it.
2060	
2061	**Because the selection is committed inside the record whose `h-identity` the
2062	universe names, a different selection is a different record, a different identity
2063	and therefore a different `sourceUniverse`.** That is what makes the required case
2064	representable: one physical source path compiled by two targets at two editions is
2065	validly analysed **under each selection, one at a time**, each with its own
2066	correct dialect and its own body identity, and **no relation payload changed** to
2067	make it so.
2068	
2069	Selection is exact and total, and the order of decision is fixed so each step has
2070	its own cause. No committed ownership refuses. `enumeration: partial` refuses
2071	**before any row is read**. Rows are those whose `path` **equals** the enclosing
2072	fact's anchor path — never a prefix, never a nearest directory, never a first
2073	match — and no row at all refuses as not-compiled. Rows are then restricted to
2074	`selectedUnitIds`, and a path compiled only by **unselected** targets refuses as
2075	not-selected rather than borrowing an out-of-scope edition. Selected owners whose
2076	effective editions **agree** are admissible — the ordinary shared-file and
2077	lib-plus-test-target case. Selected owners that **disagree** are an ambiguous
2078	unselected request and refuse. §2.1's retained-input admission independently
2079	requires every marker and owned path to be a source of the same snapshot, every
2080	selection and ownership row to name a declared unit, and every deferring unit to
2081	name a crate the same `edition` map declares.
2082	
2083	**Selected scope is not incomplete enumeration.** A selection says these targets
2084	*are* the analysis, so an owner outside them is deliberately out of scope; it is
2085	committed in the identity, so every consumer sees it and it changes the universe.
2086	`partial` says the producer did not finish, so an owner *inside* the selected
2087	scope may exist that is not listed and could contradict a listed one — a gap in
2088	knowledge, invisible as a selection, admitting no dialect at all. Silently
2089	omitting a conflicting owner from the table is not a selection either: an
2090	omission leaves no trace, whereas a selection is part of the universe identity.
2091	Partial evidence stays useful under the existing law rather than voiding a Run —
2092	the clones scope mints no body identity, its Coverage carries the incompleteness,
2093	and the predicate and seal are indeterminate.
2094	
2095	The consequence is the one that matters: an **ordinary mixed-edition workspace
2096	has a representable valid form**. Each path is owned by units of one edition, so
2097	bodies of *both* editions are admissible in the *same* universe, each carrying
2098	its own dialect. Only a path genuinely compiled under two different editions
2099	refuses, which is a real ambiguity in the input rather than a gap in the law.
2100	This record states what a producer claims it enumerated; it admits no compiler,
2101	measures no build and qualifies no enumerator.
2102

2104	reimplemented: `canonical.parse` refuses `1.0`, `1e0`, `-0`, non-finite tokens,

2106	exact-enum / exact-integer validator so `true` is never an integer and `1.0` is
2107	never `1` (`float-spelled-integer-refused`). Every native record schema is closed
2108	(`additionalProperties:false`, checked by the report's `openObjects=[]`).

62	## 1. Invocation, step, attempt, Run (AR-08)
63	
64	An invocation is one host request. Its operational identity is `RequestId`, minted
65	before admission and retained for refusal as well as success. The invocation is an
66	ordered acyclic list of at most **64 steps**; `StepId` is the zero-based position.
67	Each admitted attempt of a step receives a fresh `ExecutionId`; a step has at most
68	**3 attempts**. Only `analysis` and `verify` steps seal or link a content-derived
69	`run2`. `comparison`, `query`, `render`, `import`, `repair-preview`, `repair-apply`,
70	`test-execution`, `native-preparation`, `mutation`, `export-delivery` and `doctor` are operational steps
71	that never mint a Run. Schema: `invocation-record.schema.json`.
72	
73	**Step DAG versus derivation DAG.** The step list is the operational workflow. Each
74	analysis/verify *attempt* owns exactly one derivation DAG (`exec-plan2`, at most
75	**1024 stages**) recorded in the attempt's `derivation` binding
76	(`planId`, `executionPlanId`, `stageCount`, `stagesCompleted`, `firstFailedStage`).
77	A step never depends on a stage and a stage never references a step. A retry on
78	identical admitted inputs may bind the same `exec-plan2` and the same Run; attempts
79	remain separately auditable.
80	
81	**Dependencies.** `dependsOn` names lower StepIds only (a forward or self reference is
82	`WORKFLOW.DEPENDENCY_CYCLE`, request-rejected). `requirement` is `required` or
83	`optional`; a required step may not depend on an optional step
84	(`WORKFLOW.REQUIRED_DEPENDS_ON_OPTIONAL`). `dependencyGate` is `completed` (every
85	dependency completed) or `terminal` (every dependency reached any terminal outcome;
86	lawful only for `render`/`export-delivery`, which project whatever happened). A
87	step whose gate is unmet is `skipped` with a typed `skipReason`. Step outcomes are
88	closed: `completed`, `rejected`, `failed`, `skipped`, `cancelled`, `abandoned`
89	(crash recovery only).
90	
91	**Retries.** `retryPolicy=idempotent-retry` is lawful only for `analysis`, `verify`,
92	`query`, `render`, `doctor` and `export-delivery`, only for `faultCause=ledger-busy`,
93	and within the 3-attempt budget; exhausting it is `LEDGER.BUSY_TIMEOUT` (4) with
94	detail `WORKFLOW.RETRY_BUDGET_EXHAUSTED`. `host-io` and every other fault are never
95	retried. `mutation`, `import`, `repair-preview`, `repair-apply`, `comparison`, `native-preparation` and `test-execution`
96	carry `retryPolicy=none` by schema; a spec violating this is refused.
97	
98	**Mutation idempotence and recovery.** Generic `mutation` steps use the bare
99	64-hex `H("workflow.mutation-intent", MutationReplayScopeV1)`. The closed retained
100	scope is exactly `{schemaVersion:1,requestId,stepId,projectId,operation}`, with
101	`operation` equal to `MutationParams.mutationClass`. This explicitly succeeds the
102	former undefined `{operation,projectId,effect preimage}` description. The key is
103	operational and scoped to one host-minted request and admitted immutable step;
104	different fresh requests never deduplicate each other's generic mutations.
105	`sourceStep` resolves inside that same retained invocation, whose admitted
106	parameters and completed dependency results are immutable. Before lookup or
107	replay the host validates the scope and full params, recomputes the key and
108	requires the retained invocation/project/step/operation binding; a caller cannot
109	nominate another invocation's scope or change effect inputs under an old key.
110	Receipt lookup is never an effect-authorization mechanism. A same-scope COMPLETED
111	receipt permits delivery replay with no second effect. Failure, unknown state or
112	incomplete execution requires the operation's existing recovery law, not blind
113	re-execution. Recovery started in a new request retains its own operational scope
114	and the explicit original journal/intent links required by §§6/12.
115	
116	Repair apply is the explicit content-derived exception: it is a dedicated
117	`repair-apply` step, excluded from generic MutationParams. It uses the raw SHA-256 of
118	canonical `{operation:"repair-apply",projectId,repairPlanId,baseSnapshotId}` as its
119	idempotency key. An equal completed key performs no second effect. The original
120	receipt is immutable; a replay delivery produces a separately identified receipt
121	with the new request/attempt binding and `replayed=true`. Mutation receipts use
122	`receipt2:` plus `H('workflow.mutation-receipt', receiptWithoutReceiptId)` and remain
123	retained when an effect or later verification fails. Read-only recovery inspection
124	is distinct from separately authorized recovery writes (§6).
125	
126	**Audit gate ownership.** An analysis step declares `verdictGate=self|delegated`.
127	`self` applies its Run verdict. `delegated` requires authoritative analysis and a
128	consuming comparison step: a completed failing Run then contributes operational
129	success with its RunId, while the comparison owns the regression gate. This lets
130	inherited findings remain visible without failing the PR. Missing required Coverage
131	still contributes indeterminate; delegation cannot hide an incomplete analysis.
132	The comparison result is a distinct closed `ComparisonStepResult`, never a Run.
133	
134	**Cancellation.** A signal is recorded with the phase at which it arrived.
135	*before-settle* (some required step not yet terminal): remaining steps are
136	`cancelled`, the aggregate is `interrupted` (130), and a Run committed by an earlier
137	step is named in the termination's `runId`. *after-settle* (every required step
138	already terminal): the aggregate is **not reclassified**; the settled class stands.
139	Per kind: an analysis attempt aborts and leaves no Run; an import discards its
140	staged bytes; a repair-apply honours cancellation only before `APPLYING`, and during
141	the bounded rename loop the journal, not the signal, decides (§6).
142	
143	**Aggregate termination (D9 ordering preserved).** Over required steps only:
144	`operational-failed` > `request-rejected` > `policy-failed` > `indeterminate` >
145	`success`. An optional step's rejection or failure never changes the aggregate.
146	Policy fail dominates indeterminate across steps exactly as inside one Run, and a
147	required operational fault dominates a committed failing Run (its `runId` is still
148	carried). Exit code derives from class by the fixed table only. Ties retain the first
149	termination carrying domain detail in step order, or the first termination when
150	none carries detail, so a useful comparison remedy is preserved.
151	
152	**Ephemeral analysis.** `--ephemeral` produces the second member of the closed
153	`AnalysisResult` union: `authority=ephemeral`, `durability=not-required`, no `runId`,
154	no receipt, only semantic `planId`/`evidenceId` so the result can be cited. It cannot
155	satisfy baseline adoption, repair preview/apply, verify or authoritative replay
156	(`WORKFLOW.EPHEMERAL_CANNOT_SUPPLY_AUTHORITY`, `REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE`, exit 2). A
157	failing ephemeral verdict terminates `policy-failed` with `authority=ephemeral`
158	instead of a `runId`; the branch contract admits exactly one of the two.
159	
160	**Default invocation.** `opensip` with no arguments is discovery then one durable
161	authoritative analysis (steps `analysis`, `render`). Retention is DEFAULTED
162	durable-unbounded (CD-RT-5), disclosed with the storage root before first write.
163	No policy file is written implicitly.

167	## 2. Portable baseline and runnable prior detector (AR-10)
168	
169	`BaselineArtifactV1` lives in the repository as tracked intent
170	(`opensip.baseline.json`). `baselineId = H('workflow.baseline', descriptor)`. The
171	descriptor pins: origin ProjectId, source `snapshot2`, the **authoritative** `run2`
172	and `plan2` (an ephemeral result is refused: `BASELINE.SOURCE_EPHEMERAL`), the
173	fingerprint recipe (`finding-fingerprint`, major ≥ 2), every contributing detector's
174	`closure2` with semantics major, the complete **pivot closure** (detector executable,
175	evaluator, toolchain/stdlib, schema set; each a `closure2` with manifest digest,
176	protocol major and platform), the evaluation context digests, the **embedded**
177	policy/scope/waiver documents whose digests equal those context digests, rule
178	coverage, and sorted unique entries. Custody (outside identity) carries host release,
179	export time, `retentionPins` (the Run and every pivot closure) and an optional signed
180	`closureBundle` reference.
181	
182	**Fresh CI.** Comparison never reads the origin machine's store. A fresh host admits
183	the artifact by recomputing `baselineId`, checking schema major, recipe major,
184	sortedness, context-document digests and project correspondence (same ProjectId, or
185	explicit `--accept-origin`, else `BASELINE.PROJECT_UNMAPPED` and no comparison). It
186	resolves each pivot closure from (a) a retained generation, (b) an installed signed
187	release with the same `closure2`, or (c) the signed closure bundle; all under
188	**current trust**. A closure that is missing (`pivot-detector-unavailable`), revoked
189	(`pivot-closure-revoked`) or incompatible with the host's protocol majors/platform
190	(`pivot-closure-incompatible`) makes E0 unavailable; a revoked closure is never
191	executed, whatever bytes are present.
192	
193	**Detector semantics.** Semantics can change within a major, so two-way comparison
194	is lawful only when the closures are identical (`identical-closure`) or the current
195	detector's signed manifest lists the baseline `closure2` as exactly semantically
196	compatible at the same major (`declared-compatible`). Otherwise the baseline detector
197	must run over current source (`three-way-pivot`, an authoritative pivot analysis step
198	planned before the primary one) or the detector's entries are `INDETERMINATE`.
199	Fingerprint dual emission (`legacyFingerprint`) migrates identity only and never
200	supplies the prior algorithm. Adoption pins the Run and the pivot closures as
201	retention roots; loss of a pin is disclosed as partial availability and yields typed
202	indeterminacy, never a silent two-way fallback. `baseline-upgrade` re-adopts under the
203	current detector explicitly and is a mutation with its own receipt.

207	## 3. Multi-axis comparison (AR-11)
208	
209	`ComparisonResultV1` (`comparison2:` = `H('workflow.comparison', descriptor)`)
210	attributes every fingerprint to the **first** axis at which it changes along a fixed
211	counterfactual chain evaluated over *current* source:
212	
213	| Pivot | Facts from | Policy | Scope | Waivers |
214	|---|---|---|---|---|
215	| B | baseline artifact entries | prior | prior | prior |
216	| E0 | prior detector closure over current source | prior | prior | prior |
217	| E1 | current detector | prior | prior | prior |
218	| E2 | current detector | current | prior | prior |
219	| E3 | current detector | current | current | prior |
220	| E4 | current Run | current | current | current |
221	
222	Axis order is code (B→E0), detection (E0→E1), policy (E1→E2), scope (E2→E3),
223	waiver (E3→E4, by waived status). E1–E3 are pure re-evaluations of retained current
224	facts under the baseline's embedded documents. They are available only when their
225	results were actually bound; an unchanged axis is `not-needed`, and a required
226	unbound re-evaluation is `unavailable` with typed indeterminacy. E0 is
227	`not-needed` when the detector is unchanged or declared compatible, `available`
228	when the pivot ran, `unavailable` otherwise. Classifications are `UNCHANGED`,
229	`CODE-NET-NEW`, `CODE-FIXED`, `DETECTION-DELTA`, `POLICY-DELTA`, `SCOPE-DELTA`,
230	`WAIVER-DELTA`, `EVIDENCE-DELTA`, `INDETERMINATE`; each entry also records
231	`presence` at every pivot and `subsequentDeltas` (later axes at which it changed
232	again). Deleting a waiver while adding a bug therefore yields one `WAIVER-DELTA` and
233	one `CODE-NET-NEW`; a bug introduced and simultaneously hidden by disabling the rule
234	is `CODE-NET-NEW` with `subsequentDeltas=[policy]`.
235	
236	**Detector union.** Comparison covers the union of baseline and current detectors.
237	Added detectors set E0 false. Removed detectors require the actual current-trusted
238	prior detector pivot and set E1–E4 false; E0 must never be substituted with B.
239	Consequently a new bug hidden by removing its detector remains CODE-NET-NEW and
240	can gate. Missing prior execution is indeterminate, including detector removal.
241	
242	**Evidence axis.** Compare the exact bound `import2` identity sets per kind, with
243	payload/correspondence/scope/observation digests retained in each BoundImport.
244	Replacing an artifact with another of the same kind is still an evidence change
245	(`evidence-content-changed`). For a rule with declared `evidenceUse`: if required evidence is
246	absent on the current side the entry is `INDETERMINATE`
247	(`required-evidence-unavailable`) and the rule's coverage is unsatisfied; if
248	availability changed and the rule gates on either side, attribution is
249	`INDETERMINATE` (`evidence-availability-changed`); only for a non-gating rule may a
250	presence change be `EVIDENCE-DELTA`. Required evidence loss can never disappear as a
251	non-gating delta.
252	
253	**Audit profiles select gate semantics explicitly** (schema `AuditProfile`):
254	
255	| Profile | Gates CODE-NET-NEW | Gates newly live via policy/scope/waiver | Gates all current live | New waiver suppresses net-new | Rule gating under |
256	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
257	| `code-regression` (default for `audit`) | yes | no | no | no | baseline or current |
258	| `policy-change` | yes | yes | no | no | baseline or current |
259	| `full-current` | yes | yes | yes | yes | current only |
260	| `report-only` | no | no | no | yes | current only |
261	
262	A `CODE-NET-NEW` entry that is not live in current (hidden by a later policy/scope
263	change or by a waiver added in the same change) still gates under
264	`baseline-or-current` with `gateReason=code-net-new-policy-hidden`. Verdict is `fail`
265	if any entry gates, else `indeterminate` if any `INDETERMINATE` entry belongs to a
266	gating rule or a current gating rule has unsatisfied/unknown required Coverage or
267	evidence, else `pass`. Rule deficiencies are enumerated independently of findings;
268	zero emitted findings never establish complete analysis. Whole-comparison indeterminacy (unmapped project,
269	unsupported schema/recipe major, context document mismatch) performs no comparison
270	and emits zero entries with a typed remedy. Enum precedence never decides a gate.

274	## 4. Imported evidence: one wrapper, typed payloads (AR-11)
275	
276	There is exactly one import identity: `importId = 'import2:' + H('import', wrapper)`
277	where the wrapper is the foundation `import` descriptor (schemaVersion 2, kinds
278	`runtime|test|history|dependency|prepared`). Each kind admits exactly one canonical
279	payload domain. Native runtime/test/history formats are adapter inputs normalized
280	into the workflow-owned payload before wrapping.
281	
282	| Kind | Admitted payload domain | Owner |
283	|---|---|---|
284	| runtime | `workflow.import-payload.runtime.v1` | workflow |
285	| test | `workflow.import-payload.test.v1` | workflow |
286	| history | `workflow.import-payload.history.v1` | workflow |
287	| dependency | `native.import-payload.dependency-source.v1` | native |
288	| prepared | `native.import-payload.prepared-output.v1` | native |
289	
290	The closed registry names the exact schema document and JSON selector. Its
291	`payloadSchemaDigest` is raw SHA-256 of the entire schema document's bytes;
292	`payloadDigest` is raw SHA-256 of the canonical validated payload. The host validates
293	the selected payload, source correspondence, foundation scope descriptor,
294	BuildIdentityV1, ImportObservationV1 and wrapper using the trusted local schema
295	closure. Merely carrying a recognized payloadDomain is insufficient. Caller-supplied
296	schema bytes must equal the registry document exactly. No network schema resolution
297	is allowed. All auxiliary digests are raw SHA-256 of their canonical closed records;
298	those preimages are retained. The `import2` wrapper alone uses the H-domain recipe.
299	The same payload with different provenance or observation semantics is a different import.
300	
301	Any other pairing is `IMPORT.KIND_PAYLOAD_MISMATCH`; an unregistered payload schema is
302	`IMPORT.PAYLOAD_SCHEMA_UNREGISTERED`; no artifact-supplied schema is ever admitted.
303	`opensip import KIND PATH` is a mutation step with an import receipt; the user-named
304	PATH is a `UserInputPath` opened through the security unit's nofollow custody and
305	never enters identity; every path inside a payload is a strict `LogicalPath`.
306	
307	Source correspondence is mandatory (`IMPORT.MAPPING_REQUIRED`, `CONFIG.INVALID`):
308	the shared closed SourceCorrespondence union in common.schema.json,
309	`exact-snapshot` or `vcs-revision` with VCS/build/mapping fields. Staleness
310	against a Plan is a closed table (`StalenessRule`): snapshot-equal → `current`,
311	consumable; snapshot-differs / commit-differs → `stale`, unmapped-only;
312	commit-equal-dirty → `unverifiable`, unmapped-only; build-identity-differs →
313	`wrong-build`, unmapped-only. An equal clean commit is consumable only with an
314	admitted SourceMappingV1 whose source paths and hashes join the current snapshot
315	inventory; an equal commit without that mapping remains unmapped-only. Corrupt bytes → refused (`IMPORT.ARTIFACT_CORRUPT`).
316	Explicitly selecting a stale import for a Plan is `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`
317	with `IMPORT.STALE_FOR_PLAN` (2). Unmapped-only evidence may be listed and queried
318	but never feeds a predicate.
319	
320	**No-hits is not non-use.** Runtime subjects carry `observed-hit`,
321	`observable-unhit`, `unobservable` or `unmapped`. `observed-hit` supplies positive
322	execution evidence and `observable-unhit` supplies bounded negative evidence,
323	always together with the observation window and population; `unobservable`/`unmapped` never become unhit signals and the schema
324	refuses a hit count on them. One window never establishes universal non-use;
325	runtime coverage is never OpenSIP Coverage. History payloads are advisory priority
326	inputs unless a policy predicate explicitly declares `evidenceUse` for them.

330	## 5. Declarative policy DSL, authoring test, candidate → inspect → review
331	
332	**DSL.** `PolicyDocumentV1` is closed data: rules with a `ruleProgramRef`
333	(contribution, stable id, semantics major, program digest), `enabled`, `severity`
334	(`note|warning|error`), `gate`, a `subjectEnumeration` (universe, subject kind,
335	include/exclude globs over `LogicalPath` with only `*`, `?` and whole-segment `**`),
336	an `emitWhen` predicate tree and `evidenceUse` declarations. Predicates are exactly
337	the evaluator's set: atoms `exists|none|count-at-most|all-covered` over a relation,
338	minimum resolution and typed field filters (`eq|neq|in|prefix|glob|gte|lte`), plus
339	`and|or|not`, depth ≤ 8, ≤ 64 nodes per rule, ≤ 512 rules. Evaluation is strong
340	Kleene: under incomplete Coverage `exists` is true on a match else indeterminate,
341	`none` false on a match else indeterminate, `count-at-most` false above N else
342	indeterminate, `all-covered` indeterminate. A true predicate emits a finding; false
343	is a retained no-match; an indeterminate gating rule is a typed deficiency. An atom
344	over imported evidence must be declared in `evidenceUse`; required evidence absent
345	makes the rule indeterminate, optional evidence absent is disclosed as
346	`IMPORT.ABSENT_FOR_PREDICATE` and is not a gating deficiency. There is no string
347	expression, hook, script, include or exec key; any such key is a schema violation
348	(`POLICY.IMPERATIVE_KEY_REFUSED`). Policy, ScopeDocumentV1 and resolved WaiverSetV1
349	digests are raw SHA-256 of their canonical closed documents, retained as blobs.
350	The compiled RuleProgramV1 separately hashes its policy digest and ordered rule
351	programs to proof.ruleProgramDigest; these are auxiliary hashes, not H identities.
352	
353	**Waivers.** A waiver targets a fingerprint or `(ruleId, subjectPath)` with a reason
354	and `expires` (date or null). Expiry and duplicates are resolved at **Plan
355	construction** against the admitted trust clock: expired waivers leave the effective
356	set and are disclosed (`POLICY.WAIVER_EXPIRED`), two waivers on one target refuse
357	(`POLICY.DUPLICATE_WAIVER`, `CONFIG.INVALID`), and the Plan's `waiverDigest` is that of
358	the *resolved* effective set, keeping evaluation pure. `opensip waive` is the explicit
359	tracked-intent write; nothing writes a waiver implicitly.
360	
361	**Authoring test.** `opensip policy test SUITE` is Query class. A suite supplies the
362	candidate policy, waivers, an `asOfDate`, optional test-only overrides and cases with
363	typed fact fixtures (subjects, facts, declared Coverage, available evidence kinds) or
364	a bounded source fixture. Facts cases are evaluated by the deterministic fixture
365	verifier (the finite declarative fixture evaluator; this is reference evidence, not
366	qualification of the production evaluator or native providers); sources cases run only under an ephemeral non-authoritative Plan with
367	bundled providers and otherwise report `not-executable`. Expectations are
368	`finding{ruleId,minCount,maxCount,subjects}`, `no-finding`, `verdict`, `indeterminate`.
369	The result (`policytest2:`) records candidate and effective digests, resolver
370	acceptance and refusals, applied overrides, waiver resolution and
371	`enforcementUnchanged=true`; the same suite always yields the same result identity.
372	
373	**Candidate → inspect → review (Map side).** `opensip candidates` lists
374	`Candidate` records derived from one sealed Run: findings plus advisory kinds
375	(`clone-candidate`, `low-confidence-unused`, `runtime-unhit`, `history-stale`) with an
376	evidence level. Only a finding on a gating rule is `controlBearing`. `opensip inspect`
377	returns a bounded `InspectionBundle` (≤ 4096 facts, Coverage, imports, limitations).
378	`opensip review join` records a `ReviewDisposition` (`accept|reject|defer`, reviewer
379	principal human/model/policy-rule, note, `suppressUntil` ≤ 365 days) as a mutation
380	with a receipt. The disposition schema admits no verdict, Run, baseline or
381	authorization field: review can never mint a Control verdict or authorize a repair.
382	`reject`/`defer` suppress the candidate from listings until `suppressUntil` or until
383	its fingerprint changes; expired suppressions resurface with `previouslyReviewed`.
384	`opensip review brief` is an advisory, bounded (≤ 1000) ordering labelled with its
385	producer (a model producer names its `closure2`); truncation is explicit.

389	## 6. Repair preview, apply, verify (AR-08)
390	
391	Three separately authorized steps; schemas in `repair.schema.json`.
392	
393	**Preview** (`repair-preview`, Query class) requires an **authoritative** evidence Run
394	(`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_NOT_AUTHORITATIVE` for ephemeral) whose availability is retained
395	and whose sealed assurance is replayable (else the plan is not applicable with
396	`REPAIR.EVIDENCE_RUN_UNAVAILABLE`), a recipe closure admitted under current trust
397	(`REPAIR.RECIPE_TRUST_REVOKED`; an absent admission is also refused), targets present in that Run, and a live tree equal to
398	the Run's snapshot (`REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED`). It emits `RepairPlanV1`
399	(`repairplan2:` = `H('workflow.repair-plan', descriptor)`) bound to `snapshot2`,
400	`run2`, `plan2`, exact per-file edits (`replace|delete|create`, preimage digest from
401	the snapshot inventory, postimage digest and bytes; ≤ 4096 files, ≤ 16 MiB each,
402	≤ 64 MiB total), evidence requirements, the recipe's permitted edit scope (an edit
403	outside it is `REPAIR.EDIT_OUTSIDE_PERMITTED_SCOPE`), `applicable`, unmet
404	preconditions and limitations. Destructive unused-code recipes additionally require
405	native closed-world resolution evidence; an advisory similarity or runtime-cold
406	signal alone never authorizes deletion. Preview never writes.
407	
408	**Apply** (`repair-apply`, mutation) is bound to the exact `repairPlanId`, base
409	snapshot and project by a security-unit authorization (`REPAIR.CONSENT_NOT_BOUND`);
410	CI requires policy consent. Current recipe trust and live authorization are checked
411	again immediately before apply. It journals `RepairApplyJournalV1` through
412	`PREPARING → STAGED → APPLYING → APPLIED → COMMITTED`: every postimage is written to a
413	same-directory temp and digest-verified, every preimage is re-verified against the
414	live file (`REPAIR.TARGET_PREIMAGE_MISMATCH` leaves `FAILED_CLEAN`), renames proceed in
415	ascending path order, then the tree is re-snapshotted (`appliedSnapshotId`) and the
416	receipt written. A fault during `APPLYING` restores every renamed target
417	(`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK`, rollback `completed`); a renamed target that is neither
418	preimage nor postimage is `RECOVERY_BLOCKED` with the paths listed and no automatic
419	action. Replaying apply with the same idempotency key returns the completed receipt
420	with a new replay delivery receipt and `replayed=true`; the original is preserved.
421	
422	**Recover** (`repair-recover`) is a closed table over journal state: PREPARING/STAGED
423	→ discard temps (`FAILED_CLEAN`); APPLYING → roll back renamed (`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK`)
424	or block if a target is unrecognized; APPLIED/INDETERMINATE → verify every exact
425	postimage and the complete applied-path set before re-snapshot and commit;
426	COMMITTED/FAILED_* → none; RECOVERY_BLOCKED → refuse (`HOST.IO_FAILURE`,
427	`REPAIR.RECOVERY_BLOCKED`, exit 4). Every recovery mutation requires an authorization
428	bound to this repairPlanId and journal requestId; inspection alone is read-only.
429	Restore verifies all available retained preimage hashes before its first write.
430	Corrupt bytes yield LEDGER.CORRUPT / REPAIR.PREIMAGE_CORRUPT (4) with no target change.
431	Unavailable bytes return an exact restore intent and REPAIR.RECOVERY_REQUIRES_BROKER,
432	without claiming rollback completed. Recovery never re-applies an edit.
433	
434	**Verify** (`verify`) always admits a **fresh snapshot** after apply; it never reuses
435	the pre-apply Run. If the fresh snapshot differs from `appliedSnapshotId` the step is
436	`REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED` / `REPAIR.SOURCE_MOVED` and no Run is sealed; otherwise
437	it seals a new authoritative Run and reports `VerificationOutcome`
438	(applied/verified snapshot, targets remaining, net-new findings). A separate immutable VerificationLinkV1 binds receiptId, verificationRunId, both
439	snapshots and the verification request/step. The apply receipt is never rewritten
440	and remains retained if verification fails.

444	## 7. Explicitly authorized test execution (AR-08)
445	
446	Repository code execution is disabled by default. `opensip test run` (request class
447	`execution`) is admitted only when: the security unit admits a `RepoExecutionGrantV2`
448	with principal `P-TRUSTED-REPO`, execution class `test-runner`, bound to this
449	project, snapshot digest and the exact `argv` digest, expiry operation-end, never
450	inherited (`TEST.PRINCIPAL_NOT_ADMITTED` otherwise); CI uses a pre-existing policy
451	record (`TEST.INTERACTIVE_CONSENT_IN_CI`); `argv[0]` is a `LogicalPath` member of the
452	sealed snapshot or a member of the declared toolchain `closure2`
453	(`TEST.ARGV_NOT_IN_CLOSURE`); the working directory is the project root or a
454	`LogicalPath` inside it; the environment is constructed from an allowlist only, `PATH`
455	is never copied (`TEST.ENV_NOT_ALLOWLISTED`) and is set to the toolchain closure; and
456	the live tree still equals the `afterStep` snapshot. There is no shell string and no
457	interpolation anywhere in the schema.
458	
459	The step **discloses** and does not confine: `effects.network/subprocess/
460	filesystemWrite` are `DISCLOSURE-ONLY` unless the security unit's platform truth
461	table measures a primitive; a claimed enforcement without a measured primitive is
462	refused (`TEST.CONFINEMENT_CLAIM_REFUSED`). The mandatory sentence before spawn is
463	"Repository test command will run with your user authority. OpenSIP does not prevent
464	network access or other effects on this platform." Output is bounded and truncation
465	is recorded. The outcome is a `TestPayloadV1` wrapped as an `import2` of kind `test`
466	— evidence, never Coverage and never a verdict; a verdict may depend on it only
467	through a declared policy predicate. Imported independently prepared test results
468	are the supported alternative.

543

551	indeterminate carries `reasonCodes`; interrupted carries `signal` and a `runId` only

553	detail beside an existing code, never a termination code. Selected goldens (the complete retained set
554	is in the inventory and exercised by the model):
555	
556	| Situation | Class / exit | Code | Detail / remedy |
557	|---|---|---|---|
558	| fresh project, providers installed | success 0 | — | DEFAULTED durable retention disclosed; no policy file written |
559	| required provider closure not installed | indeterminate 3 | `COVERAGE.PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` | `COMPONENT.REQUIRED_CLOSURE_NOT_INSTALLED` → `opensip install provider-typescript` |

127	candidate report: exact host, provider/data closure, harness, matrix, corpus,

130	measurement campaign; an older report cannot satisfy a different campaign.

132	runner inventory. A report cannot supply or alter its own expected subject,

177	fixture names exact source/input bytes, selected capability/rung, expected
178	normalized observations, expected exit and independently chosen work/stress
179	bounds. Native reference scenarios supply semantic obligations; executable
180	native fixtures and their results must be admitted at implementation
181	qualification before a cell becomes QUALIFIED.

183	The gate's expectedCells is constructed from the verified matrix/corpus and
184	release selection by the first-party gate. It cannot be supplied as a CLI JSON
185	argument, copied out of report fields or recomputed from candidate answers.
186	Expected observation atoms have closed fields `kind`, `subject`, `value` (all
187	strings); `value` is the schema-defined normalized scalar or canonical JSON
188	text for structured payloads. The admitted fixture's normalizer and schema
189	are part of its pinned harness closure. Report atoms sort by canonical bytes,
190	are unique, and must equal the independent oracle exactly. Counts and
191	correctness are calculated by the gate; they are absent from the submitted
192	schema. Duplicate cells/observations, wrong cell sets, wrong exit or substituted
193	answers cannot be hidden by a reported PASS flag because no such flag is read.
194	
195	Each benchmark records 3 warmups followed by 7 measured runs in that order,
196	with positive integer elapsed nanoseconds and peak RSS bytes. The gate calculates median
197	elapsed time and maximum RSS. For an existing baseline the limits are 1.20×
198	median time and 1.25× peak RSS, using checked wide-integer cross multiplication (never wrapping), plus the
199	fixture's independently reviewed absolute bounds. A new supported cell needs
200	an explicitly reviewed initial baseline and absolute budget; absence is not a
201	zero or automatic pass. The two baseline measurements must be both present
202	or both null. A null pair admits an initial-measurement report but never qualifies
203	a release-selected cell; reviewed initial baseline promotion is a separate gate act. Baseline host/provider/harness, fixture, environment and
204	platform profile must be compatible by the release gate's signed inventory;
205	changing the measuring subject cannot silently reuse an unrelated baseline.
206	Cold-start and retained-evidence workloads are separate fixtures, so warmup
207	cannot conceal startup or storage regressions. The old reference adapter
208	retains its historical hardware/performance baseline semantics unchanged.
209	
210	A well-formed authenticated report may report a failing observation. Report
211	admission and release qualification are separate: admission verifies custody,
212	shape and joins; qualification requires every selected cell's correctness and
213	performance to pass on every required profile lane. Missing, unavailable or
214	failed lanes block promotion. The release gate also requires lifecycle,
215	security, output parity and recovery gates; G13 alone never authorizes release.

217	## 4. Reference evidence and implementation obligations
218	
219	`foundation/check-foundation.py` retains the original integer and G13
220	counterexamples, valid controls, exact canonical byte vectors and actual
221	Ed25519 signature verification with temporary test keys. The reference invokes
222	the local OpenSSL executable solely to exercise cryptography; production uses
223	the authenticated first-party implementation, never ambient tool discovery.
224	`foundation/check-identity.py` independently replays a bounded finite-relation
225	fixture and exercises identity, proof tampering, retention and crash-state
226	joins. It explicitly discloses its trusted evaluator callback and in-memory
227	carrier scope; it is not a general native interpreter or a durability proof.
228	The full-product report checks exercise a separate TS/JS/Rust-shaped cell set,
229	forged subject/corpus/answers, missing lanes and false performance claims.
230	
231	Reports record every scenario, source pins and limits. Independent review reads
232	semantics and executes adversarial controls; source hashes establish the
233	reviewed bytes, not correctness. Legacy self-reporting checker claims and their
234	observability escapes do not enter product evaluation authority. The corrected
235	product uses explicit admitted data plus trusted pure evaluation; an adversarial
236	program sharing the verifier's process is not claimed to be contained by Python
237	introspection. Native measurements, independent implementer reproduction and
238	supported-platform qualification remain the concrete pre-release gates.
239	
240	Discovery observations are folded into the trusted `defaults` layer by the host
241	before the reference Config2 resolver runs; their recognizer identity and path
242	provenance remain in the discovery record. The reference resolver does not scan
243	frameworks. A missing profile is `CONFIG_PROFILE_MISSING`; an unknown profile is
244	`CONFIG_PROFILE_UNREGISTERED`. Both pack and waiver IDs require registry admission.
245	
246	## 5. Complete product-boundary successor (DR-117)
247	
248	D-371/D-372 prospectively replace P-1/P-2/G3 only as enumerated here. These are the seven dispositions required by architecture file02, “Current V1 product boundary and required successors”; the historical enumeration and preview acceptance keep their original scope.
249	
250	1. **Marketplace/catalog and governance depth:** the selected product has one signed first-party component/recipe/schema registry. It has no public marketplace, third-party publisher admission or ecosystem governance promise. Unknown contributions refuse through the closed registry; declaring an id does not establish trust.
251	2. **External lifecycle parity and discovery:** supported first-party components receive the common installation, update, rollback, offline, doctor and removal contracts. Repository/framework discovery selects applicable admitted capabilities; it is not an external service and cannot install or execute discovered code. Third-party lifecycle parity is outside the selected scope, not a partially specified admission mode.
252	3. **Contribution roles beyond narrow/data-only:** first-party native providers may produce typed facts/Coverage and prepared input imports. Signed first-party declarative recipes/profiles may select host-owned steps. Only the host constructs findings, evaluates policy/verdict, owns persistence, finalization, rendering and termination. A component cannot acquire those powers by declaring a root command or emitting an output record.
253	4. **Untrusted native or WASM admission and enforcement:** neither is admitted in this product. No process/WASM boundary is claimed as a sandbox. Separately authorized repository-code preparation/tests are the explicit trusted-code principal of security S10, with the actual platform disclosure/enforcement matrix and revocation/cleanup rules. They do not open an untrusted plugin admission path. G09/G21/G29/G30 must exercise these refusal and authority boundaries; a synthetic fixture is not enforcement evidence.
254	5. **Imperative contributions, probes, project hooks and root commands:** arbitrary imperative contributions/project hooks/root-parser extensions are not admitted. The closed host command inventory owns every command. Named first-party repair, test, preparation and doctor operations have their exact explicit authorization and effect contracts; a recipe/profile cannot bypass them. Metadata discovery/help/recommend do not run repository hooks or probes. Consent to one executable step never becomes general command or persistence authority.
255	6. **Network-granted analysis and egress defaults:** ordinary analysis/discovery are offline; there is no implicit index refresh, download, telemetry or required egress. Explicit trust refresh/offline import and explicitly required export delivery have their named host lifecycle/output semantics. Repository-code effects are disclosed/admitted by their actual trusted-code grant; they are never silently reclassified as confined analysis. Required delivery failure can fail the invocation without changing a committed Run's assurance.
256	7. **G3 physical substrate:** the selected substrate is a signed Rust distribution core/semantic host, pure first-party evaluator, supervised native TS/JS and Rust components, and the signed offline assets and verified storage mechanics required for the selected authoritative profile. This replaces the prototype's lockstep Node/npm train and the preview's narrow command/provider set. The default product profile is authoritative-capable; an explicitly selected management-only installation is not an authoritative closure and refuses analysis until the required signed closure is separately installed through an authorized lifecycle operation. Missing assets never trigger ambient downloads or a weaker analyzer. Every physical dependency, including compiler/runtime/standard-library/LLVM/storage assets actually used, belongs to the admitted closure/TCB inventory and its packaging/offline/quality gates.
257	
258	The selected exclusions are D-371's credentials, third-party ecosystem, untrusted contributions and TUI exclusions; this section introduces no new scope cut. Product measurements remain required by the named release gates. This is a complete boundary selection now, not a promise that future implementation will choose these policies.

56	## S3. Discovery and custody (AR-03)
57	
58	Discovery is deterministic over lstat/ACL results obtained through O_NOFOLLOW
59	handles: no environment variable, no `PATH`, no `HOME` (the account home comes
60	from the account database). Output is the closed `DiscoveryProvenanceV1`.
61	
62	The disposable discovery instrument accepts only its named host-observation keys:
63	required `invokingUid`, `accountHome`, `cwd`, `fs`; optional `ci`,
64	`trustProjectOwner`, `authorizedGroupIds`, `explicitProject`, `explicitResolved`,
65	`explicitJoins`, `configWorkspaceRoots`. Unknown/missing keys or wrong outer
66	scalar/container types are `DISCOVERY_OBSERVATION_SHAPE` instrument errors,
67	not public D9 input refusals. Boolean observations are exact booleans and uid/gid
68	observations are nonnegative integers, never coerced strings or booleans. The
69	lstat/ACL map remains a synthetic trusted observation, not proof of native custody.
70	Public invocation/configuration admission still precedes this host-only seam.
71	
72	**Custody of a directory** passes only if: it is a real directory (no symlink);
73	owner is the invoking uid or root; mode has no other-write bit; mode has no
74	group-write bit unless the directory's gid is in the explicitly authorized set;
75	no ACL write grant (POSIX ACL on Linux, `acl_get_fd_np` on macOS) to any
76	principal other than the invoker, root, or an authorized group; and the ACL was
77	readable. Mode bits alone never establish exclusion. **Custody of a config
78	file** adds: regular file, link count 1, at most 4 MiB. Group authorization
79	exists only through an explicit `--trust-group <gid>` invocation argument and
80	is recorded in provenance; configuration cannot grant it. `--trust-project-owner`
81	waives only the owner check and only with an explicit `--project` path.
82	
83	**Walk rule.** With `--project`, the resolved path is examined exactly once
84	(symlink resolution recorded). Otherwise, from the launch directory upward, at
85	most 256 levels: a custody failure at the launch directory refuses
86	(`PROJECT.ROOT_CUSTODY_REFUSED`); a custody failure at an ancestor is a
87	boundary and that ancestor is never examined for a config. At each passing
88	directory the config, if present, is custody-checked (failure refuses
89	`CONFIG.CUSTODY_REFUSED`; it is never skipped) and selects that directory
90	(`mode: config`). Boundaries after a directory without config, in precedence:
91	VCS marker (`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.jj`), account home, filesystem root, mount
92	change. A VCS boundary selects **that repository root** (`mode: vcs-default`),
93	never the launch directory, so default scope does not change with launch
94	directory. Home, root, mount and custody boundaries without any candidate
95	select the launch directory (`mode: cwd-default`).
96	
97	**Nested config is a deliberate project boundary (decided; ADV-3).** A config
98	file found below a VCS root is an author-declared project root and wins for
99	launches inside it; the walk never continues above a config. The enclosing
100	VCS-root project treats that directory exactly like a nested repository: it is
101	recorded in `nestedProjects`, automatic discovery never enters it (excluded
102	unit reason `INSIDE_NESTED_PROJECT`), and an explicit join crossing into it
103	refuses `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_CROSSES_NESTED_PROJECT`). Scope
104	therefore depends only on which project a launch is inside, never on which
105	directory of one project. The alternative (VCS root always wins) was rejected
106	because it would silently ignore a config the repository author placed. Cases
107	`nested-config-inside-a-vcs-root-*` and
108	`explicit-join-crossing-into-a-nested-project-refuses`.
109	
110	**VCS data.** A `.git` indirection file (`gitdir:`) is data: its target is
111	recorded and never followed by discovery; VCS digests for the snapshot are the
112	identity unit's concern and read only inside custody.
113	
114	**Authority roots versus workspace units.** Two different things are
115	distinguished. A *project authority/custody root* is the selected root: one
116	custody domain, one ProjectId, one lease namespace. Repositories nested under
117	it are other custody roots: they are recorded as `nestedRepositories`, never
118	entered, and reachable only by their own `--project`; a join that crosses into
119	one refuses `PROJECT.EXPLICIT_PATH_INVALID` (`JOIN_CROSSES_NESTED_REPOSITORY`).
120	A *language workspace unit* is a directory inside the admitted root that
121	carries a manifest marker: `Cargo.toml`, `package.json`, `tsconfig.json` or
122	`jsconfig.json` (markers may co-locate; a unit lists all its markers). Units are
123	discovered **automatically** for the zero-config full product, with precedence:
124	
125	| Source | Provenance `unitSource` | Custody failure |
126	|---|---|---|
127	| repeatable CLI `--workspace-root PATH` overrides | `explicit-joins` | refuses (explicit intent) |
128	| admitted Config2 `discovery.workspaceRoots` (foundation product-configuration schema v2) | `config-workspace-roots` | refuses |
129	| marker scan of the admitted root | `automatic` | unit excluded, recorded in `excludedUnits` with the reason |
130	
131	An explicit source suppresses automatic discovery. Every directory from the
132	root to a unit must pass directory custody and stay inside the root (no
133	absolute, `.`, `..`, backslash or NUL segments); every marker file must pass
134	file custody. A manifest is **data**: discovery records its presence and later
135	readers parse it as data only, never running scripts, hooks, plugins or
136	workspace globs and never writing source.
137	
138	**One shared discovery rule (MUST-3).** The zero-config rule is stated once, in
139	`docs/coop/design-corrections/discovery-defaults.py`, and consumed by this
140	instrument and by the native unit instrument (native §1.4); neither restates
141	it. Before any custody walk, automatic discovery prunes, by **exact path
142	segment** (never substring): dependency trees (a segment `node_modules`), VCS
143	trees (`.git`, `.hg`, `.svn`, `.jj`) and Cargo build output (a segment
144	`target` whose parent directory holds `Cargo.toml`, an actual Cargo root; a
145	source directory merely called `target`, such as `packages/target` or
146	`src/target`, is ordinary source). A pruned tree yields no unit, no marker,
147	no custody walk and no program member; its anchor is recorded **once** in
148	`prunedTrees` with the number of markers it hid, so 4200 installed package
149	manifests are one record, never 4200 units. A `Cargo.toml` inside a pruned
150	tree does not create a Cargo root. First-party unit directories are capped at
151	4096; exceeding the cap refuses typed `PROJECT.WORKSPACE_UNIT_LIMIT` (D9
152	`REQUEST.UNSATISFIABLE`, detail `WORKSPACE_UNIT_LIMIT:<n>><cap>`) with no
153	truncation; installed dependencies never count toward it (checker sweep
154	`discovery-prunes-installed-dependencies-and-refuses-real-cap-typed`: 4200
155	installed manifests admit with one unit; 4200 first-party directories refuse;
156	exactly 4096 admit).
157	
158	**Explicit roots are exact roots.** CLI `--workspace-root` and Config2
159	`discovery.workspaceRoots` values are normalized by the shared
160	`normalize_explicit_root`: `.` alone denotes the admitted project root
161	(identity-and-evidence §3 sentinel; internal root ``, the same value the native
162	instrument uses), one trailing `/` is dropped from a CLI value (a Config2 value
163	spelled with a trailing `/` is refused earlier by the foundation
164	product-configuration resolver's logical-path grammar and never reaches either
165	instrument; case
166	`cli-workspace-root-with-trailing-slash-normalizes-like-the-native-instrument-config2-refuses-it-earlier`),
167	and any other empty, `.`, `..`,
168	absolute, backslash or NUL segment is `JOIN_PATH_GRAMMAR`. An explicit root
169	inside a pruned tree refuses `JOIN_INSIDE_PRUNED_TREE:<reason>:<anchor>`. An
170	explicit root **without a language marker** is admitted here for custody (unit
171	recorded with `markers: []`, warning
172	`EXPLICIT_ROOT_WITHOUT_LANGUAGE_MARKER:<path>`) and refused by the language-unit
173	layer as `CONFIG.INVALID` / `native.explicit-root-without-marker` (native
174	§1.4); the invocation terminates typed with this provenance retained. That is
175	the selected behaviour: custody admission and language-unit existence are two
176	different facts, and neither instrument normalizes the same value differently.
177	Custody-excluded units are explicit unknown required scope, not a successful
178	empty scope; later syntax scanners cannot read their uncustodied source. There is
179	no config "project list" and no duplicate `--project` implicit multi-project
180	mode: `discovery.workspaceRoots` is the only configuration carrier. Cases

183	
184	**Pruned trees and the read set (A-5).** "No custody walk" for a pruned tree

193	**Admitted boundary inventory for the language-unit instrument (decided; post-reset

765	into `AuthorizedExecutionV2.effects` and its `owners[]` are this grant's

773	proc-macro owners, workflow `native prepare`) or a workflow test-execution step

791	The Plan-time join is separate and later. `semantic_projection_for_grants`
792	lists the `trusted-repository-code` principals (`{kind, closureId,

795	evidence enters a Plan only as an `import2` payload whose wrapper and
796	test-execution step receipt retain the operational `securityGrantRef`. When the
797	analysis is admitted, `admit_plan_execution_projection(planPrincipals,
798	consumedGrants, preparedResolution)` requires, under `host-prepared`, that the
799	plan2 semantic-grant projects exactly those principals
800	(`PLAN.EXECUTION_PRINCIPAL_NOT_PROJECTED:<digest>` /
801	`PLAN.PROJECTED_PRINCIPAL_WITHOUT_GRANT:<digest>`), refuses any
802	`trusted-repository-code` principal under `imported-inert` or `none` (prepared
803	availability never implies this host held a grant), and refuses a test-runner
804	grant offered as a consumed grant (`PLAN.TEST_RUNNER_HAS_NO_PLAN`). The
805	projection comes from the Plan and the grants from the step receipts; they must
806	agree, and neither is derived from the other. D9: `REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED`

810	`integration-host-model.py` derives the Plan requirement through

812	`ctx.semanticGrantPrincipals` before operational admission and then checks the Plan-time join
813	(`consuming-plan-preparation-principal-join`, `consuming-plan-missing-principal-refused`,
814	`imported-inert-does-not-infer-local-grant`, `test-runner-is-operational-not-a-plan-principal`,
815	`test-runner-cannot-be-consumed-as-preparation`).
816	
817	### S10.1 Repair apply authorization (not a repository-execution grant)
818	
819	Repair apply is host-brokered **first-party** source mutation: the host writes
820	postimages it computed from a signed recipe closure under the EXCLUSIVE lease.
821	No repository code runs. Its authorization is therefore a separate record,
822	`RepairApplyAuthorizationV1` (product data; identity
823	`H("security.repair-apply-authorization.v1", record)` is the workflow
824	`RepairApplyParams.authorizationRef`), admitted only when: projectId,
825	`repairPlanId` (`repairplan2:`) and `baseSnapshotId` (`snapshot2:`) equal the
826	invocation's; the live tree still equals the base snapshot
827	(`AUTHZ.SOURCE_MOVED`); `recipeClosureId` (`closure2:`) equals the recipe in
828	the rehashed repair plan (`AUTHZ.RECIPE_CLOSURE_MISMATCH`) and is positively
829	admitted under current signed-closure trust (`AUTHZ.RECIPE_CLOSURE_NOT_ADMITTED`).
830	Absence from the revocation set is insufficient. Revocation refuses first
831	(`AUTHZ.RECIPE_CLOSURE_REVOKED`, D9
832	`EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED`); consent is `interactive-explicit` (never in
833	CI) or `policy-record`, with a real boolean `ci` equal to the invocation's;
834	expiry operation-end; `leaseMode` `EXCLUSIVE`; `repositoryExecution` is the
835	constant `false` and cannot be set. Live revocation: every brokered write
836	passes the S6 authority checkpoint; a revoked recipe closure at any checkpoint
837	is `REV(trust-revoked)` with postimage-checked rollback and the workflow's
838	`FAILED_ROLLED_BACK` / `RECOVERY_BLOCKED` states. Reference
839	`admit_repair_authorization`; fixture `repair-authorization-cases.v1.json`.
840	
841	### S10.2 Repair recovery authorization (decided; post-reset v2 N-4/P9)
842	
843	Recovery inspection (`repair recover` without `--apply-recovery`, workflows §6
844	`repair_inspect`) is read-only and needs no authorization. Every recovery
845	**mutation** (`discard-temps`, `roll-back-renamed`,
846	`verify-postimages-and-commit`) is a separately authorized host-brokered
847	write within the **original** plan's authority, under the EXCLUSIVE lease, and
848	its authorization is the closed security record `RepairRecoveryAuthorizationV1`
849	(product data; identity `H("security.repair-recovery-authorization.v1", record)`
850	is the workflow `RepairApplyJournalV1.recoveryAuthorizationRef`, always the full
851	reference, never a truncated prefix). It is admitted by
852	`admit_recovery_authorization(authz, ctx)` only when every binding holds:
853	
854	- **Project, plan, snapshot, recipe.** `projectId`, `repairPlanId`,
855	  `baseSnapshotId` and `recipeClosureId` equal the admitted project and the
856	  rehashed original plan (`AUTHZ.*_MISMATCH`).
857	- **Exact journal identity (noncircular).** `journalRef` =
858	  `security.repair-apply-journal-identity.v1:` + `H` over the closed identity
859	  preimage `{schemaFamily, schemaMajor, requestId, stepId, executionId,
860	  repairPlanId, baseSnapshotId, authorizationRef}`: only fields fixed when the
861	  apply journal was created, never `state`, paths, blobs, blocked/restore lists
862	  or any `recoveryAuthorizationRef` the journal later carries, so one journal
863	  has one identity in every state and the reference written into the journal
864	  never enters its own preimage (`journal-identity-mismatch-*`,
865	  `journal-of-a-different-plan-*`).
866	- **Observed journal state and replay/crash semantics.** `journalState` and
867	  `observedJournalStateDigest` (raw SHA-256 of canonical `{state, stagedPaths,
868	  appliedPaths, preimageBlobs}`) equal the journal **as read under the EXCLUSIVE
869	  lease before any recovery write**. Every successful recovery mutation changes
870	  `state`, so a retained authorization cannot be replayed after one
871	  (`AUTHZ.JOURNAL_STATE_MOVED`; `replay-after-a-successful-rollback-*`); a crash
872	  or a `requires-broker` return before the first write leaves the digest
873	  unchanged. The same authorization may continue only within the same still-admitted
874	  recovery execution and lifetime. A process crash ends that execution; a fresh
875	  attempt requires a newly admitted authorization bound to its new execution id (`crash-before-the-first-recovery-write-*`).
876	- **Finite action.** `recoveryAction` equals the one the journal state admits
877	  (`PREPARING`/`STAGED` → `discard-temps`; `APPLYING` → `roll-back-renamed`;
878	  `APPLIED`/`INDETERMINATE` → `verify-postimages-and-commit`;
879	  `AUTHZ.RECOVERY_ACTION_MISMATCH` otherwise). Terminal states (`COMMITTED`,
880	  `FAILED_*`, `RECOVERY_BLOCKED`) admit no mutation
881	  (`AUTHZ.RECOVERY_NOT_MUTATING:<state>`); the table mirrors the workflow
882	  recovery table's mutating rows, and the integration checker asserts that equality today
883	  (`security-workflow-recovery-action-table-identical`, comparing the mutating rows of
884	  `W.RECOVERY_TABLE` with `S.RECOVERY_ACTION_FOR_STATE`).
885	- **Fresh attempt.** `originalRequestId` equals the journal's `requestId`;
886	  `recoveryRequestId`/`recoveryExecutionId` equal the recovery invocation's own
887	  ids and differ from the original (`AUTHZ.RECOVERY_REQUEST_NOT_FRESH`).
888	- **Consent and policy.** Consent is `interactive-explicit` (never in CI) or
889	  `policy-record`, with a real boolean `ci` equal to the invocation's; the project
890	  policy admits repair.
891	- **Time.** `issuedAt` ≤ S4 admitted evaluation time ≤ `expiresAt`, lifetime at
892	  most 24 h; no admitted time context refuses (`AUTHZ.NO_ADMITTED_TIME_CONTEXT`).
893	- **Boundary.** `leaseMode` `EXCLUSIVE`, `mutationBoundary` `host-broker`,
894	  `repositoryExecution` and `newEdits` are the constant `false`: recovery can
895	  never grant repository code execution, write a byte the original plan did not
896	  name, or broaden the plan (`planScope: original-plan-only`).
897	- **Current host custody.** The S3 custody rule is re-run on the recovery
898	  invocation (`AUTHZ.CUSTODY_NOT_ADMITTED`); an old admission does not carry over.
899	
900	**Safe rollback versus re-executing a revoked recipe.** `discard-temps` and
901	`roll-back-renamed` restore retained preimages or discard temps and **never
902	consult recipe trust**: rolling back after the recipe was revoked is exactly what
903	revocation rollback is (`rollback-recovery-admits-although-the-recipe-closure-is-revoked-*`).
904	`verify-postimages-and-commit` would commit the recipe's postimages, so it
905	re-consults current signed-closure trust: a revoked recipe refuses first
906	(`AUTHZ.RECIPE_CLOSURE_REVOKED`, D9 `EXTENSION.ADMISSION_REJECTED`) and a recipe
907	not positively admitted refuses (`AUTHZ.RECIPE_CLOSURE_NOT_ADMITTED`). The
908	workflow recovery table's guarded preimage/postimage law (every target at its
909	plan preimage or postimage before any restore or commit; otherwise
910	`RECOVERY_BLOCKED`) is mandatory and never waived by this record.
911	
912	**Trusted context inputs**, each a host observation and none supplied by the
913	caller of `repair recover`: `projectId`, `repairPlanId`, `baseSnapshotId`,
914	`journal` (as read under the lease), `recoveryRequestId`, `recoveryExecutionId`,
915	`ci`, `admittedTime`, `custodyAdmitted`, `policyAdmitsRepair`, `recipeClosureId`,
916	`revokedClosures`, `admittedClosures`. Output `RecoveryAuthorizationAdmissionV1`;
917	fixture `repair-recovery-authorization-cases.v1.json`. **Implemented, not owed:** the workflow
918	journal's `recoveryAuthorizationRef` takes the closed grammar above,
919	`integration-host-model.py` `recovery_authorization_projection` composes
920	`admit_recovery_authorization` exactly as it composes `admit_repair_authorization`, and
921	`repair_recover` consumes that host-created projection rather than a caller dictionary — the
922	caller-dictionary path is a checked refusal
923	(`recovery-caller-projection-refused`), beside
924	`security-workflow-journal-preimages-identical`, `security-to-recovery-full-reference-commits`,
925	`recovery-moved-journal-refused`, `recovery-revoked-commit-refused`,
926	`recovery-original-execution-not-fresh` and `recovery-revoked-recipe-still-rolls-back`.

928	## S11. Offline windows and doctor (AR-16)

931	issue; root expires 365 d after issue; warning from 14 d before the earliest
932	cliff. Continuation (already-verified components run) stops when the revocation

958	### S12.1 Projecting a refusal onto the one closed public detail vocabulary
959	
960	A public termination carries exactly one `domainDetail` = `{code, remedy, subject?}`, and `code` is a
961	member of the single closed registry (`design-corrections/public-detail-registry.v1.json`, mirrored by
962	`workflows/schemas/common.schema.json#/$defs/DomainDetailCode`). This section states the projection
963	this unit's refusals take, so that "detail" in the prose above is never ambiguous between a registry
964	member and free subject text. Reference `public_detail` / `public_details`, record
965	`PublicDetailProjectionV1`, fixture `public-detail-cases.v1.json`, sweep
966	`public-domain-details-are-a-closed-set-with-a-bounded-pending-registration-gap`.
967	
968	1. **Base code, then subject.** The base code is everything before the **first** colon; everything
969	   after it is subject data. `ROOT.ROLE_SET:1` is code `ROOT.ROLE_SET`, subject `1`.

## ladderAuthority -> "This registry is the SINGLE authority for every relation's resolution ladder, as identity-and-evidence section 3 states. `ladder` is that relation's total order over its OWN resolution methods, listed weakest-first, inherited verbatim from fact-plane.v1 relationRegistry.relations[].ladder (plus [observed] for unresolved-edge). Every other copy in the kit - native_evidence_model.v2.py LADDERS and capability-manifest-domains.v2.json RELATION-LADDER-DOMAIN-V2.ladders - is a declared MIRROR of this array and is drift-checked against it exactly and IN ORDER. A one-rung ladder is not a deficiency; it means the relation is fully determined at that rung."
## rungsAreFieldRulesNotTheLadder -> "`rungs` is a different table: the per-rung required/forbidden PAYLOAD FIELD rules. It is legitimately the empty object for a relation with no per-rung field variance, which is every single-rung relation. Reading `rungs` as the ladder is the defect this key exists to prevent: an empty field-rule table must never be read as an absent ladder, and never as a licence to skip ladder membership. Membership is checked against `ladder`, always, with no fallback."
## membershipRule -> "A resolution is admissible for a relation only if it is a member of THAT relation's `ladder`. A rung that is a member of another relation's ladder is refused, not accepted as a live vocabulary token; the flat rung vocabulary published elsewhere is necessary but never sufficient. Order comparison is the index within one relation's ladder; nothing orders a rung of one relation against a rung of another, and there is no global rank."
## subjectKindLaw -> "What a subject-scope's `subjects` entries IDENTIFY, per relation. `source-path`: each subject is a path in the snapshot this scope names, so the scope's own extent is exactly those paths - `file` and `vcs-change` bind it through their registry snapshotJoins pathField, and `clones` binds it through bodyIdentityJoin, whose single anchor IS the body span the identity is over. `package-name`: a package identifier, not a path. `symbol`: an opaque SubjectIdV1 that the record associates with no path; the enumerator's attribution of symbols to files is trusted and is NOT re-derivable from the retained Run, so no per-subject path law is possible for these relations and any capability question about them can only be answered at the coarser retained extent. That limit is stated rather than worked around: inventing symbol-to-path parsing would be fabricated evidence."
## snapshotJoinLaw -> "Normative. Each row states what the enclosing fact snapshot must contain for this relation payload to be admissible. Rows are applied by identity-model close_run on every owning fact; a relation absent from this table declares that it names no snapshot path and no retained artifact, which is itself the record that nothing constrains it."
## codec -> "C (identity-and-evidence section 3 canonical JSON)"

# --------------------------------------------------------------------------

def make_plan(store, snapshot, cap, semantic_closures, analysis_spec, native_contexts,

    kit.validate("identity", "#/$defs/analysis-spec", analysis_spec)

    kit.validate("identity", "#/$defs/semantic-grant", semantic_grant)
    grant_digest = store.put_record(semantic_grant)

    if budget != snapshot["config"]["analysis"]["budget"]:

                      "%r vs %r" % (budget, snapshot["config"]["analysis"]["budget"]))
    desc = {"schemaVersion": 2, "snapshotId": snapshot["id"],
            "capabilityManifestId": cap["capabilityManifestId"],
            "semanticClosures": sorted(set(semantic_closures)),
            "analysisSpecDigest": spec_digest,
            "resolvedConfigDigest": snapshot["configDigest"],
            "nativeContextDigests": sorted({c["hex"] for c in native_contexts}),
            "importIds": sorted(set(import_ids)),

            "scopeDigest": scope_digest, "budget": budget,
            "semanticGrantDigest": grant_digest,
            "capabilityManifestBytesDigest": cap["capabilityManifestBytesDigest"]}
    kit.validate("identity", "#/$defs/plan", desc)
    d = store.put_frame("plan", desc)
    return {"id": "plan2:" + d, "hex": d, "descriptor": desc,
            "policy": policy_doc, "waivers": waiver_set, "analysisSpec": analysis_spec,
            "semanticGrant": semantic_grant, "scope": scope}

def make_execution_plan(store, plan, stages):
    """stages: [{producerClosure, operation, parameters, outputDomains,
                 outputSchemaDigest, requires}]"""
    rows = []
    for i, s in enumerate(stages):
        spec = {"schemaVersion": 2, "planId": plan["id"],
                "producerClosure": s["producerClosure"], "operation": s["operation"],
                "parameters": s["parameters"], "outputDomains": sorted(s["outputDomains"]),
                "outputSchemaDigest": s["outputSchemaDigest"]}
        kit.validate("identity", "#/$defs/stage-spec", spec)
        for p in spec["parameters"]:
            if p not in plan["analysisSpec"]["parameters"]:
                raise Refusal("stage-takes-a-hidden-input", str(p))
        if spec["producerClosure"] not in plan["descriptor"]["semanticClosures"]:
            raise Refusal("stage-producer-not-plan-selected", spec["producerClosure"])
        rows.append({"ordinal": i, "stageSpecDigest": store.put_record(spec),
                     "requires": sorted(s.get("requires", [])),
                     "outputDomains": sorted(s["outputDomains"])})
        for r in rows[-1]["requires"]:

                raise Refusal("derivation-dag-not-acyclic", "%d requires %d" % (i, r))
    desc = {"schemaVersion": 2, "planId": plan["id"], "stages": rows}
    kit.validate("identity", "#/$defs/execution-plan", desc)

def node_addresses(pred, addr="p"):
    """Total, deterministic node addressing (identity section 3)."""
    out = {addr: pred}

    if op in ("and", "or"):

    elif op == "not":

    rec = {"schemaVersion": 2, "programPredicateDigest": program_predicate_digest,
           "matchingFactIds": sorted(set(fact_ids)),
           "coverageIds": sorted(set(coverage_ids)),
           "countLimit": count_limit, "childPredicateIds": sorted(set(child_ids))}
    kit.validate("identity", "#/$defs/predicate-witness", rec)
    return store.put_record(rec), rec


def make_finding(store, rule_stable_id, detector_major, subject_key, related,
                 rule_closure, message_code, parameters, severity, evidence_refs):
    fp_desc = {"schemaVersion": 2, "ruleStableId": rule_stable_id,
               "detectorSemanticsMajor": detector_major, "subjectKey": subject_key,
               "relatedSubjectKeys": sorted(set(related))}
    kit.validate("identity", "#/$defs/finding-fingerprint", fp_desc)
    fp = "finding-key2:" + store.put_frame("finding-fingerprint", fp_desc)
    params = {"schemaVersion": 2, "messageCode": message_code, "parameters": parameters}
    kit.validate("identity", "#/$defs/finding-parameters", params)
    desc = {"schemaVersion": 2, "fingerprint": fp, "ruleClosure": rule_closure,
            "subjectId": subject_key["qualifiedName"], "messageCode": message_code,
            "parameterDigest": store.put_record(params), "severity": severity,
            "evidenceRefs": sorted(evidence_refs,
                                   key=lambda r: osip.c_encode(r))}
    kit.validate("identity", "#/$defs/finding", desc)
    d = store.put_frame("finding", desc)

def make_proof(store, plan, exec_plan, evaluator_closure, rule_program_digest,
               input_refs, predicate_proofs, finding_ids, verdict):
    refs = sorted(input_refs, key=lambda r: osip.c_encode(r))
    osip.check_order(refs, "canonical-set")
    pp = sorted(predicate_proofs,
                key=lambda p: (p["ruleId"], p["subjectId"], p["predicateId"]))
    osip.check_order(pp, "predicate")
    desc = {"schemaVersion": 2, "planId": plan["id"], "executionPlanId": exec_plan["id"],
